Abstract: Efficient management of soil–water resources is critical for global food security under intensifying climatic and demographic pressures. This review provides a comprehensive synthesis of artificial intelligence (AI) and distributed deep learning methodologies applied to soil–water interactions in precision agriculture. The physical and hydraulic foundations of soil–water systems—including water retention, unsaturated flow governed by the Richards equation, and soil degradation processes—are examined and situated within a unified framework of AI-based modeling and decision support. Classical machine learning (ML) algorithms (Random Forests, Support Vector Machines, gradient boosting) and deep learning architectures (convolutional neural networks, long short-term memory networks, transformers) are evaluated with respect to their capacity to predict soil moisture dynamics, estimate hydraulic properties, support smart irrigation scheduling, and generate digital soil maps at field-to-regional scales. Distributed training paradigms, federated learning for privacy-preserving multi-farm analytics, and edge AI deployment on low-power IoT hardware are assessed as enabling infrastructures for scalable agricultural intelligence. This review further addresses explainability, uncertainty quantification, and ethical dimensions inherent to AI-driven agricultural systems. Key challenges—including training data scarcity in data-poor regions, model interpretability, integration with physics-based hydrological models, and real-time deployment constraints—are critically discussed. Prospective research directions encompass physics-informed neural networks, foundation models for earth observation, autonomous digital twins of soil–water systems, and federated learning architectures aligned with data sovereignty frameworks. The synthesis underscores AI’s transformative potential for sustainable agricultural water management while delineating the technical and sociotechnical barriers that must be resolved to realize this potential at a global scale. © 2026 by the author.

Title: Physics-informed modular modeling of a gas turbine with component-level thermodynamic constraints and system-level consistency
Affiliations: Department of Mechanical Engineering, University of Manitoba, Winnipeg, R3T 2N2, MB, Canada; Department of Mechanical Engineering, Universiti Teknologi PETRONAS, Seri Iskandar, 32610, Malaysia; School of Mechatronic Engineering, Southwest Petroleum University, Chengdu, China

Abstract: Accurate and physically consistent modeling of gas turbine systems is essential for improving performance prediction, reliability, and energy efficiency. Conventional data-driven approaches often lack physical interpretability, while purely physics-based models struggle to capture complex nonlinear system behavior. This study presents a modular physics-informed modeling framework for gas turbine performance and emission prediction, in which thermodynamic constraints are embedded at the component level and preserved during system-level integration. The proposed approach incorporates differential thermodynamic relations for compressor and turbine components, along with an energy balance formulation for the combustor, directly into the learning process. A coordinated system-level fine-tuning strategy is introduced to enforce consistency across interconnected components and mitigate the accumulation of integration errors. The framework is evaluated using three datasets with varying levels of complexity, including a high-fidelity simulated turbofan engine dataset based on Pratt & Whitney PW-4056, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Commercial Modular Aero-Propulsion System Simulation (C-MAPSS) benchmark dataset, and a real industrial gas turbine Predictive Emission Monitoring System (PEMS) dataset for emission prediction. At the component level, the physics-informed formulation achieves mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) below 0.28% for key variables, outperforming conventional neural network models. At the system level, the proposed integration strategy reduces prediction errors by up to 86.39% for thrust, 81.85% for thrust-specific fuel consumption, and 75.70% for overall pressure ratio relative to baseline data-driven models. On the C-MAPSS dataset, the approach maintains MAPE values below 0.33% under limited sensor conditions. For the industrial PEMS dataset, the model achieves mean absolute errors of 0.8536 mg/m3 for Carbon monoxide (CO) and 4.8419 mg/m3 for Nitrogen oxides (NOx) under real operating conditions. These results demonstrate that integrating thermodynamic constraints with data-driven learning improves prediction accuracy, robustness, and physical consistency, particularly under varying operating conditions across gas turbine systems. The proposed framework provides a foundation for developing physics-consistent digital twins for condition monitoring and predictive maintenance applications. © 2026 The Author(s).

Abstract: Urban multi-energy systems require coordinated operation across electricity, gas, heating, carbon markets, and mobility-driven demand, yet existing scheduling models often treat these layers separately or rely on deterministic assumptions under renewable, price, and mobility uncertainty. This paper develops an integrated optimization framework for green energy communities in which traffic-dependent mobility electric bicycle demand is coupled with energy exchange, carbon allowance trading, Digital Twin correction, and hierarchical operator-community coordination. The framework combines a Traffic-aware Spatiotemporal Transportation Network, a two-stage stochastic–robust formulation, and a Lyapunov-integrated Stackelberg structure to support cost-effective and uncertainty-aware scheduling. Numerical results show that enforcing network constraints and demand response reduces community-level operating costs by up to 31.4% compared with the unconstrained baseline. Joint energy and carbon trading lowers the total system cost by 8.5%, even after mobility-related demand is included. Under renewable generation, price, and mobility uncertainty, the stochastic–robust formulation increases total cost by about 4.4%, representing the robustness premium needed to preserve feasibility. Additional benchmarking confirms that the proposed framework reduces ex-post operating cost by 8.50% relative to deterministic scheduling while eliminating infeasibility exposure. These findings show that coordinated energy, carbon, and mobility scheduling can improve economic performance while maintaining robust operation in interconnected green energy communities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Abstract: Reliable Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) is essential for assessing the condition of bridges, civil infrastructure, and industrial assets. However, sensor degradation, environmental variability, communication disturbances, and incomplete observations can reduce monitoring reliability and lead to inappropriate maintenance decisions. This study proposes an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled Digital Twin (DT)-based SHM framework, termed AI-DT-SHM, that integrates Internet of Things (IoT) sensing, adaptive sensor fusion, DT synchronization, and a Weighted Bayesian Belief Network (W-BBN) for uncertainty-aware structural-condition assessment. The principal contribution lies not in introducing a new standalone AI algorithm, but in establishing an end-to-end workflow that connects reliability-aware Bayesian inference, recursive DT updating, Structural Health Index (SHI) estimation, and Value of Structural Health (VoSH)-based maintenance decision support. Sensor observations are weighted according to their estimated reliability, thereby limiting the influence of noisy, missing, or low-confidence measurements on structural-state inference. The resulting probabilistic estimates are converted into an interpretable SHI, while the VoSH model supports risk-informed and cost-sensitive maintenance planning. The framework is validated using the Z24 Bridge benchmark dataset together with real-world IoT environmental observations. Repeated stratified cross-validation, statistical significance testing, uncertainty analysis, and comparisons with Decision Tree, k-nearest neighbor, and Random Forest classifiers are employed. It also reduced normalized posterior uncertainty from 0.148 to 0.072 compared with the conventional Bayesian configuration. These findings demonstrate that the proposed AI-DT-SHM framework provides an interpretable, computationally efficient, scalable, and reproducible approach for near-real-time structural assessment and lifecycle-oriented predictive maintenance. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Abstract: Edible coatings are widely studied as food-compatible formulations for reducing moisture loss, oxidation, microbial spoilage, oil uptake, and quality deterioration. Their translation from laboratory formulation to industrial use, however, depends not only on film-forming composition but also on controlled deposition, retained dose, surface coverage, drying history, defect formation, hygienic operation, and reproducible performance on heterogeneous food surfaces. An OpenAlex-supported evidence-map audit (2014–2026) was used to separate direct food-coating validation from adjacent engineering models. This review reframes edible coatings as engineered deposited interfaces and proposes a claim-controlled, evidence-tiered framework linking food-grade biopolymer fluids, processability, atomization, droplet impact, wet-film evolution, dry-film structure, image-based metrology, multiphase modeling, and food-performance endpoints. This review outlines the prerequisites for future digital-twin-ready edible coating workflows by linking functional biopolymer fluids, deposition technologies, droplet physics, intelligent image metrology, Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), Volume of Fluid (VOF), uncertainty reporting, food-performance endpoints, safety, Life-Cycle Assessment (LCA), Techno-Economic Analysis (TEA) and patent-aware innovation. Digital twins are treated as a future integration target that depends on validated inputs, standardized reporting, deposition metrology and food-specific model validation. The central argument is that progress in edible coatings requires fewer isolated formulation claims and stronger validated links between deposited-interface properties and food-relevant function. A minimum reporting checklist is proposed to support reproducible comparison of deposition routes, coating structures, and translation potential. © 2026 by the authors.

Abstract: This chapter discusses the application of artificial intelligence (AI) in aerospace engineering, focusing on aerodynamic analysis, structural design, aerospace materials, and autonomous systems. Machine learning, deep learning and physics-informed models help to rapidly generate an approximation (surrogate model) and minimize reliance on computational expensive simulations like the computational fluid dynamics (CFD). These methods include increasing the prediction accuracy, aiding in real-time optimization, and uncertainty analysis. The chapter also discusses generative design and topology optimization of lightweight aircraft structures. The use of AI in Aerospace Materials facilitates faster property prediction and material discovery, digital twins enable predictive maintenance and intelligent monitoring. Data quality, model validation, interpretability and certification requirements are key challenges. Copyright © 2027, IGI Global Scientific Publishing. Abstract: Transitions of control between automated driving systems and human drivers remain safety-relevant and cognitively demanding moments in human–automation interaction. Recent studies show that transition performance depends not only on takeover timing or response speed but also on traffic complexity, driver readiness, automation limitations, trust calibration, and situational-awareness recovery. As in-vehicle interaction evolves toward conversational and agentic AI assistance, takeover support also becomes a problem of governing how natural-language AI systems communicate with the driver under uncertainty. This paper proposes a digital-twin-mediated framework for human-aware takeover support in automated driving. In this framework, the companion AI is treated as an assumed LLM-based in-vehicle conversational or agentic assistant used as an advisory interaction component. The contribution is defined at the architectural level: human, vehicle, and context/road digital twins provide structured semantic state abstractions through a semantic state interface exposing confidence, freshness, provenance, and consistency metadata, while a trustworthy companion AI (TCAI) layer grounds, constrains, validates, and governs companion AI output proposals before HMI delivery. Building on the research on driver-state monitoring, adaptive HMI, trust calibration, explainability, conversational assistance, and human assistance systems (HASs), the framework coordinates advisory interaction across vigilance support, contextual explanation, trust-calibrating communication, and directive handover guidance. The TCAI layer combines bounded reasoning, human-factor-derived guardrails, state-consistency management, dynamic explanation-depth control, trust-dynamics modeling, graded watchdog veto handling, mandatory access-control assumptions, and deterministic fallback. Safety-critical vehicle-control and minimum risk condition (MRC) functions remain assigned to the deterministic vehicle-control stack, while the authorized output path of the TCAI layer is validated HMI delivery. The paper concludes with a validation agenda and technical roadmap covering planned transitions, urgent handovers, degraded or adversarial conditions, temporal fusion of driver-state evidence, phase-sensitive HMI policies, trust-calibration trajectories, driver veto and partial-disabling mechanisms, and staged simulator-to-vehicle evaluation. Although motivated by SAE Level 3 automation, the framework may also inform fallback-related Level 4 scenarios in which human and automated agency must be managed under uncertainty. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Toward Digital Twin-Enabled Smart Buildings: An Evolutionary Neural Network Approach for Energy Prediction

Abstract: The increasing pace of urbanization and climate change necessitate a holistic assessment of building energy performance during the early design phase. This study proposes an Evolutionary Field Optimization (EFO)-based multi-input multi-output artificial neural network (MIMO-ANN) model to simultaneously predict the heating load, cooling load, CO2 emissions, and lighting energy consumption of smart buildings. The model’s dataset consists of 7963 observations generated via EnergyPlus building energy simulations of standardized TOKİ residential units constructed post-earthquake in Türkiye. No operational or physically measured building energy consumption data were used in the model development process. For the validation setting, the simulation-generated dataset was split into training (60%), validation (10%), and test (30%) subsets. The EFO algorithm was employed to automatically optimize the ANN architecture by dynamically determining the optimal number of hidden layers and neurons. The optimization process demonstrated strong global search capability and fast convergence, reducing the objective function by approximately 86% within 10 iterations. Experimental results on the test subset showed exceptional predictive accuracy for simulation data, with test R2 values ranging from 0.9996 to 0.9998 across all four outputs, indicating that the optimized network topology effectively avoided overfitting. While the model’s performance under real-world operational uncertainties and varying occupant behaviors remains to be fully investigated, the proposed EFO-ANN framework provides a computationally efficient and highly accurate analytical core for early-stage design. It serves as a strategic decision-support tool intended for architects and engineers designing post-disaster housing, public authorities forming national energy efficiency policies, and developers building predictive engines for digital twin-enabled smart building systems. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Generative prediction of laser-induced rocket ignition with dynamic latent space representations

Authors with affiliations: Zahtila T., Center for Turbulence Research, Stanford University, United States; Saetta E., University of Naples Federico II, Italy; Cutforth M., Center for Turbulence Research, Stanford University, United States; Brouzet D., Center for Turbulence Research, Stanford University, United States; Rossinelli D., Center for Turbulence Research, Stanford University, United States; Iaccarino G., Department of Mechanical Engineering, Stanford University, United States
Abstract: Accurate and predictive scale-resolving simulations of laser-ignited rocket engines are highly time-consuming because the problem includes turbulent fuel–oxidizer mixing dynamics, laser-induced energy deposition, and high-speed flame growth. This is conflated with the large design space primarily corresponding to the laser operating conditions and target location. To enable rapid exploration and uncertainty quantification, we propose a data-driven surrogate modeling approach that combines convolutional autoencoders (cAEs) with neural ordinary differential equations (neural ODEs). The present target application of an machine learning-based surrogate model to leading-edge multiphysics turbulence simulation is part of a paradigm shift in the deployment of surrogate models toward increasing real-world complexity. Sequentially, the cAE spatially compresses high-dimensional flow fields into a low-dimensional latent space, wherein the system’s temporal dynamics are learned via neural ODEs. Once trained, the model generates fast spatiotemporal predictions from initial conditions and specified operating inputs. By learning a surrogate to replace the entirety of the time-evolving simulation, the cost of predicting an ignition trial is reduced by several orders of magnitude, allowing efficient exploration of the input parameter space. Further, as the current framework yields a spatiotemporal field prediction, appraisal of the model output’s physical grounding is more tractable. This approach marks a significant step toward real-time digital twins for laser-ignited rocket combustors and represents surrogate modeling in a complex system context. © The Author(s), 2026. Title: A Time-Aware Machine Learning Framework for Behavioral Anomaly Monitoring and Short-Horizon Forecasting in Goats Using RFID-Derived Activity Data

Abstract: Precision livestock farming requires monitoring approaches that extend beyond static activity thresholds to enable dynamic, animal-level decision support. A time-aware machine learning framework was developed to transform RFID-derived goat activity records into an interpretable behavioral monitoring system. Time-stamped activity data were processed into temporal features such as lagged activity, rolling mean, activity change, and elapsed-time variables to capture short-term behavioral history. The framework integrated latent-state discovery, fuzzy-uncertainty analysis, transition modeling, supervised classification, short-horizon forecasting, and dashboard-based alert visualization within a predictive dashboard-based monitoring framework. Four latent behavioral clusters were identified, with the dominant cluster representing a stable low-activity baseline and accounting for 77.88% of observations. Boundary-zone analysis indicated that 7.30% of observations were in transitional regions, while fuzzy clustering classified 21.42% as uncertain or mixed-state points, suggesting gradual shifts in activity. Transition analysis revealed greater persistence in baseline states and lower persistence in high-activity/non-baseline states, which exhibited the highest volatility and entropy. Using nested time-blocked validation, Random Forest predicted future high-activity/non-baseline onset with AUC values of 0.869 and 0.841 for 5 and 10 min horizons, respectively. These results demonstrate that activity instability can be detected and forecasted over short horizons, supporting behavior-based monitoring. However, external biological validation is still required before implementation as a health- or disease-detection system. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Towards Practical Digital Twin Construction Systems
Source title: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Automation and Robotics in Construction
Affiliations: Seskin Virtual Construction Laboratory, Technion - Israel Institute of Technology, Israel
Authors with affiliations: Yeung T., Seskin Virtual Construction Laboratory, Technion - Israel Institute of Technology, Israel; Sacks R., Seskin Virtual Construction Laboratory, Technion - Israel Institute of Technology, Israel
Abstract: Building construction projects are socio-technical production systems in which variance, uncertainty and unpredictable events are the norm. Such systems need short-cycle Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) loops to detect anomalies in production flow as early as possible so that remedial actions can be evaluated and well-informed decisions made. This is the goal of Digital Twin Construction (DTC). We define practical DTC as a minimal coherent system that captures a project’s current status, compares the status to design and planning intent, analyses variance, predicts the outcomes of possible interventions, and thus informs specific managerial decisions at the required cadence. We introduce a ‘thinking backward’ decision-centric design approach for DTC systems that traces requirements from a target decision and its PDCA cycle through knowledge and information needs to data acquisition and enabling technologies. The approach characterizes managerial decisions by autonomy, fidelity, and scope, and proposes five degrees of implementation as system capability configurations for incremental development. This contributes an actionable basis for specifying and incrementally implementing DTC systems that deliver decision value early while maintaining a clear pathway toward more advanced implementations. © 2026 International Association on Automation and Robotics in Construction. Title: From Sensing to Scheduling: Deviation-Based Framework for Sensor-Aware Progress Monitoring and Schedule Control
Source title: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Automation and Robotics in Construction
Affiliations: Department of Structural Engineering, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beersheba, Israel; Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Catholic University of America, Washington, DC, United States
Authors with affiliations: Isaac S., Department of Structural Engineering, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beersheba, Israel; Lucko G., Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Catholic University of America, Washington, DC, United States
Abstract: Automated progress monitoring has advanced through reality capture (images, laser scanning, SLAM/mobile mapping) and data-driven interpretation aligned to BIM/4D models. Yet many workflows still stop at percent-complete estimates and leave the schedule-update step under-specified, especially when completion depends on inspections, tests, and formal acceptance. This paper proposes a management-oriented sensing-to-scheduling method that makes that step explicit and computable. First, it separates production-facing progress monitoring from schedule control, highlighting their different units (work vs. time) and decision contexts. Second, it introduces sensor-aware activity scheduling based on evidence: Existence evidence from geometry/vision and performance/acceptance evidence from QA tests, inspections, and approvals. Third, it defines a translation layer that converts measured work quantities into work backlog/forelog, time delay, forecasted finishes, and recovery targets (required productivity) suitable for schedule updating. The approach is designed to complement existing 4D BIM and digital twin pipelines rather than replace them. A small illustrative example demonstrates the calculations and shows how acceptance gates remain explicit milestones. The discussion clarifies applicability, limitations, and research needs for fusing QA data and handling uncertainty. © 2026 International Association on Automation and Robotics in Construction. Authors: Babanagar N.; Sheil B.
Author full names: Babanagar, Nandeesh (58627979300); Sheil, Brian (55820332500)
Title: Reflective Twins for Deep Excavation using Physics-Informed Machine Learning
Source title: Proceedings of the International Symposium on Automation and Robotics in Construction
Affiliations: Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge, United Kingdom
Authors with affiliations: Babanagar N., Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge, United Kingdom; Sheil B., Department of Engineering, University of Cambridge, United Kingdom
Abstract: Basement construction projects often experience low productivity, schedule delays, cost escalation, safety risks, and high embodied carbon. These challenges largely arise from uncertainty in ground conditions and construction-stage soil-structure interaction, which cannot be fully resolved during design. The observational method offers a structured means of managing this uncertainty by updating design assumptions using monitored performance during construction. However, its adoption remains limited due to the lack of digital tools that robustly integrate monitoring data with predictive and reflective models within construction timescales. This paper proposes a digital twin framework for deep excavations that embeds the observational method within a layered architecture to enable stage-wise model updating and adaptive decision-making. This structure supports progressive automation from descriptive to prescriptive operation while clarifying interactions between monitoring, data handling, modelling, and decision support. The central contribution of the paper is the development of a reflective twin enabling back-analysis engine, based on physics-informed neural networks. The engine enables continuous updating of the virtual model using field observations, allowing physically consistent inference of loads and deformation profiles from sparse and noisy monitoring data. Validation using canonical cantilever retaining wall problems demonstrates robust reconciliation between observed and predicted behaviour. This capability enables rapid model updating and adaptive construction control, thereby operationalising the observational method within a digital twin environment. © 2026 International Association on Automation and Robotics in Construction. Abstract: This research presents an integrated framework for electric delivery fleet routing in urban logistics, in which the dynamics of the real environment are modeled through digital twin and operational uncertainties with a fuzzy approach. The proposed model is designed as a multi-objective model and simultaneously optimizes energy consumption, delivery time, operational cost, and environmental impact. The results show that the use of digital twin leads to a significant reduction in delivery time, cost, and delay compared to static routing, and significantly improves the quality of service. Scenario analyses also showed that in high-density conditions, performance indicators increase nonlinearly, while the proposed framework was able to control these effects. Also, the difference of less than 3.18% with the reference solutions confirms the high accuracy of the model. These findings indicate that the proposed approach can be used as an effective tool to improve the efficiency and sustainability of urban logistics systems. © 2026, Nexora Academic Press. Abstract: Aluminium-waste hydrolysis is a potential route for decentralized hydrogen generation because it can use post-consumer and industrial aluminium residues while reducing dependence on continuous electricity input during the reaction. This review critically evaluates aluminium waste-based hydrogen production by linking reaction chemistry, oxide-layer passivation, reactor design, performance benchmarking, techno-economic assessment (TEA), life cycle assessment (LCA), safety, and system-level integration. Reported hydrogen yields vary because of differences in alloy composition, oxide thickness, surface pretreatment, sodium hydroxide (NaOH) concentration, temperature, reactor hydrodynamics, and gas-collection methods. Continuous-flow and heat-assisted reactors generally provide better reaction stability than simple batch reactors. Still, their scale-up remains limited by corrosion, fouling, alkaline recovery, hydrogen purification, feedstock inconsistency, and aluminium hydroxide sludge management. Reported levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH), energy return on investment (EROI), carbon dioxide (CO2) reduction, and circularity values should therefore be interpreted as condition-dependent ranges rather than universal indicators. The review also discusses machine learning (ML), digital twins, predictive monitoring, and artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted fuel-cell energy management as future tools for improving reactor stability and hybrid renewable integration. Key research needs include standardized reporting, uncertainty-based TEA and LCA, long-duration pilot testing, safe scale-up, closed-loop NaOH recovery, and validated utilization of byproducts. © 2026 American Institute of Chemical Engineers.

Title: Multimodal Ontology: Semantic Substrate for Human Digital Twins in AI-Driven Metaverse Telerehabilitation and Immersive Medical Education

Horbachevsky Ternopil National Medical University, Ternopil, Ukraine; Malakhov K., V.M. Glushkov Institute of Cybernetics of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine, Kyiv, Ukraine
Abstract: The convergence of the metaverse with AI and digital twin technologies is reshaping healthcare delivery and medical education, yet Human Digital Twins (HDTs) – continuously updated virtual patient models – often lack a unifying semantic substrate capable of integrating heterogeneous multimodal evidence (sensor streams, clinical text, imaging, and interaction traces) into actionable meaning for perception, reasoning, and decision support. This viewpoint positions multimodal ontology as that substrate and as a prerequisite for robust AI-driven metaverse workflows in telerehabilitation and immersive medical education. Multimodal ontology is defined at a high level of abstraction and specified via a minimal formalization capturing its essential elements: domain concepts and relations, modality sets, semantic grounding operators that map raw observations to ontological entities, and state-update functions that maintain a temporally evolving HDT knowledge state. Building on recent HDT-enabled telerehabilitation work, the ontology layer is shown to operationalize core metaverse AI functions – environmental perception, semantic understanding, behavioral planning, and human–machine collaboration through interoperable representations, rule-and graph-based inference, and explainable agent behavior across clinician, patient, and intern interfaces. A testable research agenda is outlined for ontology-backed HDTs, emphasizing integration with large-scale multimodal models, validation in simulation and real-world deployments, and evaluation using semantic consistency, reasoning fidelity, user trust, and patient or intern outcomes. The specific contribution is not a new classifier, simulator, or network-optimization mechanism; rather, it is a formal semantic substrate that couples multimodal grounding, confidence-weighted fusion, uncertainty-aware HDT state evolution, and ontology-constrained interaction with large-scale foundation models. © 2026 by author(s). Title: Decision-grade digital twins for in situ bioremediation of contaminated soil and groundwater: a critical review
Affiliations: Department of Microbiology, Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Medical University of Silesia, Sosnowiec, Poland
Authors with affiliations: Cycoń M., Department of Microbiology, Faculty of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Medical University of Silesia, Sosnowiec, Poland
Abstract: Field claims about in situ bioremediation often fail because monitoring data are not mapped to the causal process they are intended to prove. This critical review defines decision-grade digital twins as inferential systems, not as visualization tools, data lakes, or calibrated trend models. A decision-grade twin must connect a living conceptual site model with evidence streams that test competing hypotheses, prediction models with stated admissibility limits, uncertainty updates, and auditable trigger logic. The review evaluates how geochemistry, compound-specific isotope analysis, functional genes and transcripts, flux measurements, geophysical imaging, toxicity endpoints, and high-frequency sensing can support claims about pathway activation, treatment limitation, rebound risk, secondary impacts, and closure readiness. It also distinguishes the decision value of reactive transport models, hybrid process-data models, surrogate models, data-driven surveillance, and microbial process representations. Across hydrocarbons and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, chlorinated solvents, pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances, decision value depends on whether the evidence can distinguish among reaction, retention, redistribution, metabolite formation, and durable risk reduction. The review concludes that digital twins deserve decision-grade status only when they reduce ambiguity that can affect intervention choice, operating intensity, switching criteria, monitoring design, secondary-risk management, or closure judgment. Title: Iron Ore Pelletization in Transition: A Critical Review of Raw Material Constraints, Technological Innovations, and Pathways Toward Low‑Carbon Steelmaking
Source title: Metallurgical and Materials Transactions B: Process Metallurgy and Materials Processing Science
Affiliations: Tata Steel Limited, Jharkhand, Jamshedpur, 831001, India
Authors with affiliations: Mishra B., Tata Steel Limited, Jharkhand, Jamshedpur, 831001, India; Basha S.M., Tata Steel Limited, Jharkhand, Jamshedpur, 831001, India; Dwarapudi S., Tata Steel Limited, Jharkhand, Jamshedpur, 831001, India; Misra S., Tata Steel Limited, Jharkhand, Jamshedpur, 831001, India
Abstract: Iron ore pelletization is becoming increasingly critical to ironmaking as global crude steel production exceeded 1.85 billion tons in 2024, while the availability of high-grade lump ore and sinter feed continues to decline. Current pellet feedstocks are increasingly derived from low-grade and complex ores, typically containing less than 62 pct Fe, (Al2O3 +SiO2) levels above 6 to 8 wt pct, high loss on ignition (LOI), or multimineral ores such as Ti-, V-, and Cr-bearing magnetites. These characteristics impose significant constraints on pellet strength development, reducibility, and high-temperature stability. This review critically examines advances in iron ore pelletization reported over the last decade, with emphasis on raw material beneficiation and blending strategies, binder–flux–additive design, and process innovations directed toward decarbonization. Reported quantitative relationships are synthesized to clarify governing mechanisms and limitations, including reductions in blast furnace productivity of up to ~ 4 pct per 1 wt pct increase in Al2O3, basicity-controlled improvements in reduction degree from ~ 60 to ~ 85 pct in Ti-bearing magnetite pellets, and strength–porosity trade-offs influencing hydrogen reduction behavior. Recent process developments are assessed, including cold-bonded pelletization achieving compressive strengths above 200 kg/pellet without high-temperature induration, electrified and hydrogen-fired induration routes that reduce peak firing temperatures by 50 °C to 75 °C, and digital twin-assisted control of oxidation and sintering profiles. Their associated challenges related to scalability, durability, and industrial robustness are discussed. Particular attention is given to hydrogen-ready pellets, where accelerated reduction kinetics are increasingly offset by sticking, dense iron shell formation, and the absence of well-defined specification frameworks. The review maps how ore quality degradation, decarbonization pressures, and data-driven process control are collectively reshaping pelletization practice and identifies the technical uncertainties relevant to deployment across blast furnace and direct-reduction-based steelmaking routes. © The Minerals, Metals & Materials Society and ASM International 2026.

Title: Bioinspired Microgrid Management: An Approach Based on the Brain’s Sensorimotor Gating
Affiliations: Renewable and Distributed Generation Laboratory, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering’s Power Systems, Patras, 26504, Greece; NTUA, Athens, 15780, Greece; National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (NKUA), Psachna, 344 00, Greece
Authors with affiliations: Papageorgiou P.C., Renewable and Distributed Generation Laboratory, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering’s Power Systems, Patras, 26504, Greece; Giannopoulos A.E., NTUA, Athens, 15780, Greece, National and Kapodistrian University of Athens (NKUA), Psachna, 344 00, Greece; Spantideas S.T., NTUA, Athens, 15780, Greece
Abstract: Microgrids are emerging as key enablers of resilient, sustainable, and intelligent power systems, but they continue to face challenges in dynamic disturbance handling, protection coordination, and uncertainty. Recent efforts have explored brain emotional learning (BEL) controllers as bioinspired solutions for microgrid control. Building on this growing trajectory, this article introduces a new paradigm for neuro-microgrids (NMGs), inspired by the brain’s sensorimotor gating mechanisms, specifically, prepulse inhibition (PPI) and prepulse facilitation (PPF). Sensorimotor gating offers a biological model for selectively suppressing or amplifying responses, depending on contextual relevance. By mapping these principles onto the hierarchical control architecture (HCA) of microgrids, a sensorimotor gating-inspired NMG (SG-NMG) framework is proposed. In this architecture, PPI-like control decisions correspond to protective damping in the primary and secondary management of microgrids, whereas PPF-like decisions correspond to adaptive amplification of corrective control actions. The framework is presented through analytical workflow design, neurocircuitry analogies, and integration with machine learning (ML) methods. A model-based evaluation benchmark is also presented, considering representative microgrid operation scenarios. Results indicate that sensorimotor gating can act as a practical supervisory layer for improving resilience, reducing nuisance actions, and coordinating adaptive responses in converter-dominated microgrids. Finally, open challenges and research directions are outlined, including the mathematical modeling of gating, digital twin validation, and cross-disciplinary collaboration between neuroscience and industrial power systems. The resulting paradigm highlights sensorimotor gating as a promising framework for designing self-protective, adaptive, and resilient microgrids. © 2007-2011 IEEE.

Title: Digital Twin-Based Geometric Error Modeling and Inverse Kinematics Compensation for 5-Axis CNC Machining

Affiliations: German International University, Department of Robotics Engineering, New Administrative Capital, Egypt
Authors with affiliations: Kassem M., German International University, Department of Robotics Engineering, New Administrative Capital, Egypt; Tolba K., German International University, Department of Robotics Engineering, New Administrative Capital, Egypt
Abstract: This paper presents a digital twin-based framework for geometric error modeling and inverse kinematics compensation in 5 -axis CNC machining. The proposed approach models ten geometric error sources using homogeneous transformation matrices embedded within a multibody representation of the machine kinematic chain. A complete digital twin is developed in Simulink from a CAD-derived model of an XYZAB machine and is used to analyze the propagation of individual and combined errors. An inverse kinematics formulation is introduced to address non-orthogonal rotary axes, where conventional Euler-based extraction becomes invalid under realistic machine deviations. A calibration method based on indirect point measurements is implemented within the digital twin to estimate geometric error parameters through a nonlinear system of equations, with simulated noise to replicate realistic measurement uncertainty. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework for identifying and compensating geometric deviations, enabling accurate axis command generation without hardware modification. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: This study presents a prescriptive digital twin framework for the optimal design of methane sensor networks in industrial facilities under uncertain operating conditions. The proposed approach integrates high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics simulations, artificial neural network-based surrogate modeling, Bayesian probabilistic inference, and multi-objective optimization to support severity-weighted risk-informed decision-making. CFD simulations are used to generate detailed methane dispersion data under varying leak scenarios and environmental conditions, capturing the effects of facility geometry, wind dynamics, and turbulence. An ANN surrogate model is developed to provide rapid prediction of key performance metrics, including methane concentration and time-to-detection. Uncertainty in leak characteristics and atmospheric conditions is explicitly modeled and updated using Bayesian inference through an ensemble Kalman Filter, enabling continuous refinement of predictions. The sensor placement problem is formulated as a constrained multi-objective optimization problem and solved using the NSGA-II algorithm to identify Pareto-optimal configurations that balance detection probability, response time, deployment cost, and severity-weighted risk. The results show that methane dispersion is strongly influenced by flow structures such as recirculation zones and high-velocity corridors, which significantly affect detection performance. The proposed framework achieves a higher detection probability (up to ∼96–97%) and a reduced time-to-detection compared to uniform and heuristic placement strategies under equal cost conditions. Moreover, severity-weighted risk analysis identifies high-risk leak scenarios and hazardous regions, while Bayesian updating improves robustness, reduces prediction uncertainty, and enables adaptive risk-informed sensor placement. © 2026 The Author(s). Abstract: Visual navigation offers a low-cost, information-rich solution for agricultural robots, but its deployment is constrained by the diversity and uncertainty of agricultural environments. This review systematically evaluates key technologies—path extraction, tracking control, and multisensor integration—through the S2TAP framework, which examines five interconnected dimensions: Scenario structure, sensing modality, task abstraction, agent mobility, and performance trilemma (the inherent difficulty of simultaneously maximizing accuracy, efficiency, and robustness). The analysis reveals a fundamental dichotomy between wheeled agents (precision tracking) and tracked agents (disturbance rejection), and identifies deep learning’s accuracy gains at the cost of efficiency. Based on these trade-offs, the paper proposes actionable pathways including geometry-first perception, hardware-aware neural architecture search (HW-NAS), uncertainty-aware control, and community-driven standardization (AgriROS and digital twins). Emerging frontiers such as neuromorphic vision and federated learning are also discussed, providing a road map toward robust, scalable visual navigation for autonomous agriculture. This paper presents a structured narrative review that synthesizes the literature through a novel analytical framework rather than an exhaustive systematic review. The paper provides a good reference for the development of visual navigation technology for agricultural robots and vehicles. Copyright © 2026 Yu Han and Zhiyu Song. Abstract: Despite advances in computational hardware and algorithms in the last 30 years, multiphysics computational methods are still not computationally efficient enough for real-time prediction for online controls, digital twins, or a large number of forward functional evaluations in iterative designs, sensitivity analysis, and uncertainty quantification loops. Among the most challenging industrial processes is steel solidification thermo-mechanical phenomena in continuous casting, responsible for over 90% of the world’s steel production. Two innovative deep learning operator methods are trained with coupled thermo-mechanical data from an advanced steel solidification finite element model and studied for encoding multiple input sequential data to predict complete thermal and mechanical solution fields from a real-world steelmaking process. While both trained sequential operator methods can predict solutions accurately and several orders of magnitude more efficiently than the classical finite element method, the single-branch sequential operator network predicted more accurate results than the multiple-branch operator that encodes thermal and mechanical inputs separately. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Abstract: Ecological substrates have emerged as multifunctional slope protection materials with dual engineering stability and ecological restoration benefits, yet their large-scale and long-term application remains constrained in harsh slope environments characterized by steep terrain, arid climates, freeze–thaw cycles, and severe land degradation. The complex coupling of hydromechanical and biological processes in extreme field conditions leads to insufficient systematic understanding of the optimal design criteria and in-situ performance evolution of ecological substrates, restricting their reliable engineering promotion.This critical review comprehensively synthesizes recent advances in ecological substrates from the perspectives of material composition, functional mechanisms, design principles, construction technologies, maintenance strategies, and performance evaluation, with an explicit focus on surface soil erosion and erosion-induced shallow landslides. Particular attention is given to the coupled physical–chemical–biological processes governing substrate behavior and the interactions among substrate properties, vegetation development, and environmental stressors. Based on the existing literature, an integrated framework is proposed to link material design, ecological adaptation, hydrological regulation, monitoring, and long-term performance assessment. The review identifies four major challenges that currently limit the broader application of ecological substrates in harsh environments, including insufficient understanding of early-stage performance, incomplete knowledge of hydro–mechanical–biological coupling, uncertainty in long-term root–substrate evolution, and limitations of existing life-cycle assessment approaches. Future research priorities include the development of low-carbon and bio-based materials, mechanistic studies across multiple scales, intelligent design and digital twin technologies, standardized databases and evaluation systems, and policy support for green infrastructure. These advances are expected to promote the transition from empirical design toward more predictive and sustainable vegetated slope protection. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Abstract: A revolutionary approach for solving worldwide medical inequities has been created at the convergence of digital twin technology, artificial intelligence (AI), and the metaverse. For offering assertive, accurate, and customized care, electronic replicas of patients, pharmaceuticals, or medical facilities can be integrated into metaverse contexts. This chapter explores the methods that these technologies may boost the scheduling of therapy, enable distant diagnosis and measures, and address unique medical issues. These technologies enable healthcare providers to evaluate uncertainty, depict disease growth, and evaluate the effectiveness of medications by recreating patients’ physiological and behavioural characteristics instantaneously, with no need for human interaction. These characteristics may be deployed to better healthcare facilities, simulated medical centers, and interactive medical educational spaces that operate under virtual worlds. © 2027 Balasubramaniam S and Seifedine Kadry.

Abstract: Digital twins are emerging as powerful tools for virtual sensing in power electronics, avoiding the need for dedicated junction temperature sensors. However, adapting thermal models to parameter variations, particularly under changing boundary and operating conditions, without junction temperature measurements remains a key challenge. A hybrid thermal digital twin for power modules is developed based on a physics-informed Cauer network combined with a memory-enhanced Radial Basis Function Network (RBFN) for residual error compensation without requiring direct junction temperature feedback during operation. The Cauer model captures the dominant thermal dynamics of the power module but is affected by uncertain boundary conditions, approximations in power-loss modeling, and structural simplifications of the lumped thermal network. The RBFN compensates residual thermal-model errors through a memory-enhanced correction mechanism that accounts for past operating conditions. The proposed approach is experimentally validated under varying cooling conditions, including forced-to-natural convection transitions. The results demonstrate improved robustness and estimation accuracy compared to the standalone physics-based model, while maintaining a compact structure through residual learning with a lightweight RBFN model. © 2026 IEEJ-IAS.

Title: Hybrid Optimization Approaches for Line Maintenance Scheduling: A 20-Year Review Focused on Turnaround Efficiency in Low-Cost Airlines
Affiliations: Higher Colleges of Technology, Department of Aviation, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates; Military Technological College, Aeronautical Department, Muscat, Oman
Authors with affiliations: Rodrigo W.T.S., Higher Colleges of Technology, Department of Aviation, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates; Khan A.A., Military Technological College, Aeronautical Department, Muscat, Oman; Atukorala N.U., Military Technological College, Aeronautical Department, Muscat, Oman
Abstract: Aircraft line maintenance is essential for flight safety, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency, particularly in the high-frequency, cost-sensitive operations of low-cost carriers (LCCs). As LCCs depend on tight schedules and minimal ground times, optimizing line maintenance during aircraft turnaround has become a critical research focus. This paper provides a systematic review of hybrid optimization approaches developed between 2005 and 2025 to enhance line maintenance scheduling and minimize turnaround time (TAT). Drawing on over 100 academic and industrial sources, the review categorizes contributions across three domains: dynamic programming, heuristic and metaheuristic methods, and machine learning driven predictive analytics. It examines how hybrid models’ combinations of algorithmic approaches have evolved to address complexity, uncertainty, and real-time demands in maintenance environments. Industrial adoption is also assessed, with attention to successful applications, scalability challenges, and limitations in LCC operations. A structured methodology was employed to select and evaluate literature by relevance, rigor, and practical implications. Key performance indicators including TAT reduction, resource utilization, task delay mitigation, and system robustness are synthesized using comparative tables and graphical summaries. The paper highlights research gaps such as limited integration with real-time control systems, underuse of reliability data, and insufficient attention to human factors. The review concludes with recommendations for integrating predictive maintenance data, reinforcement learning, and digital twin technologies into future optimization research. By consolidating fragmented knowledge, this work provides actionable insights for reducing TAT and improving maintenance decision-making in low-cost airline operations. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

Abstract: Predictive maintenance and operational dependability depend on an accurate estimate of the remaining useful life (RUL) of aircraft engines. It helps airlines to schedule maintenance procedures, preventing unplanned downtime and unanticipated malfunctions. Through the use of sensor signals and complex DL models, RUL estimation ensures safety, maximizes engine utilization, and saves on maintenance costs. This paper proposes an AI-powered predictive maintenance system that leverages NASA C-MAPSS data to function as a full-fleet engine (turbofan) system. The process of data preprocessing involves Remaining Useful Life (RUL) generation, Health Index (HI) generation, feature selection, normalization, and sliding window generation. Three deep learning models are designed and tested LSTM with SelfAttention, BiLSTM with Multi-Scale Attention, and Transformer with Squeeze-Excitation on the basis of RMSE, MAE, and R2. Alternatively, experimental findings show that Transformer + SE model works best with a R2=0. 8 5 3 0 and RMSE =15.93 which is superior to the previously employed methods. Moreover, the framework incorporates Explainable AI (XAI), uncertainty-driven risk evaluation, monitoring with a digital twin, and cost-benefit analysis to make decisions and their interpretation more interpretable. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: In the context of climate change, robust operational strategies are required to mitigate water supply depletion and ensure the reliable operation of decentralized water infrastructure systems. Rainwater Harvesting, Treatment and Reuse Systems (RHTRSs) are a feasible option, especially for non-drinking purposes, but their effectiveness depends on maintaining service continuity and compliance with water quality standards under uncertain environmental and operating conditions. In this study, a reliability-oriented Digital Twin (DT) was developed and implemented to simulate the RHTRS of a commercial building, combining the Building Information Modeling (BIM)-based geometry, hydrological study, physical-chemical treatment, Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) modeling, and an immersive Mixed Reality (MR) interface. The DT enables dynamic reliability assessment under uncertainty of system operation under stochastic environmental and demand variability by coupling structural data, hydraulic behavior, and time-series predictions of critical variables, including water availability and total suspended solids. The joint application of BIM, DT, ARIMA-based forecasting module supporting future soft sensing (e.g., turbidimeter), and MR visualization of a real-world, building-scale RHTRS is novel and provides a decision-support system to enhance the reliability, resilience, and safety of complex constructed infrastructure. © 2026 The Author(s).

Abstract: As one of the core technologies of predictive maintenance, the development of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is gradually transitioning from early single-mechanism modeling to a new phase characterized by the deep integration of physics-based approaches, data-driven methods, and uncertainty awareness. This paper first analyzes the fundamental challenges facing this development, such as multi-stress coupling, sensor degradation, and non-stationary noise. By comparing the core advantages and applicability boundaries of statistical models, data-driven models, and hybrid models, it constructs a capability map for RUL prediction. It further points out that current RUL prediction still faces critical capability gaps in areas such as physical consistency and uncertainty decoupling. Finally, the paper distills a new paradigm for engineering implementation, including mechanism-guided neural architecture design and digital twin-driven online parameter adaptation. The research indicates that future RUL prediction studies must transcend the competition over accuracy metrics and shift toward the coordinated development of robustness, interpretability, and decision adaptability—a trinity guided by the principles of “trustworthy AI.” © 2026 by the authors.

Abstract: Urban health and sustainability management is essential for residents, which requires data analytics and visualization tools for decision support. Digital twins are real-time virtual replicas that can map the states and behaviors of physical entities and environments in urban systems. This study proposes a digital twin framework for urban health and sustainability and builds a large-scale air quality management prototype system in Manhattan. The framework comprises: (i) a data-collection module that acquires, cleans, and time-aligns multidimensional streams from CO2/pollutant monitors and other IoT sources, with device metadata, geospatial referencing, and quality-control routines; (ii) an interactive frontend with a 3D digital-twin dashboard, multiscale emissions analytics, and dynamic heatmaps for hotspot detection; and (iii) a backend that couples a Unity WebGL model with a Bayesian spatiotemporal estimator in a state-space formulation. The prototype supports CO2-focused environmental monitoring, spatial analysis, and exploratory scenario evaluation by integrating heterogeneous data, uncertainty-aware estimation, and interactive visualization. © 2026

Abstract: The increasing global generation of municipal, industrial, and agricultural waste, coupled with rising energy demand and stringent environmental regulations, has accelerated the development of intelligent Waste-to-Energy (WtE) systems. Although WtE technologies including incineration, gasification, pyrolysis, anaerobic digestion, and plasma conversion, offer significant potential for sustainable waste management and renewable energy production, their performance is constrained by feedstock heterogeneity, nonlinear process dynamics, emission control requirements, and economic uncertainty. Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a transformative enabler capable of addressing these challenges through advanced data-driven modeling, optimization, and decision-making frameworks. This review provides a comprehensive and critical synthesis of AI applications across the WtE value chain, including feedstock characterization, process optimization, intelligent control, emission monitoring, predictive maintenance, and techno-economic planning. Techniques such as machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, evolutionary algorithms, and hybrid physics-informed models are systematically evaluated. The analysis shows that AI-based approaches can improve energy efficiency by 5–15%, reduce emissions by 10–25%, and decrease operational downtime by up to 40%, while enhancing prediction accuracy beyond 90% in key applications. Beyond summarizing existing studies, this review contributes a unified systems-level perspective and quantitative comparison of AI techniques, while identifying critical challenges related to data quality, model interpretability, cybersecurity, transfer learning, and regulatory integration. Emerging trends, including digital twins, edge AI, explainable AI, and large language model-driven decision support, are highlighted as key enablers of next-generation WtE systems. Overall, the integration of AI into WtE systems represents a paradigm shift from reactive operation to predictive, adaptive, and autonomous management, supporting circular economy strategies and global decarbonization goals. © The Author(s) 2026.

Abstract: Global-wave hindcast products are widely used as environmental inputs in ship design, weather routing, and maritime digital twins. However, their reliability in regions of strong western boundary currents has not been sufficiently quantified from an engineering perspective. This study investigates the effect of wave–current interaction (WCI) on hindcast accuracy and its propagation into ship responses and propulsion performance. Multi-source validation was conducted using global drifting buoys and full-scale measurements from a very large ore carrier equipped with X-band wave radar and strain gauges operating in the Agulhas Current. While hindcasts show high accuracy in open-ocean conditions, a systematic underestimation of the significant wave height is observed under opposing wave–current alignment. Numerical response analyses demonstrate that this bias propagates into ship engineering assessments: vertical wave bending moments (VWBM) can be underestimated by up to a factor of two. Propulsion simulations further show that current-induced wave amplification could offset the expected power reduction from following currents. These findings highlight the need to incorporate WCI-related uncertainties into operational assessments and provide an uncertainty-based framework for risk-informed maritime applications. © 2026 Published by Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Designing multi-view Speed and Separation Monitoring system for multi-robot and multi-human interactions in shared workspace
Affiliations: Department of Mechanical and Materials Engineering, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, 45221-0072, OH, United States; Department of Aerospace Engineering and Engineering Mechanics, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, 45221-0072, OH, United States
Authors with affiliations: Pan Q., Department of Mechanical and Materials Engineering, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, 45221-0072, OH, United States; Onaga K., Department of Mechanical and Materials Engineering, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, 45221-0072, OH, United States; Li R., Department of Aerospace Engineering and Engineering Mechanics, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, 45221-0072, OH, United States; Dong J., Department of Mechanical and Materials Engineering, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, 45221-0072, OH, United States; Ma O., Department of Aerospace Engineering and Engineering Mechanics, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, 45221-0072, OH, United States; Jia X., Department of Mechanical and Materials Engineering, University of Cincinnati, Cincinnati, 45221-0072, OH, United States
Abstract: Designing multi-view Speed and Separation Monitoring (SSM) systems for multi-robot and multi-human environments remains challenging due to high-dimensional solution space and uncertainties in human behavior. Therefore, this paper presents a novel simulation-driven methodology for multi-view SSM system design that integrates probabilistic modeling of human motion, danger-zone-based safety representation, and voxelized visibility analysis, in multi-robot, multi-human work units. Safety-critical events in the proposed methodology are defined as near-miss human intrusion into dynamically updated robot and end-effector danger zones rather than direct physical contacts. Camera placement optimization is formulated as a joint optimization of positions and orientations to balance coverage, occlusion, and viewpoint diversity. To address the resulting computational complexity, a Parallel Efficient Global Optimization (EGO) approach is adopted to search optimal solution based on computationally expensive digital simulations. The proposed approach is validated in two representative human-robot interaction (HRI) scenarios: a CNC machine tending unit with a single robot and a single human, and palletizing lines with multiple robots and multiple humans. In the CNC machine tending case study, the proposed Parallel EGO method identifies a three-camera layout with no uncovered regions (dark areas) and only 1.25% overall vision occlusions (gray areas). It reduces the number of objective-function evaluations by 74.2% compared with GA and 88.5% compared with NOMAD, while achieving a comparable or lower total loss. In the palletizing case studies, the optimized one-, two-, and three-line layouts requires 3, 6, and 11 cameras, respectively, with dark area percentages of 0%, 0.60%, and 1.43%, and gray area percentages of 6.18%, 14.59%, and 16.36%. © 2026 The Society of Manufacturing Engineers

Title: Agora: Digital Twin-Guided Online Reverse Auction for Trust-Aware Vehicular Edge Service Procurement
Source title: Proceedings - 2026 2nd Asia Conference on Communications and 6G, ACC6G 2026
Affiliations: Tongji University, Dept. Of Control Sci. & Eng., Shanghai, China; Guizhou University, Coll. Of Big Data & Information Eng., Guizhou, China
Authors with affiliations: Qi H., Tongji University, Dept. Of Control Sci. & Eng., Shanghai, China; Liwang M., Tongji University, Dept. Of Control Sci. & Eng., Shanghai, China; Zou S., Guizhou University, Coll. Of Big Data & Information Eng., Guizhou, China
Abstract: Reliable and incentive-aware edge service provisioning is critical for emerging vehicular applications. Conventional edge scheduling and offloading methods mainly optimize instantaneous performance, often neglecting provider incentives and dynamic service uncertainty. Purely price-driven procurement similarly fails to capture key non-price factors in highly dynamic vehicular environments, such as mobility, interruption risk, and service continuity. We study a digital twin (DT)-enabled vehicular edge service market, comprising a platform acting as auctioneer, latency-sensitive mobile task requesters, and heterogeneous edge providers hosting standardized virtual service units. To enable responsive, trustworthy, and economically robust scheduling, we propose a digital-twin-guided online trust-aware reverse auction mechanism, termed Agora. Agora integrates DT-based quality evaluation with online reverse auctioning, jointly considering quoted asks and non-price attributes, including delay, interruption risk, continuity mismatch, trust level, and twinmaintenance overhead. A critical-payment rule ensures meaningful provider incentives while maintaining competitive welfare and service performance. Extensive simulations demonstrate that Agora achieves superior performance across multiple metrics and exhibits desirable economic properties, including nonnegative utility for truthful winning providers, value-payment consistency, and empirical robustness against bid manipulation. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Digital Twin technologies for process mechanical systems: Physics-based integration, degradation modeling, and lifecycle-oriented research framework
Source title: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers, Part C: Journal of Mechanical Engineering Science
Affiliations: Department of Mechanical Engineering, Chennai Institute of Technology, India
Authors with affiliations: Amur Venugopal S.B., Department of Mechanical Engineering, Chennai Institute of Technology, India
Abstract: While Digital Twin (DT) technology has proliferated in industries and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS), the application of DT technology to process mechanical systems remains fragmented. Existing reviews have primarily concentrated on discrete manufacturing, machining, or general Industry 4.0 concepts, with little emphasis on the multiphysics, degradation, and integrity needs of pumps, compressors, turbines, heat exchangers, or pressure vessels. This review collates recent advancements in physics-based, hybrid physics-AI, and data-centric DT techs, particularly for process mechanical systems. New contributions of the paper include: a unified treatment of thermo-mechanical, fluid-structure interaction (FSI), rotor system, and physics-of-failure aspects within DTs; comparison with existing manufacturing-centric DTs; and the explicit connection of degradation-aware prognostics to asset integrity and maintenance optimization. By identifying the outstanding issues in realizing real-time multiphysics coupling, uncertainty quantification, validation, and scalability, the paper outlines a domain-specific research roadmap that will enable the transition of DTs from descriptive models to decision support tools that can be trusted for process industries. © IMechE 2026

Title: A Human-in-the-Loop and Explainable AI Framework for Decision Support in Battery Lifecycle Management Using Digital Battery Passports
Source title: International Conference on Human Centric Artificial Intelligence, ICHCAI 2026 - 1st International Conference

Abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are central to electrified transport and renewable energy systems, yet evaluating their sustainability under real operating conditions remains challenging. Conventional life cycle assessment (LCA) approaches rely on static assumptions, generic datasets, and nominal performance values, limiting their ability to support timely and contextaware decision-making across battery use, second-life deployment, remanufacturing, and end-of-life management. These limitations are particularly critical in industrial settings where human actors must make safety-, sustainability-, and valuesensitive decisions under uncertainty. This paper proposes a human-centric Artificial Intelligence (AI) framework for dynamic LCA based on a Digital Battery Passport (DBP) architecture that integrates real-time operational data into environmental assessment and decision support. The system treats the passport as a continuously evolving digital entity that ingests telemetry from the Battery Management System (BMS), interfaces with enterprise systems, and updates environmental indicators through a Digital Twin (DT) environment. AI-enabled analytics interpret degradation behavior, estimate State of Health (SoH), detect anomalies, and generate explainable recommendations for human stakeholders such as fleet operators, sustainability managers, remanufacturing engineers, and recyclers. A dynamic functional unit based on cumulative delivered energy is introduced to replace static capacity-based metrics, enabling a more realistic representation of battery performance over time. The framework supports continuous recalculation of carbon footprint and related environmental indicators, while preserving human oversight through transparent indicators, role-based access, and auditable event logging. Use cases are demonstrated for firstlife operation, second-life classification, and end-of-life pathway selection. The results show that integrating DBP, DT infrastructure, and explainable AI establishes a scalable foundation for human-centered environmental intelligence in the circular battery economy. The challenges include trust, interpretability, data governance, interoperability, SME adoption barriers, and uncertainty in battery health estimation. The proposed approach positions dynamic LCA not only as an automation tool, but as a human-in-the-loop AI system for critical sustainability decisionmaking.  © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Background: Digital twin technology can improve operational visibility, system monitoring and decision support in logistics. However, empirical evidence on organisational readiness for adoption remains limited in emerging logistics economies. Objectives: This study examines organisational readiness for digital twin adoption in Egypt’s logistics sector by assessing the effects of perceived operational benefits, digital workforce skills, managerial support and investment uncertainty. Method: A cross-sectional survey was conducted with 500 logistics professionals across major logistics hubs in Egypt. The questionnaire measured perceived digital twin benefits, workforce digital capabilities, managerial commitment and financial uncertainty. Multiple regression analysis was used to test the determinants of adoption readiness. Results: Perceived operational benefits, digital workforce skills and managerial support had significant positive effects on adoption readiness. Investment uncertainty had a significant negative effect, showing that financial concerns remain an important implementation barrier. Conclusion: Digital twin adoption readiness in logistics depends less on technological feasibility alone and more on organisational capability, managerial commitment and investment clarity. Contribution: The study provides Egypt-specific evidence on the readiness conditions shaping digital twin adoption before full implementation. It offers practical guidance for logistics firms and policymakers seeking to move from digital twin awareness to adoption readiness. © 2026. The Authors.

Abstract: This study presents H2ST, a contextual urban traffic digital twin of the Hay Hassani district in Casablanca, developed within the SUMO framework. We benchmark three car-following models (Krauss, Wiedemann, and IDM) calibrated using Simulation-Based Inference. Specifically, we compare Sequential Neural Posterior Estimation (SNPE) and its active learning variant (ASNPE) under an equal simulation budget. To manage high-dimensional speed outputs, we employ 57 robust summary statistics aligned with real-world TomTom observations. Our results show that SNPE achieves lower posterior uncertainty and greater stability than ASNPE, which exhibits convergence issues in certain parameters. At the model level, IDM provides the best agreement with empirical data, achieving near-perfect fit according to RMSE and NSE metrics. These findings indicate that active learning does not yield measurable benefits in this calibration setting and that IDM combined with SNPE offers a reliable and computationally efficient approach for urban traffic digital twin calibration. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Digital Twin Modeling of Hypersonic Flight Vehicles Based on Dynamic Regression Neural Network
Affiliations: Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing, China; Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology, Shanghai, China
Authors with affiliations: Gao Y., Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing, China; Zhou C., Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing, China; Jian G., Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing, China; Han F., Shanghai Academy of Spaceflight Technology, Shanghai, China
Abstract: As a highly dynamic, strongly coupled, and parameter time-varying uncertain nonlinear dynamic system, Hypersonic Flight Vehicle (HFV) have the problem of difficulty in accurately characterizing their full envelope dynamic characteristics in uncertain environments using traditional analytical models. In response to this issue, a hybrid data-driven digital twin modeling method based on analytical models and dynamic regression neural network is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the residuals between the actual state variables of the HFV and the state variables of the analytical model are calculated. Introducing a dynamic regression neural network based on Gate Recurrent Unit (GRU) encoder-decoder to predict model residuals and actuator input instructions. Secondly, based on the predicted values of the actuator input instructions, the state variables of the analytical model are calculated as the reference values, and the residuals predicted values are used to dynamically compensate the reference values online to ensure the high fidelity of the HFV model. Finally, the parameters of the digital twin model are further updated online according to the actual data measured by the sensor to realize the real-time dynamic matching calibration of the hybrid digital twin model and the HFV dynamics. The digital twin model not only integrates the efficiency and interpretability of the traditional analytical model but also improves the approximation accuracy and rate of convergence and reduces the amount of online training computation by using the analytical model as a priori knowledge compared with the traditional deep learning model. This paper verifies the effectiveness of the proposed hybrid data-driven digital twin model through simulation. © Chinese Society of Astronautics 2026.

Abstract: This article presents a digital twin (DT)-based resilient consensus control framework for multiunmanned aerial vehicles (MUAVs) under integrity attacks. A cyber-physical architecture is developed where distributed DTs support coordination and attack awareness, while physical unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) implement adaptive control to achieve consensus. The contributions are threefold: 1) a data-driven attack detection mechanism using LSTM-RNN is employed to identify integrity attacks affecting system states; 2) a decentralized adaptive control strategy is designed to mitigate attack effects, with Lyapunov-based stability analysis guaranteeing bounded tracking errors under actuator saturation and modeling uncertainties, provided specific gain conditions and graph robustness properties are satisfied; and 3) the framework is validated through simulations on ring and directed leader-follower topologies under single-node, multinode, and leader-targeted attacks, achieving 99.7% detection accuracy on a real UAV fault dataset. The cyber-layer detection outputs trigger adaptive compensation in the physical control loop, ensuring resilient consensus without requiring removal of compromised UAVs.  © 2014 IEEE.

Abstract: Economic Threshold (ET) and Economic Injury Level (EIL) are fundamental concepts in Integrated Pest Management (IPM), providing scientific guidance for determining when pest control measures become economically justified. However, conventional threshold estimation methods often rely on empirical observations, fixed decision rules, and historical field experiments, limiting their ability to respond to dynamic agroecosystems characterized by changing climatic conditions, pest population variability, and fluctuating economic factors. Recent advances in Artificial Intelligence (AI) have created new opportunities for developing intelligent, adaptive, and data-driven approaches for predicting economic thresholds with greater accuracy and efficiency. This review examines the current state of AI applications in predicting economic thresholds for pest management across diverse agroecosystems. The paper first discusses the evolution of economic threshold-based pest management and reviews existing literature on conventional and AI-assisted approaches. Subsequently, recent developments in machine learning, deep learning, reinforcement learning, explainable artificial intelligence, and hybrid AI models are critically analyzed with respect to their capability to forecast pest populations, assess crop damage, estimate yield losses, and support threshold-based decision-making. The review further highlights practical applications of AI in cereal, oilseed, horticultural, plantation, greenhouse, and precision agriculture systems. Current challenges, including limited availability of standardized datasets, model interpretability, regional variability, and climate-induced uncertainty, are also discussed, together with emerging research opportunities involving multimodal data fusion, edge AI, digital twins, and autonomous decision support systems. © 2026, Tehran: Amayesh Shale Consulting Engineers Company.
