Abstract: Road traffic accidents continue to be a significant problem in terms of public health and transport safety. Whilst traditional statistical methods are of fundamental importance for drawing conclusions and evaluating policies, certain approaches have limitations stemming from predefined functional structures, distribution assumptions, limited forms of interaction, and difficulties in processing heterogeneous, high-dimensional or continuously updated data. This review critically synthesises artificial intelligence (AI) applications that directly support safety decisions through accident detection and prediction, the determination of accident frequency and risk, and the assessment of injury severity and duration. The literature is organised within a two-dimensional framework. In the first dimension, studies are classified as vision-based approaches, data-driven AI techniques and spatiotemporal AI models. The second dimension focuses on the roles of these studies in detection, prediction, explanation and decision support. The framework highlights developments ranging from standalone machine learning, convolutional and recurrent models to multimodal fusion, graph-based learning, transformers, foundation models, generative AI and digital-twin-supported simulations. However, the increase in predictive power gives rise to various trade-offs in terms of interpretability, robustness, computational cost, scalability, transferability, data requirements, fairness and readiness for deployment. Consequently, this study focuses not only on performance but also on the explanatory capacity of model families, their applicability and their contribution to engineering and policy decisions. Cross-regional comparison, causal and uncertainty-aware modelling, rare event learning, vision-language reasoning, synthetic scenario generation, digital twin validation and human-supervised decision support systems have been identified as key research priorities. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: A Review on Integration of AI and IoT in Geotechnical Engineering
Source title: Applications of AI and IoT in Geotechnical Engineering for Sustainable Infrastructure
Affiliations: Department of Civil Engineering, Mepco Schlenk Engineering College, Tamil Nadu, Sivakasi, India; Centre for Advanced Research in Environment, School of Civil Engineering, SASTRA Deemed University, Tamil Nadu, Thanjavur, India
Authors with affiliations: Kannan G., Department of Civil Engineering, Mepco Schlenk Engineering College, Tamil Nadu, Sivakasi, India; Sujatha E.R., Centre for Advanced Research in Environment, School of Civil Engineering, SASTRA Deemed University, Tamil Nadu, Thanjavur, India
Abstract: The uncertainty in geotechnical systems and the complexity involved mandate the need for progressive approaches that are continuing in nature for areas like decision-making, analysis and monitoring. Artificial intelligence (AI) and Internet of Things (IoT) offer a transformative framework to address the abovementioned areas of concern as they permit continuous real-time acquisition of geotechnical data using IoT and facilitate its integration using AI for intelligent interpretation, pattern recognition and risk forecasting using a wide range of AI techniques, including machine learning models and hybrid predictive models. Several geotechnical applications such as slope stability assessment, early warning systems, tunnel operations and performance monitoring of structures and substructures like dams, bridges and foundations using integrated AI and IoT techniques have shown considerable success. For example, parameters such as pore pressure, vibration, soil moisture and deformation/settlement are collected using a distributed sensor network and are integrated by applying predictive models to develop early warning systems for natural hazards like floods and landslides or to assess slope stability for large-scale infrastructure and developmental projects. The AI–IoT framework helps in improving prediction accuracy and reduces design uncertainty, thereby enhancing infrastructure resilience and public safety. Also, digital twins offer the potential of real-time simulation and optimization for geotechnical systems. Challenges like data quality, sensor durability, interoperability, reliability of acquired data and its interpretation are present in the current scenario, necessitating interdisciplinary collaboration and development of standard protocols for deployment in the field in case of full-fledged adaptation. AI and IoT can redefine geotechnical engineering practice and open pathways for sustainable infrastructure that is resilient and adaptive. This review aims to summarize the development and available techniques that have been explored and reported in geotechnical engineering using AI and IoT, highlighting the need for progress in this direction. © 2027 selection and editorial matter, Vedprakash C. Title: AI for EV battery health: Statistical meta-analysis and Autonomous Intelligence Pyramid
Affiliations: Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Anil Neerukonda Institute of Technology and Sciences, Sangivalasa, Andhra Pradesh, Visakhapatnam, 531162, India
Authors with affiliations: Tanala S., Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Anil Neerukonda Institute of Technology and Sciences, Sangivalasa, Andhra Pradesh, Visakhapatnam, 531162, India; Venkatesh A., Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Anil Neerukonda Institute of Technology and Sciences, Sangivalasa, Andhra Pradesh, Visakhapatnam, 531162, India
Abstract: The transportation sector accounts for approximately 21% of global CO2 emissions (≈[jls-end-space/]8.4Gt CO2 in 2024), and the electrification of road transport is a critical lever for decarbonisation. Annual global EV battery deployment reached 1.2TWh in 2025, making accurate battery health monitoring essential for both performance and sustainability. This review, conducted via a PRISMA-based protocol over 531 peer-reviewed studies (2018–2026), provides a statistical meta-analysis of all major AI families deployed in battery management: classical machine learning, ensemble methods, deep sequential networks, hybrid CNN architectures, Transformers, Physics-Informed ML (PIML), Explainable AI (XAI), Federated Learning, and Large Battery Foundation Models. A DerSimonian–Laird random-effects meta-analysis with 95% confidence intervals and I2 heterogeneity statistics confirms that CNN–LSTM achieves a pooled RMSE of 0.47% (95% CI: 0.41%–0.53%, (Formula presented) vs EKF baseline) and Transformer architectures reach 0.42% (0.36%–0.48%, (Formula presented) ). The Foundation Model group, based on only nine studies at TRL 2–3, yields a preliminary pooled RMSE of 0.42% that is sensitivity-dependent on a single influential study; this figure should not be directly compared with the more robustly supported Transformer estimate. Critical limitations of all emerging methods are explicitly characterised. Environmental and social impacts of battery energy systems, including CO2 lifecycle analysis, are discussed. An author-proposed five-layer Autonomous Battery Intelligence Pyramid is presented as a speculative research roadmap, with a dedicated implementation pathway discussion, clearly distinguished throughout from experimentally validated findings. © 2026 The Authors. Title: From optimizable to interactable: Mixed digital twin-empowered testing of vehicle-infrastructure cooperation systems
Source title: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies

Abstract: Sufficient testing under corner cases is critical for the long-term operation of vehicle-infrastructure cooperation systems (VICS). However, existing corner case generation methods are primarily AI-driven, and VICS testing under corner cases is typically limited to simulation. In this paper, we introduce an L5 “Interactable” level to the VICS digital twin (VICS-DT) taxonomy, extending beyond the conventional L4 “Optimizable” level. We further propose an L5-level VICS testing framework, IMPACT (Interactive Mixed-digital-twin Paradigm for Advanced Cooperative vehicle-infrastructure Testing). By enabling direct interactions between human operators and VICS entities, IMPACT introduces realistic human-related uncertainties into the testing loop and supports the human-in-the-loop generation of corner cases as a complement to AI-driven methods. Furthermore, the mixedDT-enabled “Physical-Virtual Action Interaction” facilitates safe VICS testing under corner cases, incorporating real-world environments and entities rather than purely in simulation. Finally, we implement IMPACT on the I-VIT (Interactive Vehicle-Infrastructure Testbed), and experiments demonstrate its effectiveness. The experimental videos are available at our project website: https://dongjh20.github.io/IMPACT. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Robustness Evaluation of a Foundation Segmentation Model under Simulated Domain Shifts in Abdominal CT: Implications for Health Digital Twin Deployment
Source title: Proceedings - 2026 IEEE 14th International Conference on Healthcare Informatics, ICHI 2026
Affiliations: University of Illinois Springfield, Healthcare Informatics, Springfield, United States
Authors with affiliations: Basu S., University of Illinois Springfield, Healthcare Informatics, Springfield, United States
Abstract: Foundation segmentation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) have demonstrated strong generalization across natural images; however, their stability under clinically realistic medical imaging domain shifts remains insuﬃciently quantified. We present a systematic slice-level robustness audit of SAM (ViT-B) for spleen segmentation in abdominal CT using 1,051 nonempty slices from 41 volumes in the Medical Segmentation Decathlon. A standardized, ground-truth-derived bounding-box protocol was employed to isolate encoder robustness from prompt uncertainty. Controlled perturbations simulating inter-scanner variability, including Gaussian noise, blur, contrast scaling, gamma correction, and resolution mismatch, were applied across ten conditions. The clean baseline achieved a mean Dice of 0.9145 (95% CI: [0.909, 0.919]) with failure rate of 0.67%. Across all perturbations, absolute mean change in Dice remained below 0.01. Paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction identified statistically significant but small-magnitude changes under selected conditions, while McNemar analysis revealed no significant increase in failure probability. These findings suggest that SAM exhibits stable segmentation behavior under moderate CT domain shifts, supporting its role as a robust foundation baseline for medical image segmentation research. As health digital twins increasingly incorporate foundation segmentation models for anatomical modeling and organ-level monitoring, formally characterizing the robustness of these components under real-world imaging variability becomes a prerequisite for trustworthy twin deployment. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: The rapid growth of energy markets and demand-side response programs has created a significant need for intelligent building-level control strategies to capture high volatility energy consumption in response to price signals and grid conditions. This paper presents a reinforcement learning (RL)-based building energy management framework that models commercial buildings as active, grid-interactive assets capable of providing real-time flexibility while maintaining occupant comfort. The proposed approach integrates historical and real-time data from IoT sensors, HVAC systems, and weather forecasts to build an adaptive environment for RL agents. The RL model is applied to learn optimal control policies that minimize operational energy cost in response to flexibility markets through load shifting, peak shaving, and short-term demand response actions. The framework also incorporates a forecasting module to predict 30-minute interval energy consumption using deep learning, enabling proactive decision-making under uncertainty. Results from simulation experiments demonstrate that the RL agents achieve significant cost savings compared to rule-based control strategies and offer a reliable, automated control to unlock underlying flexibility within building systems. The paper discusses problem formulation, algorithmic development, simulation workflows, comparative metrics, and practical deployment considerations for Saudi Arabia's smart city initiatives. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Multi-line LiDAR 3D construction environment modeling and BIM consistency update method for digital twins
Affiliations: Sichuan University Jinjiang College, Sichuan, Pengshan District, Meishan, 620860, China; Sichuan Tourism University, Sichuan, Chengdu, 610100, China
Authors with affiliations: Liu C., Sichuan University Jinjiang College, Sichuan, Pengshan District, Meishan, 620860, China; Xu X., Sichuan University Jinjiang College, Sichuan, Pengshan District, Meishan, 620860, China; Ding X., Sichuan University Jinjiang College, Sichuan, Pengshan District, Meishan, 620860, China; He G., Sichuan Tourism University, Sichuan, Chengdu, 610100, China
Abstract: Construction digital twins aim to maintain an up-to-date, BIM-consistent as-built state from streaming multi-line LiDAR to enable progress verification, dimensional compliance control, and proactive safety management on construction sites. However, converting sequential LiDAR observations into a temporally stable, element-centric BIM state is difficult in realistic AEC environments. Existing approaches mainly fall into geometry-driven Scan-to-BIM registration frameworks and learning-based point cloud perception models, with some system-level digital-twin frameworks built on BIM-centric reasoning. Purely geometric alignment is brittle under occlusion, clutter, and repetitive structures, and registration uncertainty can propagate to downstream progress and deviation conclusions. Meanwhile, generic perception networks are often trained on static frames, lack temporal stabilization, and do not explicitly optimize BIM-consistent element association or geometry-aware alignment cues. In addition, many digital-twin systems expose limited, loosely coupled state representations that hinder causal, reliable site updates. To address these gaps, we propose LiBiDT (LiDAR–BIM Digital Twin), a causal LiDAR–BIM digital-twin model—where “causal” refers to computational online updating in which only past observations enter the current state—that integrates spatio-temporal mapping, geometric–semantic perception, and scan-to-BIM association for consistent state evolution. LiBiDT consists of Spatio-Temporal Global Registration (STGR) with LiDAR–IMU–GNSS priors, Multi-task Perception (MTP) using a PointNet++ backbone with semantic/instance/normal heads, and Scan-to-BIM Association and State Updating (S2B) via normal-guided point-to-plane refinement, bipartite matching with fused overlap/deviation/semantic evidence, and exponential moving average (EMA) stabilization. The Decision and Risk Analytics (DRA) layer turns the BIM-aligned state into auditable construction-management indicators—weighted completion, deviation summaries, and three forward-evaluable safety/compliance hazard flags. Experiments on three public benchmarks (Hilti SLAM, CV4AEC 2024 Scan-to-BIM, and S3DIS Area-5) cover trajectory, perception, and association evaluation. On CV4AEC 2024 Scan-to-BIM, LiBiDT reaches association F1 = 0.837 and Chamfer Distance (CD) / surface Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 3.2/3.5 cm; relative to the perception-replacement baseline (PointNet++ + S2B, F1 = 0.758) the gain is large, while relative to the strongest competing baseline—CoFiNet (Reg) + S2B at F1 = 0.822—the absolute association gain narrows to 0.015 F1 points, with the bigger gains coming from temporal identity consistency (IDF1 0.854 0.861) and ID-switch reduction. A held-out tile-stream case study visualises BIM-element state evolution, alignment refinement, EMA-stabilised evidence streams, and hazard-flag firing as the scan progressively covers the floor; a strict temporal validation under active construction will require time-stamped multi-acquisition data and is left to future work. Ablation results confirm that evidence stabilization and multi-cue matching contribute complementary gains in accuracy and temporal consistency, yielding a favorable efficiency–accuracy trade-off. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Saltation-consistent event-aware digital twins for uncertainty transport in non-smooth dynamical systems
Affiliations: Sir Geoffrey Leigh Academy, Kent, Dartford, United Kingdom; Institute of Physics, London, United Kingdom
Authors with affiliations: Mosekari S., Sir Geoffrey Leigh Academy, Kent, Dartford, United Kingdom, Institute of Physics, London, United Kingdom
Abstract: Non-smooth mechanical systems challenge prediction not only because their trajectories contain impacts, frictional transitions, and unilateral constraints, but because these events reorganize state propagation, sensitivity, uncertainty, and control authority. Existing digital-twin, hybrid-systems, Bayesian-estimation, and reduced-order frameworks each address part of that difficulty, yet they are usually developed on separate mathematical layers and therefore become least reliable precisely where engineering decisions are most event-sensitive. This paper introduces an event-aware mechanics and inference architecture for non-smooth dynamical systems in which event surfaces are treated as first-class transport interfaces rather than as numerical exceptions. Starting from a high-fidelity hybrid mechanical model with unilateral contact, friction, and measure-valued impulses, we derive saltation-consistent transport laws for sensitivities and covariance, formulate forced Bayesian correction at mechanically determined event times, and establish reduced-order error bounds that isolate jump mismatch as a distinct approximation channel. The resulting framework couples full-order mechanics, event-aware uncertainty propagation, online parameter updating, and reduced-order approximation within a single mathematically consistent architecture. Benchmarks involving impact, stick–slip, and shock-response dynamics show that event-aware transport preserves post-event state accuracy, concentrates parameter information in short event windows, and improves reduced-order fidelity during discontinuity-dominated transients. The central advance is the identification of event surfaces as the structural interfaces through which mechanics, inference, uncertainty transport, and control are coupled in non-smooth digital twins. © The Author(s) 2026.

Abstract: Accurate assessment of the shear buckling behavior of steel beams is essential for ensuring the safety and reliability of steel structures. This study proposes an integrated geometric and mechanical digital twin (DT) framework for the assessment and prediction of shear buckling behavior in steel beams. Steel beams tested to shear buckling failure are taken as the physical entities, whereas the corresponding high-fidelity finite element models reconstructed from 3D laser-scanned point cloud data are regarded as the virtual entities. A geometric DT is first established to explicitly capture the as-measured initial geometric imperfections of the web. Based on sensitivity analysis and particle swarm optimization, the measured mid-span deflection, web out-of-plane displacement, and strain responses collected from the physical entity are fused with the virtual entity to establish a mechanical DT, thereby reducing mechanical uncertainties and improving physical–virtual consistency. The developed DT is finally used for shear buckling assessment and prediction. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework is both feasible and effective, significantly enhancing the accuracy and robustness of structural performance assessment. © 2027 World Scientific Publishing Company

Abstract: Accurate online identification of building thermal states, model parameters, and unknown thermal disturbances is essential for reliable building thermal modeling and advanced energy management. However, conventional Kalman filter-based approaches are highly dependent on manually adjusted noise covariance matrices, making them sensitive to non-Gaussian and time-varying uncertainties commonly encountered in building operations. To address this challenge, this study proposes a neural network-assisted unscented Kalman filter under unknown input (UKF-UI-Net) for the joint estimation of thermal states, RC model parameters, and unknown heat inputs. The proposed framework combines a recurrent neural network with an unscented Kalman filter under unknown input (UKF-UI), enabling adaptive learning of the evolution patterns of process and measurement uncertainties from filtering residuals. RC parameters are augmented into the state vector for simultaneous online identification, while unknown heat inputs are reconstructed through weighted least-squares estimation. This hybrid physics-data framework eliminates the need for manual covariance tuning and enhances adaptability to complex noise environments. The framework is evaluated against fixed-covariance UKF-UI and Sage–Husa-UKF-UI under Gaussian, t-distributed, and nonstationary noise conditions using 35 Monte Carlo trials, and is further validated through experiments conducted in a south-facing test room. Compared with the baseline methods, the proposed method generally improves the overall accuracy and stability of parameter and unknown-input identification while maintaining reliable temperature estimation under complex noise conditions. These results demonstrate that UKF-UI-Net improves the robustness and accuracy of building thermal model identification under uncertainty conditions, providing a practical solution for online model calibration, digital twins, and model predictive control applications. Abstract: Modern digital twins integrated with artificial intelligence (AI) provide significant opportunities for real-time financial governance of critical infrastructure. This paper presents the design and theoretical validation of an intelligent financial decision support system (FDSS) embedded within digital twin ecosystems, spanning the full lifecycle of infrastructure assets. The proposed methodology integrates AI-driven predictive models for cost estimation and failure forecasting, digital twins as continuous real-time data sources, capital and operational expenditure (CAPEX/OPEX) optimization algorithms, and risk-aware investment management strategies that account for cyber threats and systemic uncertainties. The framework introduces a Risk-Aware Financial Digital Twin (RA-FDT) architecture that synchronizes technical state parameters with financial performance indicators through a three-layer integration model encompassing data fusion, analytical intelligence, and decision orchestration. An illustrative scenario-based assessment on energy and transportation infrastructure datasets indicates that the RA-FDT may reduce lifecycle costs by approximately 12-18% under the assumed maintenance, failure-probability, and cybersecurity-risk parameters, while improving risk-adjusted return on infrastructure investment. The principal contribution lies in formalizing the coupling between physical degradation dynamics and financial decision logic within a unified computational environment, thereby advancing transparency, accountability, and effectiveness in critical infrastructure management. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: As digital twins (DTs) become foundational technologies for critical infrastructure (CI), their integration with artificial intelligence (AI) creates new opportunities and risks for financial security, financial intelligence, and governance resilience. Beyond technical and cybersecurity threats, human factors - including decision-making biases, operator trust, and organisational behaviour - significantly influence cyber-financial exposure and the economic performance of DT ecosystems. This paper proposes a human-centric and AI-augmented financial risk management (FRM) framework for secure DTs in CI. The approach integrates real-time DT data, AI-based predictive analytics, explainable decision support, and human-in-the-loop (HITL) mechanisms. It comprises four interconnected components: (1) AI-based forecasting of operational failures and financial losses; (2) behavioural modelling of decision-makers under uncertainty; (3) trust-aware and explainable AI (XAI) mechanisms; and (4) dynamic allocation of financial resources according to risk exposure and infrastructure state. Its methodological contribution is a hybrid decision architecture that links technical system conditions with financial decision-making through a trust-weighted optimisation function, formalised alongside an aggregate financial risk index (FRI) and a Markowitz-style cybersecurity-budget allocation. The framework is assessed through scenario-based simulation for energy and smart-city infrastructure, with parameters informed by open-source cybersecurity and risk-management materials (ENISA threat-landscape reports, NIST IR 8286 Rev. 1, IBM/Ponemon Cost of a Data Breach Report 2025). For the illustrative configuration considered, total expected financial losses across five representative disruption scenarios decrease from 5.82 to 2.70 million USD - a reduction of 53.6% - relative to a baseline FRM without HITL/XAI integration. The results indicate that integrating human expertise, explainable AI, and secure DT technologies can improve financial resilience, reduce disruption costs, and increase trust in AI-supported infrastructure governance. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Advances in slow pyrolysis reactors for sustainable biochar production: design principles, process optimization, and future perspectives
Affiliations: Department of Biosystems Engineering, Faculty of Agriculture, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, Mashhad, Khorasan Razavi, 9177948974, Iran
Authors with affiliations: Yarali S., Department of Biosystems Engineering, Faculty of Agriculture, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, Mashhad, Khorasan Razavi, 9177948974, Iran; Rohani A., Department of Biosystems Engineering, Faculty of Agriculture, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, Mashhad, Khorasan Razavi, 9177948974, Iran; Bayati M.R., Department of Biosystems Engineering, Faculty of Agriculture, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, Mashhad, Khorasan Razavi, 9177948974, Iran; Abhari M., Department of Biosystems Engineering, Faculty of Agriculture, Ferdowsi University of Mashhad, Mashhad, Khorasan Razavi, 9177948974, Iran
Abstract: Slow pyrolysis is a widely investigated thermochemical pathway for biochar production and long-term biogenic carbon sequestration. This review critically assesses the evolution and recent advances in slow pyrolysis reactor technologies from 1950 through December 2025, based on publication availability, focusing on reactor design, transport phenomena, product characteristics, scalability, and commercialization barriers. Four primary reactor configurations—fixed-bed, auger, rotary-kiln, and modified fluidized-bed systems—are systematically evaluated. The analysis indicates that reactor architecture strongly influences thermal management, residence-time distribution, and product selectivity. Under appropriate feedstock characteristics and operating conditions, rotary-kiln reactors can offer favorable prospects for large-scale continuous operation due to effective solids mixing, feedstock flexibility, and heat integration, whereas auger reactors may be particularly suitable for intermediate-scale and decentralized applications under appropriate operating conditions. Fixed-bed systems can remain advantageous for small-scale production, particularly where simple reactor configurations are preferred, although they are constrained by conductive heat-transfer limitations and low throughput. Conversely, fluidized-bed reactors, despite their high heat-transfer rates, require substantial hydrodynamic modifications for biochar-oriented slow pyrolysis and careful control of operating conditions to achieve the desired product characteristics. Biochar yield is strongly influenced by operating temperature, residence time, particle dimensions, and feedstock composition, with reported yields commonly falling within the range of approximately 25 to 45 wt% (dry basis) depending on these factors. Current industrial deployment is impeded by feedstock heterogeneity, thermal non-uniformity, process control limitations, and techno-economic uncertainties. Emerging digitalization strategies, including machine learning and digital twins, show potential for predictive monitoring and optimization, though their industrial implementation requires rigorous validation under transient operational conditions. Life-cycle and techno-economic assessments indicate that slow pyrolysis can contribute to carbon dioxide removal, while emphasizing the critical need for standardized evaluation frameworks. Ultimately, future commercialization will depend on the context-specific integration of advanced reactor engineering, intelligent process control, efficient energy recovery, and robust sustainability metrics. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Coupled biofouling–flow–corrosion prediction and risk assessment of subsea pipelines using bayesian stacked ensembles
Affiliations: Department of Civil Engineering, Saveetha School of Engineering, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences, Tamil Nadu, Chennai, India
Authors with affiliations: Jagajeevan V., Department of Civil Engineering, Saveetha School of Engineering, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences, Tamil Nadu, Chennai, India; Sivakumar V.L., Department of Civil Engineering, Saveetha School of Engineering, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences, Tamil Nadu, Chennai, India
Abstract: Subsea pipelines operate in complex environments where hydrodynamic loading, seawater chemistry, and biofouling interact nonlinearly to accelerate material degradation. Accurately predicting erosion–corrosion under such conditions remains challenging, as conventional assessment methods often rely on simplified assumptions that neglect the hydrodynamic regulation of biofilm stability. This study establishes a Coupled Biofouling–Flow–Corrosion modelling framework using a Bayesian Stacked Ensemble approach. Unlike monolithic data-driven models, this framework decomposes degradation into mechanism-specific learners (erosion, electrochemical corrosion, and biofouling-induced amplification) before integrating them to quantify uncertainty. The model is validated using an experimentally-anchored dataset expanded via physics-constrained augmentation, ensuring that predictions remain physically consistent with observed material behavior while covering a wide spectrum of stochastic operating scenarios. The proposed framework demonstrates superior predictive capability (R² ≈ 0.86, MAE < 0.05 mm/yr) and reveals a critical transition from flow-controlled degradation at early exposure to biofouling-dominated corrosion in mature assets. Furthermore, probabilistic risk mapping identifies localized high-uncertainty hotspots that are invisible to deterministic models. These results provide a robust, interpretable tool for Risk-Based Inspection (RBI) planning and Digital Twin integration in offshore energy infrastructure. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Title: ML-Driven Digital Twin for Supply Chain and Cash Flow Optimization Under Demand Uncertainty

Abstract: Modern retail supply chains operate under significant uncertainty due to fluctuating demand, variable lead times, and dynamic cost structures. Traditional inventory management approaches rely on static reorder policies based on historical averages, which fail to adapt to real-time demand patterns and often lead to suboptimal outcomes such as stockouts or excess inventory.This paper presents an ML-driven digital twin framework for joint optimization of inventory management and cash flow in a retail supply chain setting. The proposed system integrates demand forecasting using machine learning models, including Linear Regression and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, where comparative analysis shows that simpler models outperform deep learning approaches for the given dataset, with a discrete-event simulation engine that models day-level inventory dynamics, replenishment decisions, and financial transactions.The framework evaluates multiple inventory control policies, including a fixed baseline policy, an adaptive policy driven by ML predictions, and an adaptive policy augmented with statistically derived safety stock. Additionally, Monte Carlo simulation is employed to capture demand uncertainty and quantify risk in terms of stockout rates and cash flow variability.Experimental results on a real-world retail dataset demonstrate that the adaptive policy consistently outperforms the baseline approach by improving service levels and stabilizing cash flow, while the inclusion of safety stock significantly reduces stockout risk at the expense of higher holding costs. The proposed digital twin framework provides a robust decision-support tool for supply chain optimization under uncertainty. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: Two-dimensional shallow water equations (2D-SWEs) are essential to watershed flood control, river and lake ecological management, and digital twin development. However, model uncertainty can significantly reduce the accuracy of simulation results. Model structure, including spatial discretization and numerical schemes, is one of the key uncertainty sources. This study conducted an uncertainty analysis of 2D-SWEs using mesh independence, computational efficiency, and computational accuracy as evaluation criteria. It investigated differences in model structure and computational characteristics and further explored the structural causes for these computational differences. The results indicated that all mesh types in Delft3D FM exhibited excellent mesh independence, whereas in MIKE 21 FM, triangular meshes demonstrated better mesh independence than quadrilateral meshes. Compared with the boundary conditions involving upstream and downstream discharge, the boundary conditions including upstream discharge and downstream water level can reduce model uncertainty but may also mask underlying model issues. The computational efficiency of unstructured triangular meshes (UTM) was significantly lower than that of unstructured quadrilateral meshes (UQM) and hybrid meshes (UQM_UTM). Specifically, the computational time of MIKE 21 FM using UTM was 1.54 times that of MIKE 21 FM using UQM and 3.24 times that of Delft3D FM using UQM. All combinations of models and mesh types accurately simulated the spatiotemporal evolution of flow. However, Manning's coefficient for quadrilateral meshes in MIKE 21 FM differed significantly from other combinations. This is primarily because the numerical scheme of MIKE 21 FM is better suited for triangular meshes, whereas that of Delft3D FM is suitable for quadrilateral meshes. Overall, model uncertainty is influenced by boundary conditions, numerical schemes, mesh types, and the coupled effects of various factors. © 2026 Published by Elsevier B.V. on behalf of Hohai University. Abstract: Marine cables are key infrastructure in offshore energy engineering, including deepwater oil and gas development and offshore wind power generation. They undertake essential functions such as energy transmission, production control, signal communication, and connection with subsea systems. Their design, analysis, and operation and maintenance capabilities directly affect the safe and reliable operation of offshore energy systems. Due to the limitations of traditional numerical methods for cross-sectional design and global response analysis in rapid multi-condition evaluation and online operation and maintenance, the application of artificial intelligence techniques in the design, analysis, and operation and maintenance of marine cables has gradually become a research hotspot. This paper presents a systematic review of recent advances in intelligent technologies for marine cables from the perspectives of design, analysis, and operation and maintenance. In terms of design, multi-scale intelligent optimization methods for cross-sectional layout and global configuration are summarized. In terms of analysis, rapid response prediction techniques based on surrogate models and deep learning methods are reviewed. In terms of operation and maintenance, data-driven prediction methods and digital twin systems for structural state assessment of marine cables are discussed. In addition, the key challenges faced by current data-driven methods in physical consistency, model generalization capability, and uncertainty quantification are analyzed. The review finds that artificial intelligence technologies are promoting the evolution of marine cable research from traditional numerical analysis toward an integrated intelligent system covering design, analysis, and operation and maintenance. Future studies should focus on addressing key issues such as insufficient integration between data-driven models and physical mechanisms, limited cross-condition generalization capability, and the lack of online updating mechanisms driven by multi-source monitoring data. © 2026, Editorial Office of Chinese Journal of Computational Mechanics. Abstract: Accurate prediction of complex failure modes in anisotropic composite structures—specifically matrix cracking, fiber rupture, and delamination (stratification)—remains a central challenge in computational fracture mechanics. The primary goal of this work is to bridge the gap between high-fidelity physical modeling and computational efficiency. While the extended finite element method (XFEM) enables mesh-independent crack modeling, its computational cost limits scalability. This work proposes a deep learning–accelerated extended finite element framework (DL-XFEM) that couples physically admissible XFEM fields with a neural network surrogate to predict incremental crack growth. XFEM is employed to generate stress-intensity factors and fracture-consistent state variables, which are used to train the network to replace the most computationally intensive crack-update steps while preserving fracture-mechanics constraints. The proposed framework achieves an 88.3% reduction in runtime relative to standard XFEM. Quantitatively, the method delivers an average trajectory prediction error of RMSE = 0.083 MPa√m and MAE = 0.071 mm, reducing prediction error by 61.2% compared to standard Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) baselines. Generalization is demonstrated across multiple stacking sequences and loading scenarios, and predictions are validated against experimental crack-growth data for aluminum, titanium, and carbon/epoxy laminate specimens. The results indicate that DL-XFEM provides a scalable and physically consistent approach for accelerating fracture simulations in composite structures without sacrificing predictive reliability. Abstract: Physics-Informed Machine Learning (PIML) is a highly promising hybrid model, with a combination of physical principles and machine learning methods, to improve predictive performance, interpretability, and computationally efficiency in the simulation of complex real-world systems. PIML enhances the trustworthiness of forecasting by incorporating physics-based restrictions into data-driven models, retaining causal consistency. This bibliometric work was done via Biblioshiny, VOSviewer and CiteSpace on the publications indexed on the Scopus database and gives a complete picture of the intellectual and structural development of the field. The analysis will demonstrate that the number of scientific publications is growing rapidly each year, with the most prominent authors, journals, and sources of publications. Co-citation networks are used to discover significant thematic clusters, whereas the analysis of international collaboration reveals the key contribution of China and the United States to the field development. The thematic shift of the foundational issues of machine learning and neural networks to the new fields of digital twins, parameter estimation, and anomaly detection is evidenced by keyword co-occurrence and citation burst analysis. Regardless of the rapid growth, uncertainty quantification, real-time data integration, and interdisciplinary standardization have research gaps. Overall, the findings provide a current overview of the evolving PIML research landscape and highlight emerging directions for future investigation. © Copyright Information: Copyright Author (s) 2026 Distributed under Creative Commons CC-BY 4.0.

Title: Models and modeling in human geography I: Classic or new, uncertainty and tradeoffs remain

Authors with affiliations: Grubesic T.H., Center for Geospatial Sciences, School of Public Policy, University of California at Riverside, Riverside, CA, United States
Abstract: Human geographers are constantly endeavoring to deepen our understanding of patterns and processes. As a result, we have no shortage of models to simplify, visualize, explain, and predict human activity on Earth. However, recent advances in geographic modeling approaches are rapidly changing how we address contemporary geographic problems. In this first progress report, I provide an overview and typology of uncertainty in human geography models, enabling researchers to make more informed decisions about their data pipelines and modeling choices. In particular, this work explores uncertainty in classic, deductive models, inductive models, agent-based models, and spatial digital twins. © The Author(s) 2026. Title: Artificial Intelligence for Functional Battery Materials: From Multimodal Mechanism Mining to Closed-Loop Autonomous Optimization

Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping battery-materials research, but its value extends beyond prediction accuracy on static datasets. Functional battery materials involve strongly coupled chemical, structural, electrochemical, interfacial, and processing variables, requiring contextualized data, mechanistic credibility, uncertainty assessment, and experimental validation. This review presents a unified framework connecting multimodal data infrastructure, task-matched AI models, mechanism mining, and closed-loop optimization. We examine battery data sources, representations, FAIR principles, ontologies, reusable platforms, and benchmark limitations, highlighting metadata completeness, domain shift, dataset bias, negative results, and computational-label uncertainty. We compare major model families according to the battery questions they address, their risks, and validation requirements, and discuss applications to cathodes, anodes, electrolytes, solid-state interfaces, and beyond-Li systems. Particular emphasis is placed on whether AI-derived descriptors and latent features can be linked to experimentally testable mechanisms. We further assess active learning, Bayesian optimization, robotic experimentation, real-time control, smart batteries, and digital twins through evidence-hierarchy and closed-loop-maturity perspectives. We argue that battery AI should progress from isolated prediction toward multimodal, mechanism-aware, uncertainty-quantified, and experimentally validated closed-loop discovery. © 2026 Wiley-VCH GmbH.

Title: Acceleration of nonlinear finite element methods in the era of physics-AI: Challenges for interdisciplinary medicine and engineering applications; [物理 AI 时代非线性有限元加速方法与医工交叉应用挑战]
Source title: Jisuan Lixue Xuebao/Chinese Journal of Computational Mechanics

Abstract: Nonlinear finite element analysis remains a fundamental tool for obtaining high-fidelity field variables and mechanistic interpretation in problems involving large deformation, material nonlinearity, contact, friction, and multiphysics coupling. However, the substantial computational cost associated with incremental-iterative solution procedures, tangent updates, and convergence control has created significant bottlenecks for workflows such as multi-scenario parametric studies, optimization-driven design, and uncertainty quantification. With the continued development of automatic differentiation and differentiable simulation frameworks, Physics-AI is driving the evolution of nonlinear finite elements from single-run solvers to learnable, calibratable, and deployable computational components through the integration of data, physics, and algorithms. This review summarizes recent advances in the acceleration of nonlinear finite element methods in the Physics-AI era, covering major methodological routes including data-driven surrogate models, physics-informed neural networks, neural operators, graph neural networks, multi-fidelity strategies, and reduced-order hybrid approaches. Their modeling assumptions, training and inference strategies, error sources, and applicability boundaries are discussed, together with the trade-offs among accuracy, efficiency, interpretability, and verifiability. Motivated by medicine-engineering interdisciplinary applications, the article further outlines application trends and engineering implementation status in scenarios such as personalized biomechanical modeling, preoperative planning, and intraoperative navigation. Finally, from the perspective of practical deployment in engineering and clinical settings, key challenges and future directions are discussed, including data quality, cross-geometry and cross-condition generalization, treatment of nonsmooth mechanisms, uncertainty quantification, and validation frameworks, with the aim of providing a clear technical landscape and research framework for accelerated numerical simulation of mechanics problems. © 2026, Editorial Office of Chinese Journal of Computational Mechanics. Title: Integrating Data-Driven Technologies for End-to-End Supply Chain Transformation
Source title: Data-Driven Innovation in Supply Chains and Manufacturing: From Predictive Analytics to Natural Language Processing
Affiliations: Shiv Nadar University, IOE, New Delhi, India
Authors with affiliations: Shukla S.D., Shiv Nadar University, IOE, New Delhi, India
Abstract: To assist operational choices, data-driven supply chain systems are increasingly using digital twin simulations, machine learning models, statistical forecasting, and Internet of Things–based monitoring. The Fragmented Uncertainty Modeling (FUM) problem, which occurs when uncertainty is estimated locally within individual functions—like demand forecasting, logistics monitoring, or disruption detection—but is not propagated coherently across procurement, production, and fulfillment decision layers, largely plagues current approaches despite these advancements. This fragmentation makes it impossible to reason cohesively about how environmental volatility and exogenous shocks impact the stability and resilience of the entire supply chain. We propose Uncertainty-Propagating Supply Chains (UP-SC), an end-to-end data-driven paradigm that explicitly propagates uncertainty across interdependent decision layers and models supply chains as linked economic–environmental networks. Through a single architectural design, UP-SC combines exogenous climatic volatility signals with global trade dependence structures to enable resilience-oriented decision intelligence and network-aware stability estimates. The NOAA Global Surface Summary of the Day repository and the United Nations Comtrade International Trade Statistics Database are two extensive public datasets that we use to assess UP-SC. Empirical findings demonstrate that, in comparison to function-isolated baselines, explicit uncertainty propagation shortens disruption recovery times by up to 41%, increases turnover efficiency by 22%–35%, and decreases trade corridor lead-time variability by 18%–27%. © 2027 selection and editorial matter, Parth Saxena, Srinivas R. Abstract: The complexity, dynamics, and uncertainty of supply chains in the context of smart manufacturing pose significant challenges to traditional lean management paradigms. To address the core issue of deeply integrating lean principles with intelligent decision-making in a data-driven environment, this paper constructs a lean decision-making framework for smart manufacturing supply chains based on digital twins. A four-stage model encompassing data perception, state identification, strategy optimization, and simulation verification is proposed. By integrating real-time production data, material flow information, and order fluctuation characteristics, a multi-objective lean decision optimization system comprising mathematical models is established. This system covers system state equations, inventory balance constraints, capacity matching mechanisms, multi-objective functions, and intelligent solving algorithms. An improved multi-objective grey wolf optimization algorithm is employed to collaboratively optimize inventory strategies, production scheduling. Furthermore, in supply disruption scenarios, the recovery speed is improved by 42% compared to traditional methods, significantly enhancing the lean level and resilience of the supply chain. This research provides a systematic theoretical foundation and methodological support for smart manufacturing enterprises seeking to build data-driven lean decision-making systems. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

Title: Prospective risk scenario intelligence for industry 5.0: A data-driven framework using synthetic futures, deep learning, and counterfactual interventions
Affiliations: Department of Systems Engineering, École de Technologie Supérieure, University of Quebec, Montréal, Canada; Risk Analytics AI (RAAI), AZ, United States
Authors with affiliations: Gholamizadeh K., Department of Systems Engineering, École de Technologie Supérieure, University of Quebec, Montréal, Canada, Risk Analytics AI (RAAI), AZ, United States
Abstract: Industry 5.0 is conceptualized as an integration of human-centric design, artificial intelligence, digital twins, and cyber-physical systems, through which novel risk pathways are created where safety, security, human–AI interaction, and resilience become tightly coupled. Empirical incident datasets for these emerging configurations are not yet available, by which proactive risk assessment is hindered. A prospective scenario intelligence framework is developed to stress-test future risk states without reliance on historical accident data. Based on a systematic parameter taxonomy derived from the literature, 200,000 synthetic future operating states were generated using a structured generative model. These scenarios were analyzed by transformer-based tabular representation learning, deep embedded clustering for latent risk regime discovery, graph-attention networks for cross-domain co-assurance coupling, deep ensembles with conformal prediction for calibrated uncertainty, self-supervised neural risk ranking, and counterfactual intervention analysis. Seven interpretable risk regimes were identified, including digital-twin drift, security-dominant degradation, cyber-to-physical cascade, and resilient adaptive operation. High-priority scenarios were characterized by elevated multi-domain degradation with weak resilience. The largest simulated risk reductions were obtained through digital-twin recalibration and sensor data-fusion upgrades. The framework offers a prospective computational approach for proactive reliability analysis in Industry 5.0, by which conceptual risk knowledge is transformed into an uncertainty-quantified, model-based roadmap that requires future empirical validation before operational implementation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: TrustTwinCSI: Trust-Aware Digital Twin Personalization for Wi-Fi CSI-Based Respiratory Monitoring
Source title: Proceedings - International Conference on Computer Communications and Networks, ICCCN
Affiliations: Towson University, United States
Authors with affiliations: Wakili A., Towson University, United States; Dhital D., Towson University, United States; Amuda K., Towson University, United States; Asaju B., Towson University, United States; Aderonmu O.S., Towson University, United States; Jung W., Towson University, United States
Abstract: Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) enables noninvasive respiratory monitoring using commodity wireless devices, but deployment is hindered by domain shift across environments, hardware setups, and users. We propose TrustTwinCSI, a trust-aware digital twin framework that combines cross-domain training, uncertainty-aware inference, and volunteer-level personalization for CSI-based respiratory state recognition. A shared CNN+Transformer base model is trained on source domains, Monte Carlo dropout provides predictive uncertainty, and a trust gate supports selective prediction (accept vs. defer) and uncertainty-gated routing to volunteer-specific digital twins. Digital twins are adapted using a few-shot support set via head-only fine-tuning with L2-SP regularization and are accepted only if they improve on a disjoint calibration set, reducing negative transfer. On the ResMon dataset, the selected base model achieves mean Macro-F1 of about 0.77 across four unseen target domains. Selective prediction at τ = 0.80 improves Macro-F1 by +0.051 on accepted samples at 67.8% coverage, while trust-gated digital twin routing improves full-coverage Macro-F1 by +0.037 with 6.3 seconds average adaptation time per volunteer. These results show that uncertainty can be operationalized to improve reliability and regulate safe personalization under domain shift. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Digital twins and explainable AI across the vaccine life cycle: from mRNA manufacturing to thermostability, cold-chain logistics, and immunisation services
Affiliations: Department of Research Publication and Extension, Kampala International University, Uganda
Authors with affiliations: Ugwu O.P.-C., Department of Research Publication and Extension, Kampala International University, Uganda; Okon M.B., Department of Research Publication and Extension, Kampala International University, Uganda; Ogenyi F.C., Department of Research Publication and Extension, Kampala International University, Uganda; Ugwu J.N., Department of Research Publication and Extension, Kampala International University, Uganda; Ugwu C.N., Department of Research Publication and Extension, Kampala International University, Uganda
Abstract: The COVID-19 era accelerated the deployment of mRNA vaccines while exposing persistent weaknesses in manufacturing, thermostability and cold-chain systems, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). This narrative review, informed by an explicit search of PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, IEEE Xplore and the ACM Digital Library (2019–2025), synthesises over 50 studies of digital twins (DTs) and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) across the vaccine life cycle. The evidence indicates that DTs are progressing from static simulations to operational twins for plasmid-to-mRNA production, supporting virtual commissioning, rapid scale-up and real-time optimisation. In parallel, XAI-enabled approaches improve stability prediction, and artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) architectures strengthen cold-chain monitoring and route planning. At the service level, twins of mass vaccination centres and primary-care immunisation services can improve throughput and temperature management; however, current implementations are often siloed, weakly validated and rarely designed with equity considerations. Priorities for the field include integrated, multi-scale ‘vaccine system twins’, rigorous validation, effective human-AI collaboration and deployment strategies tailored to LMIC contexts. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: Physics-Informatics Cross-Domain Consistency- Driven Multi-Time Scale Digital Twin Modeling Method for Power Grids

Abstract: Power grid digital twins (DTs) face a fundamental challenge: uniformly modeling and maintaining consistency across time scales from microsecond-level electromagnetic transients to hour-level economic dispatch. Existing multi-rate simulation techniques have not been systematically integrated into DT frameworks, and current research lacks a theoretical definition for cross-scale consistency. This paper proposes a physics-informatics cross-domain consistency-driven method. A hierarchical multi-rate simulation architecture decomposes the grid DT into Electromagnetic Transient (EMT), electromechanical Transient (RMS), and quasi-steady-state layers. A cross-scale state synchronization algorithm with error propagation suppression is developed. A novel 'Layered Age-of-Information (LAoI)' and 'Twin Bias' framework quantifies uncertainty and consistency. Theoretical analysis establishes boundedness of error propagation, asymptotic stability of the multi-scale observer, contraction of uncertainty propagation, and LAoI thresholds derived from dominant time constants. This work provides a rigorous theoretical framework for multi-time scale consistent DT modeling, including stability proofs, error bounds, and convergence guarantees. © 2026 IEEE.

Abstract: The paper considers approaches to determining secondary criteria and similarity indicators in modeling and optimal control of complex technical systems. It is shown that these criteria can be interpreted as informative features and used in intelligent information technologies, in particular in decision support systems, adaptive control algorithms, and digital twins. An algorithmic approach to integrating secondary similarity criteria into intelligent systems for optimizing the operating modes of energy and other technical objects is proposed. The study examines the mathematical formulation of optimal control problems in which objective functions and constraints are represented as polynomial expressions. Similarity criteria are derived from normalization of these expressions, and secondary criteria are introduced as ratios of primary criteria. Their invariance properties are analyzed for both defined and uncertain systems. Similarity indicators are also considered as scale-based analogues that enable parametric coordination between real objects and their digital models. A structured algorithm for integrating these criteria into intelligent information technologies is described. The approach reduces the dimensionality of optimization problems, increases the stability of control algorithms, and forms reference modes in digital twins. The results apply to optimal control of energy systems and other complex technical objects. © 2026 Copyright for this paper by its authors.

Authors: Li X.; Gao Y.; Shi L.
Title: Exercise adaptation and proactive health: an information-theoretic framework based on load entropy
Affiliations: China Institute of Sport Science, General Administration of Sport of China, Beijing, China; Beijing Normal-Hong Kong Baptist University, Zhuhai, China; Hong Kong Baptist University, Hong Kong, Hong Kong
Authors with affiliations: Li X., China Institute of Sport Science, General Administration of Sport of China, Beijing, China, Beijing Normal-Hong Kong Baptist University, Zhuhai, China; Gao Y., Hong Kong Baptist University, Hong Kong, Hong Kong; Shi L., Beijing Normal-Hong Kong Baptist University, Zhuhai, China
Abstract: Exercise is among the most powerful stimuli for promoting health, yet exercise science still prescribes load largely through fixed, population-derived intensity zones that overlook how individuals perceive and adapt to training stimuli. This review develops Proactive Health as a scientific framework in which exercise is the central means of cultivating adaptive capacity and introduces an information-theoretic model - load entropy - to explain why individuals respond differently to the same exercise challenge. Drawing on principles from complexity science, information theory and non-equilibrium thermodynamics, the framework conceptualises health as adaptive capacity rather than the absence of disease and positions entropy as a central organising principle of biological adaptation. Within this view, health is reframed as adaptive capacity rather than the absence of disease, and entropy becomes a central organising principle of biological adaptation: exercise perturbs the system, transiently raises local entropy and informational uncertainty, and thereby triggers the self-organised reorganisation that underlies training adaptation. Building on psychophysics, the load entropy model reconceptualises exercise load not as a purely mechanical scalar but as the perceptual uncertainty an individual experiences in discriminating a stimulus, which peaks at an entropy-defined "effective stimulus"- a hypothesised, individually and momentarily specific threshold of maximal adaptive challenge. We show how this construct connects to established practice such as heart-rate-variability-guided training and load monitoring, and how it could inform personalised exercise prescription, rehabilitation and digital-twin, AI-enabled care. As a conceptual and hypothesis-driven review, the work generates testable hypotheses for personalised exercise prescription, rehabilitation and exercise monitoring and provides a translational framework for proactive, adaptive healthcare. © 2026 the author(s), published by De Gruyter on behalf of Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Guangzhou Sport University.

Title: Modern weather forecasting: mathematical foundations, tools and current state of the art
Affiliations: “ItalianMeteo” National Agency, Bologna, Italy; Dipartimento di Matematica ed Informatica “Ulisse Dini”, Università di Firenze, Viale Morgagni 67/a, Firenze, 50134, Italy
Authors with affiliations: Cacciamani C., “ItalianMeteo” National Agency, Bologna, Italy; Vespri V., Dipartimento di Matematica ed Informatica “Ulisse Dini”, Università di Firenze, Viale Morgagni 67/a, Firenze, 50134, Italy
Abstract: Modern weather forecasting relies on the integration of observational systems, numerical modeling, data assimilation, high-performance computing, and increasingly artificial intelligence techniques. This paper reviews the scientific and technological foundations of contemporary weather prediction, with particular emphasis on the mathematical and computational tools that support operational forecasting. Weather prediction is based on the numerical solution of the nonlinear partial differential equations governing atmospheric dynamics. The accuracy of these forecasts critically depends on the availability of observations collected from heterogeneous sources, including ground-based networks, weather radars, satellites, aircraft, and other remote sensing platforms. These data are combined with model forecasts through advanced data assimilation techniques, which provide dynamically consistent estimates of the atmospheric state and improve forecast quality. Special attention is devoted to nowcasting, one of the most challenging areas of modern meteorology. At lead times of a few minutes to several hours, rapidly evolving phenomena such as severe thunderstorms, hailstorms, and flash floods require the integration of high-frequency observations, radar extrapolation methods, ensemble prediction techniques, and machine learning approaches. Artificial intelligence is increasingly used to enhance the detection, tracking, and short-term prediction of convective systems, complementing traditional physics-based methodologies. The paper also discusses the requirements of a modern national forecasting system and presents the high-resolution ICON-2I modeling framework operational at the ItaliaMeteo Agency. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of high-performance computing infrastructures, ensemble forecasting systems, and kilometer-scale data assimilation methods. Finally, current challenges and future developments are examined, including convective-scale prediction, uncertainty quantification, exascale computing, digital twins of the atmosphere, and the growing integration of artificial intelligence with numerical weather prediction. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Multi-Modal Urban Mobility under Uncertainty: Mode Selection Based on Dynamic Transport Parameters
Affiliations: Prince Mohammad Bin Fahd University, Al Khobar, Saudi Arabia; The University of Adelaide, Adelaide, Australia
Authors with affiliations: Muhammad S., Prince Mohammad Bin Fahd University, Al Khobar, Saudi Arabia; Mohammad N., Prince Mohammad Bin Fahd University, Al Khobar, Saudi Arabia, The University of Adelaide, Adelaide, Australia
Abstract: This paper presents a detailed model of a multi-modal transportation system that integrates various travel modes—including cars, buses, trains, and bicycles—within a unified framework. The model captures heterogeneous congestion levels, mode-specific travel speeds, and critical infrastructure such as bus stops and train stations, enabling realistic intermodal transfers. To reflect operational variability, it incorporates probabilistic elements like vehicle availability, on-time performance, and delay likelihoods across transport modes. External disruptions, including accidents and adverse weather, are also modeled to assess system resilience under real-world uncertainties. The transportation network is formalized as a Markov Decision Process (MDP), allowing for the representation of stochastic behaviors and non-deterministic route choices. System properties are specified using Probabilistic Computation Tree Logic (PCTL), and a probabilistic model checker is used to evaluate performance. A comprehensive case study demonstrates how probabilistic model checking can support the design and optimization of real-world multi-modal transportation systems by enabling informed selection of key parameters. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Title: Uncertainty-aware hybrid framework for melt pool geometry prediction and process map development in Laser Powder Bed Fusion of Inconel 718
Affiliations: Department of Mechanical and Civil Engineering, Florida Institute of Technology, Melbourne, FL, United States; Department of Industrial Engineering, University of Louisville, Louisville, KY, United States; Department of Mechanical, Materials, and Aerospace Engineering, Illinois Institute of Technology, IL, United States
Authors with affiliations: Saghaian S.E., Department of Mechanical and Civil Engineering, Florida Institute of Technology, Melbourne, FL, United States; Hemmati M., Department of Mechanical and Civil Engineering, Florida Institute of Technology, Melbourne, FL, United States; Hernanz A.C., Department of Mechanical and Civil Engineering, Florida Institute of Technology, Melbourne, FL, United States; Yang L., Department of Industrial Engineering, University of Louisville, Louisville, KY, United States; Saghaian S.M., Department of Mechanical, Materials, and Aerospace Engineering, Illinois Institute of Technology, IL, United States
Abstract: Melt pool geometry governs porosity formation, inter-layer bonding, microstructural evolution, and residual stress development in Laser Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF), making its accurate prediction central to process qualification and process-window development. However, experimental qualification is resource-intensive, high-fidelity multi-physics simulations remain computationally expensive for large-scale parameter exploration, and reduced-order analytical models often lose accuracy near melting-regime transitions. Existing machine learning (ML) approaches provide deterministic predictions but do not explicitly address uncertainty or systematic prediction bias, limiting their reliability across different operating conditions and experimental datasets. This study presents an uncertainty-aware hybrid ML framework for melt pool geometry prediction and process qualification in L-PBF of Inconel 718 (IN718). Single-track and multi-track specimens were fabricated over a broad range of laser powers, scan speeds, hatch spacings, and layer counts and characterized using optical and scanning electron microscopy. The proposed framework combines k-fold ensemble regression with physics-informed directional classification, where the ensemble standard deviation serves as a physically interpretable uncertainty signal and is subsequently converted into a targeted bias-correction mechanism. The melt pool depth-to-width ratio (D/W) was adopted as a unifying descriptor linking melt pool morphology, thermal-gradient-driven grain growth direction, melting-regime transitions, and process-map development. The framework was trained using 68 experimentally measured melt pools and evaluated using an external dataset of 54 measurements compiled from published L-PBF IN718 studies, including validation and independent test datasets. Compared with established analytical models and polynomial curve-fitting baselines, the proposed approach improved predictive accuracy, enhanced cross-study generalization, and provided useful ensemble-based uncertainty estimates. Multi-track experiments further validated the maximum hatch spacing criterion for predicting lack-of-fusion onset from single-track measurements, achieving prediction errors below 6% and enabling the identification of defect-free processing windows. The results demonstrate that ensemble prediction uncertainty contains information related to regime-dependent model sensitivity and can be exploited to improve prediction reliability near conduction-transition-keyhole boundaries. Beyond the specific IN718 case, the proposed framework provides a potentially transferable strategy for uncertainty-aware process qualification and rapid process-window development and offers a computationally efficient foundation for digital twin development, in-situ monitoring, and future closed-loop control of metal additive manufacturing (AM). © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Real-World Deployment of Reinforcement Learning in Robotics: Lessons from Industry

Affiliations: Amity Business School, Amity University, Chhattisgarh, Raipur, India; ISBM University, Chhattisgarh, Raipur, India; Symbiosis Centre for Management Studies, Symbiosis International (Deemed University), Bengaluru campus, Pune, India

Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) in robotics is a learning process, where robotic agents learn to perform tasks by trial and error through interactions with their environment, receiving feedback in the form of rewards or penalties so that their performance can be improved over time. A framework helps to understand RL’s role in robotic operation and decision-making with the aim of achieving long-term goals by maximizing cumulative rewards, without requiring overt programming for every situation, including uncertainty. This allows autonomous agents to adapt to complex and dynamic environments. Behaviors are developed in robots through these techniques for applications like navigation, locomotion, manipulation etc., where lack of environmental consistency fails to provide pre-programmed rules. This chapter explores how RL in robotics is transforming theoretical concepts into real-world industrial deployments. After integrating deep learning with RL approaches like DQN (deep Q-networks) and PPO (proximal policy optimization), robotic perceptions are significantly enhanced, enabling high-level environments policy learning. Industrial sectors that have incorporated RL to enable robots to learn control policies through environmental interaction are basically from manufacturing (FANUC), logistics (Amazon Robotics), healthcare (Stanford’s adaptive exoskeletons), and autonomous navigation (Waymo). This chapter analyzes key case studies from these domains, explaining how RL has been implemented to solve problems such as real-time adaptive control, object manipulation, and dynamic path planning. The discussion also explains major implementation challenges like the simulation-to-reality (sim2real) gap [4], sample inefficiency, safety in exploration, and the black-box nature of deep RL models. The chapter outlines best practices with the help of practical lessons from industry, such as hybrid learning methods and the use of digital twins, for overcoming these challenges. Finally, the chapter explores future research directions, including few-shot learning, explainable RL, and federated learning frameworks, which aim to expand the scalability and trustworthiness of RL-based robotic systems in safety-critical applications. © 2026 Walter de Gruyter GmbH, Genthiner Straße 13, 10785 Berlin, Germany.

Title: Next-generation electrified powertrain technologies for sustainable mobility: A systematic review of architectures, intelligent control, energy storage, and grid integration
Affiliations: Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Anil Neerukonda Institute of Technology and Sciences, Sangivalasa, Andhra Pradesh, Visakhapatnam, 531162, India
Authors with affiliations: Venkatesh A., Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Anil Neerukonda Institute of Technology and Sciences, Sangivalasa, Andhra Pradesh, Visakhapatnam, 531162, India; Tanala S., Department of Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Anil Neerukonda Institute of Technology and Sciences, Sangivalasa, Andhra Pradesh, Visakhapatnam, 531162, India
Abstract: The global imperative to decarbonise road transport has required the automotive and energy sectors to reconceptualise vehicular powertrain engineering across all scales, from atomic-level electrochemistry to fleet-level grid interaction. This PRISMA-compliant systematic review synthesises 120 peer-reviewed publications, standards, and archival documents identified from a four-database search covering January 2018 to June 2026 (1204 records identified; 847 screened; 120 included). Four interconnected technology frontiers are examined in depth: (i) advanced vehicle architectures spanning Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs), Hybrid Electric Vehicles (HEVs), Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs), and Fuel Cell Electric Vehicles (FCEVs), including distributed propulsion with active torque vectoring, in-wheel motors, and grid-connected renewable-source integration; (ii) next-generation electrochemical energy storage covering solid-state, sodium-ion, and lithium–sulfur batteries alongside hybrid supercapacitor architectures, with critical appraisal of conflicting experimental findings on dendrite formation, sodium storage mechanisms, and commercialisation timelines; (iii) intelligent Energy Management Systems (EMS) spanning rule-based control, Equivalent Consumption Minimisation Strategy (ECMS), Model Predictive Control (MPC), the full spectrum of Sliding Mode Control (SMC) variants including super-twisting second-order SMC with adaptive gain laws, Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), and physics-informed neural networks (PINNs); and (iv) grid-interactive infrastructure encompassing Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) systems, wireless power transfer under SAE J2954, and cloud–edge digital twin frameworks with federated learning and cybersecurity provisions. Wide-bandgap SiC and GaN power electronics and six thermal management strategies are analysed as cross-cutting enablers. All quantitative comparison figures in this review (Figs. 13–27) are illustrative reconstructions digitised from data reported in the cited primary literature; they are not independently simulated results, and no new experimental or simulation data are reported in this work. A bibliometric analysis of the 120 included studies reveals growth from 8 papers (2018) to 35 papers (2025). A four-criterion quality assessment framework grades each reviewed technology. A structured technology readiness roadmap with 2030 quantitative projections derived from learning-rate battery cost models and IEA fleet scenarios projects battery costs of $55–70/kWh, SiC penetration of 80–95% in premium BEV inverters, and V2G participation of 8–20% of the EU passenger fleet. These are scenario projections carrying explicitly stated model assumptions and uncertainty ranges, not forecasts; the accompanying sensitivity analysis (Section 12.1) identifies the learning rate and the cumulative-deployment trajectory as the dominant drivers, and a demonstrated-versus-projected classification is applied throughout to separate laboratory or pilot evidence from extrapolation. © 2026 The Authors

Abstract: We propose an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) architecture capable of simultaneously performing distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) and distributed temperature sensing (DTS) in a single-mode fiber (SMF) and experimentally evaluate its coexistence feasibility using a discrete-component proof-of-concept setup. This system supports parallel multi-parameter sensing based on phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry (ϕ-OTDR) and Raman optical time-domain reflectometry (ROTDR). The present experiment is conducted using discrete commercial components, while integrated polarization–wavelength de/multiplexing is retained only as a possible future compact implementation route. Hybrid amplification techniques, including Raman distributed amplification and optical-bias-assisted superimposed enhancement, are introduced to improve the communication link budget and ROTDR detectability under a reduced sensing-probe power. In addition, polarization-diversity reception is analyzed as a potential extension to mitigate polarization fading and improve the stability of Rayleigh-based vibration sensing. Experimental results demonstrate system-level coexistence of ϕ-OTDR-based DAS, ROTDR-based DTS, and single-polarization 2.5 Gbit/s non-return-to-zero/intensity-modulation direct-detection (NRZ/IMDD) communication over a 10 km SMF link. The simplified proof-of-concept experiment achieves a spatial resolution of 5 m, a temperature uncertainty of 2.8°C, and a vibration-sensing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 12.1 dB under a sensing-probe peak power of 100 mW, while no bit errors are observed in the communication branch during the experimental test. Fiber-optic communication and sensing integration technology can support traditional applications such as oil and gas pipelines, power lines, and environmental monitoring, and may provide useful sensing capability for emerging scenarios such as digital twins and intelligent optical networks. © 2009-2012 Optica Publishing Group.
