Abstract: The fast pace of urbanization, tightening discharge requirements, and efficient wastewater treatment require that municipal wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) move to adaptive and intelligent modes of operation. The present review provides an analysis of the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to different pre- and posttreatment steps in the context of municipal WWTPs. Specifically, this review considers how machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL), evolutionary optimization, reinforcement learning, and hybrid AI–mechanistic models can be utilized in municipal wastewater processes. AI-based approaches are reviewed in the area of activated sludge processes such as dissolved oxygen control, nutrient removal, effluent quality estimation, and energy management; membrane bioreactor (MBR) processes such as membrane fouling and transmembrane pressure prediction; anaerobic digestion (AD) processes for biogas generation, stability, energy recovery, and nutrients recovery; and sludge processes such as dewatering, polymer dosage optimization, digestion, and resource recovery. Moreover, AI methods are critically evaluated in the areas of nitrogen and phosphorus removal, N2O emissions prediction, fault detection, predictive maintenance, and plant-wide optimization. Evidence is provided on the implementation of AI in full-scale municipal and WWTPs with a shift from prediction and soft sensing to optimization and supervision, including aeration control, carbon dosing, coagulant optimization, and sludge dewatering. Nevertheless, the findings heavily depend on plant layout, data quality, sensor accuracy, AI architecture, and validation scheme, and none of the AI architectures currently exist that can be deemed superior to other architectures across all applications. Digital twins, explainable AI, edge computing, and federated learning represent exciting directions for future integrated and robust WWTP management. In addition, autonomous plant-level control and AI-assisted AD-nutrient recovery have not been sufficiently developed yet. The main issues to solve are cross-plant validation, uncertainty analysis, cybersecurity, interpretability, seamless integration into existing supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA)/programmable logic controller (PLC) networks, and long-term benefits demonstration. © 2026 Wiley-VCH GmbH.

Title: Digital Support to De-Risking Strategies in Global Supply Chains
Affiliations: Institute of International Politics and Economics, Belgrade, Serbia
Authors with affiliations: Stanojević N., Institute of International Politics and Economics, Belgrade, Serbia
Abstract: Global supply chains operate in a context of rising geopolitical uncertainty, energy volatility, and cyber risks, which makes traditional risk-mitigation approaches increasingly insufficient. This paper reviews key de-risking strategies, such as resilient design, diversification, risk assessment, and enhanced visibility, and examines how digital solutions strengthen their effectiveness. The analysis shows that technologies such as blockchain, digital twin systems, big data analytics, artificial intelligence, and IoT-based visibility platforms improve early risk detection, scenario simulation, and adaptive decision-making. Rather than replacing traditional strategies, digital tools strengthen their capacity to respond to complex disruptions, especially those related to sanctions, protectionist policies, and information security. The paper concludes that digital support represents a critical upgrade to existing de-risking frameworks and contributes to more robust, adaptive, and sustainable global supply chains. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Title: Physics-data fusion-based dynamic model updating of semi-direct-drive offshore wind turbine gearboxes using full-scale test data
Affiliations: State Key Laboratory of Mechanical Transmission for Advanced Equipment, Chongqing University, Chongqing, 401331, China; Goldwind Science & Technology Co., Ltd, Beijing, 100176, China

Abstract: Accurate dynamic modeling of offshore wind turbine gearboxes is essential for vibration response prediction, condition monitoring, and reliability-oriented operation of wind turbine drivetrains under complex offshore conditions. However, conventional models based on nominal parameters often fail to match measured responses because of uncertainties in mesh stiffness, support properties, damping and transmission errors. This study proposes a physics-data fusion-based dynamic model updating framework for semi-direct-drive offshore wind turbine planetary gearboxes using full-scale test data. A coupled gear-bearing dynamic model is established by incorporating time-varying mesh stiffness, nonlinear support forces, damping, and comprehensive transmission error. The uncertain dynamic parameters are normalized and evaluated through dependent sensitivity analysis to identify the dominant contributors to vibration-response discrepancies. These parameters are subsequently updated using a physically constrained optimization strategy driven by measured vibration data. The proposed framework is calibrated and validated using vibration measurements from a full-scale wind turbine gearbox test platform. Results show that the updated model significantly improves the agreement between simulated and measured vibration responses and more accurately captures the dynamic characteristics of the planetary gear train. The proposed approach provides a practical basis for high-fidelity drivetrain modeling and supports condition assessment, maintenance optimization, and digital-twin-enabled reliability management for offshore wind turbines. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Title: TC-LEG: Topology-Constrained Sequential Energy Management in Digital-Twin Smart Grids

Authors with affiliations: Yang Y., Power Dispatching and Control Center, Shenzhen Power Supply Bureau Co., Ltd., China Southern Power Grid, Shenzhen, 518001, China; Cheng W., Power Dispatching and Control Center, Shenzhen Power Supply Bureau Co., Ltd., China Southern Power Grid, Shenzhen, 518001, China; Li Z., Power Dispatching and Control Center, Shenzhen Power Supply Bureau Co., Ltd., China Southern Power Grid, Shenzhen, 518001, China; Gou J., Power Dispatching and Control Center, Shenzhen Power Supply Bureau Co., Ltd., China Southern Power Grid, Shenzhen, 518001, China; Chen Y., Power Dispatching and Control Center, Shenzhen Power Supply Bureau Co., Ltd., China Southern Power Grid, Shenzhen, 518001, China
Abstract: The increasing integration of renewable energy, distributed storage, and flexible loads has introduced substantial uncertainty and operational complexity into modern smart grids. Existing energy management methods can optimize multi-period dispatch or encode the physical grid topology, but they often do not explicitly represent the execution order and conditional dependencies among heterogeneous control actions. This paper aims to develop a safe and energy-efficient sequential control generation framework for digital-twin smart grids that reduces operating cost and renewable curtailment while maintaining voltage security and action feasibility. A topology-constrained latent execution graph learning framework, termed TC-LEG, is proposed. TC-LEG uses a physical grid graph to encode electrical connectivity and operating states, while a distinct latent execution graph represents state-dependent dependencies among storage dispatch, renewable curtailment, demand response, reactive compensation, and topology switching. A hybrid discrete-continuous control sequence generator produces multi-step actions, and a simulation-oriented digital twin synchronizes the current grid state, verifies each candidate action, projects infeasible actions onto a state-dependent feasible set, and feeds the accepted action and updated state back to subsequent generation steps. On the IEEE 33-bus system, TC-LEG achieves a normalized operating cost of 0.811, a voltage violation rate of 0.9%, a renewable curtailment rate of 4.9%, and an action feasibility rate of 98.5%. Its average inference time is 18.6 ms on the IEEE 33-bus system and 28.4 ms on the IEEE 69-bus system, both substantially shorter than the 15-minute control interval. TC-LEG provides a topology-aware and interpretable approach to sequential energy management by combining electrical-topology representation, action-dependency learning, hybrid control generation, and digital-twin verification in a closed-loop inference process. Abstract: Heterogeneous multi-UAV fleets act as highly dynamic mobile Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, but they often integrate platforms with incompatible telemetry and control semantics, hindering safe and scalable coordination. This paper presents an Asset Administration Shell (AAS)-driven digital twin architecture for the cloud continuum that decouples protocol translation from mission orchestration, pushing compute power closer to the edge. The first contribution of this work is a four-layer communication model mapped across the IoT and edge continuum, spanning physical-digital synchronization at the network edge, inter-digital-twin interaction, digitaltwin/ GCS supervision in the fog/cloud layer, and a safety-critical physical/GCS bypass. The second contribution is a UAV AAS submodel that standardizes runtime state, energy, payload, and wireless QoS descriptors. The third contribution is an analytical validation framework based on bounded digital-twin staleness (δSmax = 30 ms) to evaluate semantic task reallocation and QoS-aware telemetry adaptation. At a representative cruise speed of 15 m/s, the worst-case position uncertainty induced by semantic latency is 0.45 m, which is acceptable for highlevel mission handoff. For degraded links, stability conditions are derived for queue-bounded latest-state forwarding and hysteresis-based telemetry control. Title: A comprehensive review of reinforcement learning approaches in peg-in-hole insertion for robotic assembly tasks
Source title: International Journal of Intelligent Robotics and Applications

Authors with affiliations: Shoura A.A., Department of Mechatronics Engineering, Ain Shams University (ASU), Cairo, Egypt; Awad M.I., Department of Mechatronics Engineering, Ain Shams University (ASU), Cairo, Egypt; Maged S.A., Department of Mechatronics Engineering, Ain Shams University (ASU), Cairo, Egypt; Fattah D.E.A., Department of Mechatronics Engineering, Ain Shams University (ASU), Cairo, Egypt
Abstract: Robotic peg-in-hole insertion is a fundamental operation in industrial assembly; however, its automation remains challenging because of tight tolerances, variations in component geometries, contact uncertainties, and the complexity of real-world operating environments. Conventional preprogrammed robotic systems often struggle to cope with such uncertainties, motivating the adoption of reinforcement learning (RL) as a more adaptive paradigm for robotic insertion tasks. This review provides a comprehensive analysis of RL-based approaches for peg-in-hole insertion and examines their evolution from traditional reinforcement learning algorithms to modern deep reinforcement learning (DRL) frameworks. This review systematically categorizes the literature according to the learning paradigm, sensing modality, control strategy, and training environment. Key methodologies are discussed, including Q-learning, SARSA, deep reinforcement learning, model-based RL, meta-RL, transformer-based reinforcement learning, transfer learning, and domain randomization techniques. Particular attention is given to multimodal perception strategies that integrate visual, force, and tactile information, as well as hybrid learning frameworks that combine RL with imitation learning and classical control methods to improve the robustness, training efficiency, and deployment reliability. In addition, this review analyzes recent advances in sim-to-real transfer, digital twin technologies, and real-time deployment strategies that facilitate the transition of learned policies from simulations to industrial robotic systems. A comparative analysis of representative studies is presented to highlight current trends, methodological differences, and practical limitations in the literature. Despite substantial progress, several challenges continue to limit large-scale industrial adoption, including simulation-to-real transfer, sample efficiency, safety, generalization, interpretability, and deployment scalability. Finally, emerging research directions are discussed, including multimodal learning, digital twin-assisted training, hybrid control architectures, multi-agent reinforcement learning, and real-time edge deployment. By consolidating recent advances, limitations, and future opportunities, this review provides a structured reference for researchers and practitioners seeking to develop next-generation intelligent robotic assembly systems. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

Abstract: Interface authorization in flexible automated mine ventilation duct production lines is difficult because heterogeneous users and services access safety-critical resources under time-varying cyber-physical risk that static RBAC/ACL rules cannot capture. This study presents HGRAD, a heterogeneous-graph risk-adaptive access control framework for industrial cyber-physical systems. HGRAD models each access event as a dynamic graph with four node types: user nodes encode operator identity, role, and history; interface nodes represent exposed PLC/MES/service access points and protocol/load states; resource nodes denote commands, records, or work-order objects with different sensitivities; and physics-informed risk nodes provide conservative structural-risk proxies for critical resources. A Temporal-HGT encoder and relation-specific hierarchical attention capture temporal context, structural semantics, and abnormal-path salience, while an intervention-inspired log-based filter, adversarial perturbation, Shapley audit weighting, and MC-Dropout uncertainty estimation support adaptive authorization rather than fixed-threshold decisions. In the TON_IoT benchmark mapping, the physics-informed node is derived only from benchmark-log proxy signals, including access intensity, operation criticality, freshness, and resource criticality; it is not generated by real mine ventilation sensors, plant-side finite-element outputs, or field digital-twin measurements. HGRAD achieves the strongest validation and held-out benchmark performance among compared baselines. The results are therefore benchmark-level proof of concept for access-control design, not evidence of completed industrial deployment or field-validated mine-safety performance. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Dynamic monitoring of railway bridges via coupling digital twins with deep reinforcement learning
Affiliations: Sichuan University Jinjiang College, Sichuan, Meishan, 620860, China; Sichuan Tourism University, Sichuan, Chengdu, 610100, China
Authors with affiliations: Xu X., Sichuan University Jinjiang College, Sichuan, Meishan, 620860, China; He G., Sichuan Tourism University, Sichuan, Chengdu, 610100, China; Liu C., Sichuan University Jinjiang College, Sichuan, Meishan, 620860, China; Ding X., Sichuan University Jinjiang College, Sichuan, Meishan, 620860, China
Abstract: Railway-bridge anomaly detection during retrofitting is a core structural health monitoring (SHM) task, requiring timely alarms for safety. It is challenging because responses are strongly nonstationary and distorted by environmental and operational variability, while sensing budgets constrain what can be observed. Classical feature-and-threshold pipelines are interpretable but fragile to operating-condition drift, yielding unstable alarms without compensation. Deep time-series detectors are effective, but data-only scores are hard to calibrate into risk cues and usually assume fixed sensing. Digital twin (DT) approaches provide uncertainty-aware belief tracking, yet twin-only alarming may respond slowly and may ignore sequential accuracy–cost optimization. We propose Residual Digital-Twin Monitoring with Branching Dueling Q-learning (RDTM-BDQ), coupling an event-triggered Bayesian DT, a mask-aware residual Mamba encoder, and a Branching Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (BDQ) policy. Hybrid evidence fuses DT innovation energy and a normalized safety-margin index with an inverse-projection inconsistency score from the Mamba embedding, forming a belief-augmented state representation for joint alarm and sensing decisions. Training is off-policy with prioritized replay, using a reward that penalizes delay, false alarms, misses, and sensing cost, plus a consistency loss for the inverse projection head. Experiments on the public KW51 and Z24 datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of RDTM-BDQ: on KW51 it achieves 0.95 F1-score (F1) and 0.98 precision, and on Z24 it reaches 0.92 F1-score, confirming robustness to both retrofit-induced and environmentally-induced nonstationarity. Operating-point analysis on KW51 further shows an explicit accuracy–burden–cost trade-off, e.g., reducing detection delay from 41.4 h to 3.9 h with controllable monitoring cost. Ablations confirm that DT cues, residual Mamba encoding, and branching Q-learning each improve accuracy and stability. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: Transition-Based Digital Twin Modelling for Alzheimer’s Disease Under Sparse Longitudinal Data

Abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) progression is highly heterogeneous and is typically observed through sparse and irregularly sampled longitudinal data, posing challenges for reliable prediction and individualised monitoring. Existing machine learning approaches have improved AD prediction using multimodal data, yet they often focus on static classification or cohort-level risk estimation, providing limited support for subject-specific trajectory modelling and uncertainty-aware reasoning. To address these limitations, we present a personalised digital twin framework for Alzheimer’s disease prediction and scenario-based analysis using multimodal longitudinal data. The proposed approach integrates complementary modelling strategies to capture both short-term clinical transitions and longer-range temporal dependencies across follow-up visits. Using data from the Alzheimer’s Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI), including cognitive assessments, clinical variables, and MRI-derived structural phenotypes, the framework predicts future cognitive status and diagnostic categories while quantifying predictive uncertainty and enabling patient-specific what-if trajectory analysis under controlled perturbations of clinically meaningful variables. Experimental evaluation on leak-free subject-level splits demonstrates strong performance in both cognitive score forecasting and diagnosis classification. Importantly, in this sparse and irregular ADNI setting, transition-based modelling of adjacent visits achieved higher predictive accuracy than the sequence-based branch, suggesting that local transition modelling may be more data-efficient under the present data constraints. While sequence models remain valuable for uncertainty-aware trajectory forecasting, local transition modelling offers a more data-efficient and robust predictive strategy in this setting. These findings highlight the importance of aligning temporal modelling strategies with the structure of real-world clinical data and suggest that transition-based digital twin formulations may provide a practical and interpretable approach for personalised disease forecasting and monitoring in neurodegenerative disorders. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2027.

Abstract: As satellite structures become increasingly lightweight, adaptive, and highly integrated, conventional design–simulation workflows struggle to predict dynamic responses and assess structural health under coupled and uncertain conditions. Digital twins, which integrate multi-physics modeling, reduced-order techniques, and modern data-driven approaches, provide a promising paradigm for enabling structural intelligence. This review systematically synthesizes recent advances in structural digital twins, focusing on functional architectures, modeling strategies, and validation frameworks. Representative applications—including thermal control structures, deployable mechanisms, antennas, and propulsion components—are discussed to illustrate the integration of sensing, modeling, and closed-loop control. Key challenges are identified, including heterogeneous data fusion, real-time multi-field coupling, uncertainty quantification, model calibration, and cross-subsystem coordination. Future directions are outlined, such as AI-native digital twins that incorporate physics priors with foundation-model knowledge (i.e., large pretrained AI models), on-orbit edge learning for adaptive real-time inference, federated digital twin systems for distributed knowledge sharing, and trustworthy frameworks with certifiable reliability. These developments are expected to pave the way for adaptive, reliable, and continuously evolving structural digital twins, supporting high-fidelity satellite operations across the full lifecycle. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to The Brazilian Society of Mechanical Sciences and Engineering 2026.

Abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) with nanomaterials science is transforming materials discovery, design, synthesis and characterization. Machine learning, deep learning, generative models, and physics-informed approaches enable accelerated property prediction, inverse design, synthesis optimization and analysis of complex microscopic and spectroscopic data. Recent advances in closed-loop experimentation and autonomous laboratory platforms further demonstrate the potential of AI to reduce experimental search and improve synthesis efficiency. However, the practical translation of AI-assisted nanomaterials research remains constrained by data scarcity and heterogeneity, limited standardization, model interpretability, uncertainty, and restricted generalizability beyond the chemical and experimental spaces represented in training datasets. This review critically examines the current AI-nanomaterials landscape, emphasizing the relationship between computational prediction and experimental validation. Particular attention is given to AI-assisted materials discovery, synthesis optimization, characterization, property prediction, and sustainable and safe nanotechnology, together with methodological considerations for representation, model evaluation, uncertainty quantification, reproducibility and data management. The review also discusses emerging directions, including autonomous laboratories, digital twins, federated learning, quantum machine learning, and physics-informed AI, in terms of their current opportunities and limitations. Future progress will depend not only on improved AI algorithms but also on high-quality FAIR data, physically consistent models, rigorous validation, and closer integration between computational and experimental workflows. Abstract: Trustworthy AI in agriculture is increasingly framed around autonomy: can the system be left alone? We argue this framing is a structural mismatch for an important class of operational environments, which we name expertise-curated environments - domains characterised by expertise-as-ground-truth held by a slow-to-train expert pool, cost-asymmetric errors, and regulatory density. In such environments, autonomy-first decision-making is structurally unfit, not merely conservative to deploy. We propose Curated Uncertainty Exchange (CUE), a pattern in which the expert seeds the AI's training by curating ground truth upstream and arbitrates its operation by reconsultation on ranked uncertainty downstream, mediated by a rank-robust gate that is tolerant of imperfect confidence calibration. We instantiate CUE for heritage viticulture as a deployment pattern over the recently published vinum-Analytics pipeline for grapevine variety identification on the Vinha Maria Teresa parcel of Quinta do Crasto. We re-read vinum-Analytics' published evaluation through the CUE lens and argue that its three operationally-relevant findings - 100% Top-5 accuracy on the in-distribution test set, residual errors concentrated among morphologically similar variety pairs, and a 14.6% detection-failure rate identified as the primary deployment bottleneck - jointly motivate a two-part escalation gate (a structural abstention mechanism for upstream perception failure and a rank-percentile uncertainty mechanism for classifier uncertainty) whose combined expert-review budget is plausibly bounded at K≈15-20%, subject to validation with per-prediction confidence traces and plant-disjoint temporal data. We close by sketching how a multi-session aerial resurvey dataset, already collected at the same site and now under analysis, will support a temporal extension of the gate in future work. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Smart nanoparticle sensors and IoT integration for real-time monitoring of environmental quality in mining systems

Authors with affiliations: Eluri K., Saveetha College of Pharmacy, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences, Chennai, 602105, India; Vaganan H.M., Saveetha College of Pharmacy, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences, Chennai, 602105, India; Elumalai K., Saveetha College of Pharmacy, Saveetha Institute of Medical and Technical Sciences, Chennai, 602105, India
Abstract: The transition toward low-carbon energy systems, electric mobility, and digital infrastructure has intensified the global dependence on mineral extraction while simultaneously increasing the need for real-time, transparent, and predictive environmental governance in mining operations. Conventional monitoring strategies remain largely periodic, spatially limited, and reactive, making them insufficient for detecting rapidly evolving risks such as acid mine drainage, heavy metal mobilization, methane accumulation, airborne pollutants, tailings instability, and operational carbon emissions. This review aims to critically evaluate how nanoparticle-based sensors, when integrated with Internet of Things (IoT) architectures, edge computing, artificial intelligence, and digital twin systems, can transform environmental monitoring in mining from delayed compliance assessment to continuous predictive intelligence. This review synthesizes advances in metal oxide nanoparticles, carbon nanomaterials, plasmonic nanostructures, and hybrid nanocomposites, emphasizing their sensing mechanisms, target analytes, sensitivity, selectivity, matrix interference, durability, and field-deployment constraints. It further examines IoT-enabled wireless sensor networks, localized edge analytics, cloud-based predictive modelling, uncertainty-aware digital twins, and human-in-the-loop governance frameworks for translating nanoscale detection into actionable environmental decision support. Particular attention is given to technology readiness, calibration drift, ruggedization, cybersecurity, interoperability with supervisory control systems, lifecycle sustainability, nanoparticle ecotoxicity, green synthesis, and end-of-life management. The analysis indicates that nanoparticle sensors should not be viewed as replacements for certified laboratory and industrial monitoring tools but as complementary high-resolution screening platforms that can provide early warning, spatial mapping, and dynamic risk prediction. Future progress will depend on standardized validation protocols, long-term field trials, safe-by-design nanomaterials, self-powered sensing nodes, federated environmental data systems, and regulatory pathways that support credible deployment. Overall, nanoparticle-enabled IoT monitoring offers a promising materials-to-systems framework for developing autonomous, sustainable, and digitally governed mining ecosystems capable of minimizing ecological disruption while supporting responsible mineral production. © 2026 Chinese Society for Rock Mechanics & Engineering. Title: Uncertainty Quantification of Random Vibration Fatigue Damage based on PDD-CPM Within a Digital Twin Framework

Abstract: This paper proposes a computational framework, PDD-CPM, which combines Polynomial Dimensional Decomposition (PDD) and the frequency-domain Critical Plane Method (CPM), for the uncertainty quantification of fatigue damage in structural digital twins. Considering the dual randomness of structural parameters and loads, the frequency-domain critical plane method is employed to derive an uncertain fatigue damage function. The PDD method is introduced to efficiently estimate the probabilistic characteristics of fatigue damage. By truncating high-order coupling terms of random variables, it enables rapid calculation of the statistical moments and Probability Density Function (PDF) of fatigue damage with only a small number of samples. Finally, the applicability of the proposed framework is validated through a numerical example. The results demonstrate that, compared to direct Monte Carlo Simulation, the proposed method significantly enhances the computational efficiency of fatigue damage uncertainty assessment while ensuring accuracy. © Chinese Society of Astronautics 2026.

Abstract: Field measurements provide the most reliable validation of in-service structural performance for supertall buildings. However, the scarcity of large-amplitude data under extreme winds critically hinders empirical research into structural non-linearity and energy dissipation mechanisms. To address this gap, this study presents a full-scale field investigation of a 600 m skyscraper during Super Typhoon Hagazah, utilizing a hybrid measurement scheme integrating structural health monitoring system and non-contact interferometric radar. Then, a comprehensive multi-domain analytical framework is proposed to systematically characterize the time-varying structural dynamic behavior. First, measured wind-induced responses are decomposed into static, background, and resonant components via the low-pass filtering and variational mode extraction. Subsequently, high-resolution instantaneous frequency tracking is achieved using the adaptive superlet transform coupled with the Viterbi algorithm and Kalman filtering. Finally, time-varying modal properties and their associated uncertainties are evaluated using covariance-driven stochastic subspace identification with first-order perturbation analysis. Within this framework, the contributions of static, background, and resonant components to the total structural displacement response are quantified through the cross-validation of hybrid measurements. Additionally, the temporal evolution of structural dynamic properties under extreme wind excitation is characterized, emphasizing their dependence on wind conditions and vibration amplitudes. This work yields critical insights into the time-varying dynamic behavior of supertall buildings under extreme wind conditions, establishing an empirical foundation for advancing model-driven damage identification and digital-twin-based performance evaluation. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Digital twin-informed spatiotemporal graph neural network for buffeting response prediction of a long-span bridge
Affiliations: Department of Bridge Engineering, School of Civil Engineering, Southwest Jiaotong University, Chengdu, China; State Key Laboratory of Bridge Intelligent and Green Construction, Southwest Jiaotong University, Chengdu, China
Authors with affiliations: Jiang S.J., Department of Bridge Engineering, School of Civil Engineering, Southwest Jiaotong University, Chengdu, China; Xu Y.L., Department of Bridge Engineering, School of Civil Engineering, Southwest Jiaotong University, Chengdu, China, State Key Laboratory of Bridge Intelligent and Green Construction, Southwest Jiaotong University, Chengdu, China; Li S.M., Department of Bridge Engineering, School of Civil Engineering, Southwest Jiaotong University, Chengdu, China
Abstract: Conventional buffeting analyses of long-span bridges rely on wind tunnel tests and numerical simulations, involving many parameters of uncertainties and suffering from high computational cost. To address these limitations and provide a real-time buffeting response prediction, this study proposes a digital twin-informed spatiotemporal graph neural network (DTI-STGNN) method. This method is composed of three parts: (1) establish a digital twin for buffeting analysis of long-span bridges and generate a dataset from the digital twin, which can cover various wind and structural conditions; (2) design graph convolutional layers, temporal convolutional layers, and loss function of DTI-STGNN and train it using the dataset generated by the digital twin; and (3) develop a hybrid model combining long short-term memory (LSTM) and Transformer to achieve accurate short-term wind speed prediction based on historical wind speed data and then predict the corresponding buffeting response of the bridge using DTI-STGNN. The proposed DTI-STGNN method is finally applied to a real suspension bridge as a case study. The results of the case study show that compared to traditional LSTM and gated recurrent unit models and conventional buffeting analysis methods, the DTI-STGNN method possesses high accuracy and real-time prediction capacity, strong generalization capability, and physical consistency features, offering a new approach for real-time buffeting response prediction and safety assessment of long-span bridges. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. Abstract: Modern satellite payload modules require high structural stiffness, low mass, and thermal stability under coupled thermo-mechanical environments. Conventional separation of load-bearing and thermal-control subsystems often leads to inefficient heat transfer and degraded system performance. This study proposes an integrated structural–thermal design and data-driven digital twin framework combining CFRP honeycomb sandwich panels, a TC4 titanium-alloy ring frame, and integrated heat-transfer paths. Multiphysics simulations predict an in-plane temperature gradient of 3.2K and a maximum elastic thermal deformation of 0.075mm after removal of rigid-body motion. A literature-based comparison with conventional separated configurations indicates a 60%−80% shorter heat-transfer path and a 10%−20% lower structural mass. Model credibility was assessed through mesh-sensitivity analysis and independent analytical benchmarks, with differences of 1.48% in thermal resistance and 7.16% in structural displacement. The digital twin framework supports state prediction, parameter updating, uncertainty quantification, and health assessment. For maximum-displacement prediction, Gaussian process regression achieved R2=0.9996and an RMSE of 0.0136mm, while sequential data assimilation further reduced parameter uncertainty. Using precomputed FEM databases, the platform updated three-dimensional structural–thermal fields within 1.5s, enabling near-real-time response without online full-order FEM re-solution. Overall, the proposed approach provides an efficient and scalable solution for structural–thermal co-design, near-real-time monitoring, and health management of next-generation spacecraft payload modules. © 2026 Elsevier Masson SAS.

Title: Assessing the impact of AI-enabled BIM digital twins on construction risks: a Bayesian Network of Jordanian expert beliefs
Affiliations: Faculty of Engineering, Civil Department, Jadara University, Irbid, Jordan; Faculty of Engineering Technology, Zarqa University, Zarqa, Jordan; Faculty of Engineering, Isra University, Amman, Jordan
Authors with affiliations: Albtoush F., Faculty of Engineering, Civil Department, Jadara University, Irbid, Jordan; Al-Btoosh J.A.A., Faculty of Engineering Technology, Zarqa University, Zarqa, Jordan; Rawashdeh T.M., Faculty of Engineering, Isra University, Amman, Jordan; Al-Btoush M.A.K.A., Faculty of Engineering, Isra University, Amman, Jordan
Abstract: Building projects in Jordan routinely experience substantial schedule delays and cost overruns, yet robust empirical evidence on the impacts of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Building Information Modelling (BIM)-based Digital Twins remains scarce. This study develops a belief-based, probabilistic causal model of how AI-enabled BIM Digital Twin technologies may affect time–cost risks in Jordanian reinforced-concrete building projects. Using structured expert elicitation with 600 experienced practitioners (contractors, consultants, project managers, and academics), we capture expert judgements on causal links between four technology clusters—AI-based progress detection, contract-aware BIM assistants, predictive cost–schedule twins, and AI-assisted design/constructability—and key project mechanisms and outcomes. All quantitative results in this study come from these expert judgements; no project-level before–after performance data are used. Accordingly, results are reported as pooled expert beliefs under stated scenarios, not empirically validated predictions. Hierarchical Bayesian models pool elicited probabilities into a Bayesian Network (BN) representing collective expert beliefs, rather than observed project performance. Monte Carlo simulations, Global Sensitivity Analysis (GSA), and Expected Value of Perfect Information (EVPI) are then used to explore technology-adoption and policy scenarios and to rank influential levers. Experts believe that, under idealized, high-readiness conditions, AI-enabled BIM Digital Twins could sharply reduce the probabilities of schedule delays >20% and cost overruns >10%. These figures are belief-based, optimistic upper-bound expectations derived from expert judgement, not empirically measured or validated impacts. The Bayesian Network therefore serves as an uncertainty-aware decision-support tool for early policy and investment decisions in data-poor contexts. It highlights the roles of training, organizational readiness, and client demand alongside technology adoption. Copyright © 2026 Albtoush, Al-Btoosh, Rawashdeh and Al-Btoush.

Title: AI-Driven Optimization for Climate-Resilient Infrastructure
Source title: AI-Driven Innovations for Smart and Resilient Infrastructure
Affiliations: University of Miskolc, Hungary
Authors with affiliations: Kovács A., University of Miskolc, Hungary
Abstract: This chapter presents a comprehensive artificial intelligence (AI) framework for optimizing climate-resilient infrastructure through integration with nature-based solutions (NbS). The methodology combines predictive analytics, multi-objective optimization, and digital twin technologies to address complex challenges in infrastructure design under climate uncertainty. Through a detailed coastal city case study, the framework demonstrates 55% reduction in flood risk, 30% lower embodied carbon, and 25% cost savings compared to conventional approaches. The chapter provides practitioners with scalable tools for implementing AI-driven resilience strategies while addressing ethical considerations in algorithmic decision-making. Key innovations include hybrid physics-AI modeling, adaptive reinforcement learning systems, and explainable AI interfaces for infrastructure planning. Title: Interference- and Fidelity-Aware Hybrid Task Offloading in Digital Twin-Enabled Vehicular Edge Computing
Affiliations: RMIT University, School of Engineering, Melbourne, 3000, VIC, Australia
Authors with affiliations: Jin H., RMIT University, School of Engineering, Melbourne, 3000, VIC, Australia; Gregory M.A., RMIT University, School of Engineering, Melbourne, 3000, VIC, Australia; Li S., RMIT University, School of Engineering, Melbourne, 3000, VIC, Australia
Abstract: Reliable task offloading in vehicular edge computing (VEC) is difficult because mobility, co-channel interference, finite edge capacity, and imperfect digital twin (DT) information evolve together. Existing DT-assisted schemes may also leave a gap between the learned decision and the radio–computing action that is executed. We propose IAC-DDPG, a hybrid offloading framework that combines interference-aware clustering (IAC) with deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG). It separates the actor observation, scheduler context, and physical state, models field-dependent DT uncertainty through age of information (AoI), and constructs a mobility–workload–interference coordination context. Its actor selects local, edge, or finite partial-execution modes, per-roadside-unit admission gates, and resource shares. A common action builder and deterministic scheduler enforce lifecycle, radio, connection, and computing constraints before execution, yielding causal task progress, feasible allocation, attempt-consistent radio accounting, and exactly-once closure. Across three training seeds on a frozen paired controlled-mobility bank, IAC-DDPG records the highest arithmetic-mean success among the learned controllers (0.209 versus 0.171 for position-only), but the paired gap is concentrated in one seed. It also records the lowest mean 95th-percentile terminal delay, although all controlled p95 values lie near the 2-s upper end of the deadline range. The mechanism study shows 88.1% lower residual coupling and 47.6% lower cluster churn. We report every seed and claim neither seed-robust nor statistically significant superiority. © 2014 IEEE.

Title: CausalTwinOps: Governance-Gated Counterfactual Repair Verification for Enterprise Data Pipelines
Affiliations: Federal Express Corporation, Dallas, TX, United States
Authors with affiliations: Konduru R.K., Federal Express Corporation, Dallas, TX, United States
Abstract: Enterprise data-pipeline incidents can propagate across latency, freshness, completeness, validity, cost, and governance metrics, so recovery requires more than anomaly detection or root-cause ranking. This paper presents CausalTwinOps, a governance-gated counterfactual repair-verification framework that separates root-cause nomination from repair acceptance. The evaluated implementation uses a fixed, domain-defined fault vocabulary, an auditable ordinary-least-squares response model with selected interaction terms, counterfactual feature interventions, a template repair library, and explicit service and governance constraints. The present study focuses on offline, window-level repair verification with interpretable intervention semantics; online causal discovery, learned repair policies, and continuous twin synchronization are natural extensions beyond the evaluated scope. Across four random seeds and 489 synthetic incident cases, CausalTwinOps obtains 95.3% mean root-cause accuracy and 99.0% top-2 accuracy. Several supervised classifiers trained directly on the synthetic root labels obtain higher classification accuracy, which highlights the complementary roles of fault nomination and repair verification. The distinguishing result is the verification stage: removing the governance gate raises mean repair acceptance from 63.5% to 99.2% but yields 162 unsafe accepted repairs, whereas the configured full verifier yields none under the benchmark’s policy-risk and validity constraints within the simulator. This zero count is a compliance result relative to the configured simulator rules, not evidence that unmodeled real-world harms are impossible. The core contribution is thus a decision layer that tests whether a candidate repair is predicted to improve downstream state while remaining inside configured safety constraints. The controlled simulator provides a reproducible setting for characterizing mechanism behavior under known assumptions. To support the next validation stage, we report seed-level uncertainty, make causal and statistical assumptions explicit, and define a concrete external-validation protocol for real or semi-real incident data. © 2013 IEEE.

Title: Generative Digital Twin-Enabled Prognostics and Health Management: A Systematic Review of Concepts, Architectures, and Key Technologies

Abstract: Prognostics and health management (PHM) for industrial equipment is still constrained by scarce fault samples, incomplete observation of degradation processes, limited cross-condition generalization, and fragmented maintenance knowledge. Digital twins (DTs) provide a physical–virtual integration basis for PHM through state synchronization, model updating, and service feedback. However, conventional DT-enabled PHM remains limited in data supplementation, degradation inference, knowledge organization, and maintenance decision-making. The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) offers a new pathway for enhancing DT-enabled PHM. This review focuses on generative digital twin (GDT)-enabled PHM. It clarifies the conceptual boundaries and functional enhancement logic of GDT-enabled PHM, summarizes the roles of key GenAI models, and reviews technical progress across health data synchronization, twin data processing, virtual modeling, prognostic reasoning, and maintenance decision feedback. A cross-process perspective is introduced to trace how data, model, and reasoning errors propagate into PHM reliability risks. Representative applications in aero-engines, rotating and transmission equipment, and energy equipment are then examined with attention to their validation boundaries. Finally, the review discusses generated-data validity, physical consistency, lifecycle updating, uncertainty, and engineering deployment under Industrial Internet of Things constraints. © 2014 IEEE.

Title: A Digital Twin Model for Real-Time Electric Vehicle Energy Consumption Estimation and Validation Using Unity–Simulink Co-Simulation
Affiliations: Department of Energy, Politecnico di Milano, Milan, 20156, Italy; School of Electrical Engineering, China University of Mining and Technology, Xuzhou, 221116, China
Authors with affiliations: Canali G., Department of Energy, Politecnico di Milano, Milan, 20156, Italy; Martino A.D.I., Department of Energy, Politecnico di Milano, Milan, 20156, Italy; Longo M., Department of Energy, Politecnico di Milano, Milan, 20156, Italy; Rong C., School of Electrical Engineering, China University of Mining and Technology, Xuzhou, 221116, China
Abstract: Accurate real-time estimation of electric vehicle (EV) energy consumption is essential for range prediction, energy management, and the development of digital twins for advanced mobility applications. However, existing driving simulators often rely on simplified vehicle models that fail to capture the interaction between driver behavior, vehicle dynamics, and battery-state evolution under realistic operating conditions. This paper presents a high-fidelity digital twin framework for real-time EV energy consumption estimation based on the co-simulation of a Unity driving environment and a physics-based battery model developed in MATLAB/Simulink. The proposed architecture combines immersive vehicle dynamics, detailed road and terrain reconstruction, and a second-order equivalent circuit battery model through a low-latency User Datagram Protocol (UDP) communication layer, enabling synchronized real-time execution. The framework was calibrated using a Tesla Model 3 Standard Range and validated against experimental measurements collected on three real-world routes characterized by different traffic and operating conditions. Model accuracy was assessed through the Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and coefficient of determination (R2). Experimental results demonstrate high predictive accuracy, with route-dependent MAPE values ranging from 2.63% to 5.40% and a maximum R2 of 0.859. Furthermore, the proposed digital twin accurately reproduces energy-consumption trends over a wide range of initial battery State of Charge (SoC) conditions, from 96% to 28%. The analysis of residual errors highlights the influence of terrain elevation uncertainty, thermal effects of battery, and auxiliary loads on prediction accuracy. The results obtained demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a reliable and computationally efficient tool for EV energy assessment, digital-twin applications, eco-driving studies, and future intelligent charging and energy-management strategies. © 2013 IEEE.

Abstract: Consumer-Centric Digital Twins (CCDT) require privacy-preserving and personalized intelligence on resource-constrained consumer devices such as smartphones and wearables. To support this setting, we propose Scalable Federated Personalized Aggregation with Posterior Approximation (SFed-PAPA), a scalable personalized federated learning framework that serves as the twin assimilation layer. SFedPAPA models client uncertainty with a Gaussian posterior approximation based on Taylor expansion, empirical Fisher, and KFAC, performs posterior-guided adaptive cohort selection, and generates client-specific weighted aggregates under asynchronous updates. We evaluate SFedPAPA on four healthcare-sensing benchmarks spanning classification and regression, and further analyze asynchronous updates, dynamic client participation, hyperparameter sensitivity, computational overhead, and differential privacy. SFedPAPA achieves 95.73% accuracy on HAR, 79.37% accuracy on WESAD, 2.18 MAE on PT, and 6.93 MAE on PPG-DaLiA, indicating its potential for scalable personalization in consumer-oriented digital twins for Healthcare 5.0. © 1975-2011 IEEE.

Title: Toward AI-assisted digital force metrology: A vision for the digital metrology avatar
Affiliations: CSIR National Physical Laboratory, New Delhi, India; Force and Hardness Metrology Group, New Delhi, India
Authors with affiliations: Vikas, CSIR National Physical Laboratory, New Delhi, India; Tewari K., Force and Hardness Metrology Group, New Delhi, India; Gautam S.K., Force and Hardness Metrology Group, New Delhi, India; Kumar K., Force and Hardness Metrology Group, New Delhi, India; Kumar R., Force and Hardness Metrology Group, New Delhi, India
Abstract: Force metrology is undergoing a paradigm shift from conventional hardware-centric sensing toward smart measurement systems enabled by the confluence of novel sensors, computational imaging, optical metrology, and artificial intelligence (AI). The article presents a forward-looking perspective on how these emerging technologies may collectively reshape the future of force metrology. Rather than a complete measurement system, the article describes the concept of a Digital Metrology Avatar as a self-powered, computationally extensible, intelligent, and traceable representation of a physical force measurement system that can perform traceable sensing, computational imaging, intelligent inference, and digital metrology services in a connected measurement ecosystem. To illustrate the feasibility of this vision, we present a representative proof-of-concept case based on a precision flexure transducer and laser speckle pattern imaging. The example demonstrates how experimentally observable elastic deformation features can be extracted using Fourier optics and phase correlation image processing and subsequently correlated with the applied force using Gaussian process regression. By building upon the example and the recent developments in non-contact sensing, the article gives a vision of how software-based, AI-assisted metrology could be realized in force metrology by utilizing uncertainty-aware AI, digital twins, digitalized calibration infrastructures, and explainable AI methods. © 1998-2012 IEEE.

Title: Digital Twin Readiness of Mechanical Coffee Dryers: A Systematic Review
Affiliations: Faculty of Electronic Engineering and Telecommunications, Universidad del Cauca, Popayán, 190001, Colombia; Cluster Creatic, Popayán, 190001, Colombia
Authors with affiliations: Valencia-Payan C., Faculty of Electronic Engineering and Telecommunications, Universidad del Cauca, Popayán, 190001, Colombia; Casanova Olaya J.F., Cluster Creatic, Popayán, 190001, Colombia; Corrales J.C., Faculty of Electronic Engineering and Telecommunications, Universidad del Cauca, Popayán, 190001, Colombia
Abstract: Thermal drying is a critical phase in coffee processing, significantly influencing energy consumption, moisture uniformity, storage stability, and sensory quality. Despite the superior throughput of mechanical dryers over open-sun drying, these systems often operate with limited observability and manual control. This systematic review evaluates the readiness of mechanical coffee drying for Digital Twin (DT) integration. A comprehensive search across Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and ScienceDirect identified 22,859 records. Following multi-stage screening, 58 studies were retained for qualitative synthesis, categorized into a primary coffee-drying corpus and a secondary transferable corpus of methods from related food-processing applications. Findings indicate that while DT-enabling components, such as CFD models, drying-kinetics models, IoT monitoring, and non-destructive sensing, are established, they remain fragmented. No fully implemented and operationally validated DT for mechanical coffee drying was identified. Based on the evidence, a hybrid reduced-order physics-based model integrated with constrained supervisory control represents the most defensible near-term architecture. Future research should prioritize standardized datasets, uncertainty-aware soft sensors, and field validation across diverse dryer topologies and operating conditions. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Digital twin technology for HIV patient virtual modeling: a novel approach to treatment optimization

Abstract: Background – Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection remains a global health challenge, necessitating personalized treatment strategies to optimize patient outcomes. Digital twin technology—synchronized with real-world entities—offers a pathway to precision medicine in HIV care. Methods – We analyzed 5, 436 HIV patients (2016–2024) with demographic, immunologic, and antiretroviral therapy (ART) information. Core algorithms comprised gradient boosting and random forest ensembles; deep architectures (LSTM and Transformer networks) were evaluated as comparative benchmarks on longitudinal feature tensors under identical supervision. Models used five-fold cross-validation, regularization, dropout, and early stopping. A probabilistic treatment ranking layer generated diversified regimen suggestions conditioned on model outputs. Results – Ensemble models achieved strong explained variance on the registry-defined CD4 label (test R2 up to 0.97; cross-validation stability reported in the Results). Deep models achieved comparable held-out accuracy on the same endpoint; the ranking module produced balanced regimen distributions in an illustrative optimization cohort. Simulated digital twin scenarios demonstrated counterfactual CD4 projections under alternative ART strategies for low, moderate, and higher baseline immunology profiles. Discussion – The specific contribution is an explicit patient-state → prediction → regimen exploration pipeline suited to integration with telehealth analytics (risk dashboards, adherence supports), while transparently acknowledging endpoint and leakage limitations and the need for prospective outcome validation. A pragmatic HIV treatment optimization strategy is to route model-supported prioritization into clinician-facing dashboards and remote monitoring workflows rather than autonomous prescribing. Title: Intelligent Recognition of Building Facade Defects: A Multilevel Review from Visual Perception to Engineering Operations and Maintenance

Abstract: Building facades are continually exposed to weathering, material aging, hygrothermal cycling, and service-related disturbances. Cracks, delamination, spalling, and seepage can compromise durability and safety, while associated thermal anomalies provide indirect evidence of deterioration. Deep learning, UAV inspection, infrared thermography, LiDAR, building information modeling (BIM), and digital twins have shifted facade inspection toward automated sensing and spatially referenced assessment. Yet most studies remain focused on isolated measures of model accuracy and give limited attention to the full pathway from detection and quantification to component localization, condition rating, and repair. This review organizes the evidence along five dimensions: annotation granularity (A0–A2/A2*), visual task hierarchy (T1–T5), fusion level (F0–F3), spatial mapping level (S0–S3), and engineering maturity (M1–M3). The synthesis indicates that acquisition conditions, material heterogeneity, negative-sample composition, and annotation rules constrain model generalization. Single-modality methods cover classification, detection, segmentation, and partial geometric quantification, but facade-specific external validation remains limited. Multimodal gains depend on registration quality, thermophysical conditions, defect mechanisms, and sensor reliability. Mapping two-dimensional outputs to point clouds, BIM, and digital twins is technically feasible, but error propagation, component matching, and condition-rating protocols remain inconsistent. Interpretability tools and vision foundation models may support verification, annotation, and reporting but cannot replace dedicated systems with validated error bounds. Future work should prioritize cross-dataset benchmarks, facade-specific lightweight models, reproducible multimodal evaluation, standardized 2D-to-3D accuracy protocols, uncertainty-aware manual review, and engineering condition-rating frameworks. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Digital Twin-Assisted Chance-Constrained Energy-Aware Scheduling for Self-Sustainable IIoT Networks
Affiliations: Department of Electrical Engineering, College of Engineering, Northern Border University, Arar, 12271, Saudi Arabia
Authors with affiliations: Alenezi A.H., Department of Electrical Engineering, College of Engineering, Northern Border University, Arar, 12271, Saudi Arabia
Abstract: On-demand data sensing and Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) enable sustainable operation in large-scale Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) networks. Existing scheduling frameworks are inherently reactive, initiating charging only after an IoT node’s residual energy falls below a predefined threshold, which increases the risk of energy outages and service disruption. This paper proposes a Digital Twin (DT)-enabled proactive scheduling framework for self-sustainable IIoT networks under stochastic operating conditions. The proposed framework integrates three key components. First, a DT layer continuously mirrors IoT node states and predicts future energy availability over a finite prediction horizon. Second, a predictive charging strategy proactively schedules WPT before energy depletion occurs. Third, physical-layer security and DT-based anomaly detection protect the network against eavesdropping, false-data injection, and energy depletion attacks. Fourth, the scheduling framework is reformulated using chance constraints to explicitly account for uncertainty in wireless channels, energy consumption, and DT prediction errors while providing probabilistic reliability guarantees. The resulting sensing and WPT scheduling problems are formulated as multi-slot integer optimization problems and solved using branch-and-bound, with a low-complexity greedy heuristic for latency-sensitive deployments. Simulation results show that the proposed framework reduces energy outage events to below 1%, maintains reliable operation under increasing energy uncertainty with only a modest sensing-utility reduction, and incurs negligible computational overhead compared with the deterministic formulation. © 2026 by the author.

Title: Adaptive Digital Twin synchronization under bandwidth constraints: A quantile forecasting and Kullback–Leibler divergence approach

Abstract: Maintaining real-time synchronization between physical assets and their Digital Twins over bandwidth-limited wireless links is challenging. Existing approaches either transmit all sensed data, resulting in unnecessary network overhead, or rely solely on forecasting, which cannot guarantee fidelity when operating conditions change. In response, we propose an uncertainty-aware, event-driven synchronization framework that preserves twin fidelity while reducing network traffic. A Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) trained via quantile regression forecasts key twin states and produces 10th–90th percentile prediction intervals; an online quantile-coverage test tracks predictive reliability, and a Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence monitor detects distributional drift. During stable periods, the twin runs in predictive mode: only a subset of real states is fetched from the physical asset, while the remainder is inferred locally. If the KL-divergence monitor signals drift, the framework synchronizes the buffered ground truth and places the next interval in direct synchronization mode; the predictor is retrained only when the resulting empirical coverage falls below the required threshold. Evaluations on public LTE and 5G datasets achieve R2>0.80 in most cases, with a peak of 0.99. A multi-output variant forecasts two parameters jointly and maintains strong accuracy across the evaluated LTE traces, highlighting the utility of multi-output regression for adaptive synchronization. On-device tests with a commercial smartphone reduce network traffic by 5.41%–7.01% compared to direct synchronization, while trace-driven evaluations show that the framework lowers mean absolute error (MAE) by about 64% on average relative to simpler predictive baselines. Estimated operational cost savings range from $3.84–$38.40 per device annually, indicating substantial cost reductions at scale. Overall, the framework combines calibrated forecasting with drift-aware control to enable high-fidelity digital twinning under strict bandwidth constraints. © 2026 The Authors

Title: Machine Learning for Structural Steels: Materials Design, Property Prediction, Durability, and Future Directions

Abstract: Machine learning (ML) provides new opportunities to model the nonlinear relationships among composition, processing, microstructure, defects, properties, and in-service degradation of structural steels. This structured critical review examines ML applications to materials and process design, microstructural characterization, mechanical-property prediction, corrosion, fire and elevated-temperature performance, fatigue, fracture, and remaining-life assessment. Literature published up to 31 July 2026 was searched primarily through the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus. A total of 110 publications were retained based on their relevance to structural steels, transparency of data and modeling procedures, and availability of information on validation or engineering applicability. The reviewed studies show that model suitability depends strongly on data modality, sample independence, feature representation, and validation strategy rather than on algorithm family alone. ML has progressed from property prediction toward process optimization, inverse materials design, environmental degradation assessment, and fatigue- and crack-related prognostics. However, independent cross-manufacturer, cross-laboratory, production-scale, and field validation remains limited, while uncertainty quantification and applicability-domain assessment are still inconsistently reported. These limitations are particularly important for corrosion, fire, fatigue, and remaining-life applications, where internally validated models should not be interpreted as substitutes for established physical models or design provisions. Future research should prioritize standardized multimodal data, physics-informed and uncertainty-aware modeling, prospective validation, and rigorously evaluated closed-loop monitoring and digital-twin frameworks for structural-steel life-cycle management. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Artificial Intelligence in Orthopaedics: Current Evidence and Clinical Translation Across the Patient Care Pathway
Affiliations: Hospital Nove de Julho, São Paulo, 01409-002, Brazil; Docente no Programa de Pós Graduação em Enfermagem, Universidade Guarulhos (UnG), São Paulo, 07023-070, Brazil
Authors with affiliations: González R.D.N., Hospital Nove de Julho, São Paulo, 01409-002, Brazil; Mello P.L., Docente no Programa de Pós Graduação em Enfermagem, Universidade Guarulhos (UnG), São Paulo, 07023-070, Brazil
Abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) has expanded rapidly across orthopaedic practice, yet routine clinical adoption remains limited despite strong technical performance. This narrative review examines why a persistent gap separates technical maturity from clinical maturity across the orthopaedic patient care pathway. Methods: We performed a structured qualitative evidence synthesis of contemporary high-level evidence (systematic reviews, diagnostic test accuracy meta-analyses, and structured narrative reviews) retrieved from PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by backward screening of reference lists, covering January 2022 to June 2026. Twenty-one evidence syntheses were analysed thematically across six predefined analytical domains and organized according to the orthopaedic patient pathway. Reporting followed the SANRA (Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles) criteria. Results: Musculoskeletal imaging and fracture detection represented the most mature domains, with several applications reaching early clinical adoption. Applications in arthroplasty planning, shoulder surgery, perioperative prediction, multimodal AI, and clinical decision support remained at developing or emerging stages. Recurrent barriers included limited external validation, dataset heterogeneity, poor workflow interoperability, limited explainability, regulatory and ethical uncertainty, and scarce patient-centred outcome evidence. Conclusions: The principal challenge facing orthopaedic AI is no longer algorithm development but clinical translation. We propose the ORION Clinical Readiness Framework, an evidence-informed five-domain model describing the transition from Technical Performance through Clinical Validation, Workflow Integration, and Patient Benefit to Routine Clinical Adoption, to guide implementation and future research. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Artificial Intelligence for Structural Condition Assessment and Rehabilitation: Recent Advances and Future Directions
Affiliations: Department of Civil Engineering, College of Engineering, The University of Texas at Arlington, Arlington, 76019, TX, United States
Authors with affiliations: Zare S., Department of Civil Engineering, College of Engineering, The University of Texas at Arlington, Arlington, 76019, TX, United States; Najafi M., Department of Civil Engineering, College of Engineering, The University of Texas at Arlington, Arlington, 76019, TX, United States
Abstract: The growing need to ensure the safety, resilience, and sustainability of existing building structures has accelerated the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) for structural condition assessment and rehabilitation. This critical narrative review synthesizes 82 retained sources, including 33 application-oriented sources, through a transparent, structured literature search and study-selection process; it is not a formal systematic review or meta-analysis. To organize this fragmented evidence base, the review introduces the Data-to-Decision (D2D) Continuum, a unifying conceptual framework that traces eight engineering stages from data acquisition through damage detection, localization, quantification, condition and performance assessment, prognosis, reliability and risk assessment, to rehabilitation decision support. Classical machine learning, deep and temporal models, physics-guided and probabilistic approaches, and emerging foundation models are examined according to the engineering output required at each stage. The strongest evidence concerns bounded defect detection and localization, whereas uncertainty-aware prognosis, risk-informed rehabilitation selection, multi-site validation, and governed deployment remain markedly less mature. By integrating existing monitoring, digital-twin, life-cycle risk, and maintenance-decision concepts into an interface-centered evidence chain, the D2D framework clarifies what must be validated before an AI output can responsibly influence an intervention. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: A Review of Mechanical Degradation, Interfacial Nonlinear Dynamics and Multi-Bolt Coupling Degradation Mechanisms of Flange-Bolted Joints
Affiliations: Naval University of Engineering, Wuhan, 430033, China
Authors with affiliations: Feng X., Naval University of Engineering, Wuhan, 430033, China; Guo M., Naval University of Engineering, Wuhan, 430033, China; Wang S., Naval University of Engineering, Wuhan, 430033, China; Lu X., Naval University of Engineering, Wuhan, 430033, China; Liu Y., Naval University of Engineering, Wuhan, 430033, China; Li Z., Naval University of Engineering, Wuhan, 430033, China; Wang W., Naval University of Engineering, Wuhan, 430033, China; Xu Z., Naval University of Engineering, Wuhan, 430033, China; Liu Y., Naval University of Engineering, Wuhan, 430033, China
Abstract: Bolted flange joints are critical load-bearing connection components of complex mechanical equipment, whose service performance is dominated by the coupled evolution of bolt preload relaxation and interfacial stiffness degradation under long-term cyclic combined loads. Under cyclic transverse excitation, the contact interfaces experience successive full-stick, partial microslip and macroslip states, accompanied by embedding, creep and friction-induced wear, resulting in time-varying preload attenuation and the continuous degradation of joint mechanical properties. Distinguishing preload relaxation without nut rotation from rotational self-loosening is essential for revealing multi-bolt flange degradation mechanisms. This paper presents a systematic review of physics-driven constitutive modeling and degradation characterization of bolted flange connections. A unified classification framework for joint interface models is established, covering static friction models; velocity-dependent dynamic friction models; hysteresis stick–slip models, represented by the four-parameter Iwan model and Valanis endochronic model; and reduced-order equivalent joint models. The inherent differences between the Dahl model and LuGre model regarding the Stribeck velocity–friction characteristics are clarified. The representative models are comprehensively evaluated from the perspectives of physical interpretability, hysteresis reproduction accuracy, preload–degradation correlation and engineering applicability. A further comparative analysis is conducted of parameter identification bottlenecks of the Iwan, LuGre and Valanis models, focusing on multi-solution risk, anti-noise robustness and cross-working-condition transferability. Compared with single-bolt lap specimens, multi-bolt annular flanges exhibit prominent inter-bolt elastic interaction, circumferential contact pressure non-uniformity and local-to-global chain-reaction degradation behaviors. The common experimental test-beds and sensing techniques for joint degradation monitoring are summarized, and the measurement limitations, including sensor drift, synchronization error and installation constraints, and their influences on model parameter identification, are discussed. The existing machine-learning, digital-twin and physics-informed modeling applications for bolted joints are briefly outlined. Finally, this review summarizes the existing research consensus, unresolved contradictions and open research challenges. Special attention is paid to the limitations of existing time-variant Iwan-type models for multi-bolt flange degradation. Potential future research directions include multi-channel synchronous sensing matching time-varying constitutive models, quantification of inter-bolt load redistribution, and robust identification strategies under noisy experimental data. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Robust Adaptive Predictive Control for Hook-Based Aerial Transportation Between Moving Platforms

Abstract: This letter presents a novel model predictive control (MPC) approach for autonomous pick-and-place between moving platforms with a hook-equipped aerial manipulator. First, for accurate and rapid modeling of the complex dynamics, a digital twin model of the quadcopter equipped with a hook-based gripper, implemented in MuJoCo, is constructed and used as the predictive model for the MPC. To handle uncertainties of the predictive model (e.g. due to aerodynamics and uncertain payloads), a robust adaptive MPC approach is proposed. By systematic integration of zero-order robust optimization (zoRO) based uncertainty propagation and an extended Kalman filter (EKF) for parameter estimation, the MPC algorithm ensures robust constraint satisfaction, high performance, and computational efficiency. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated in complex simulated scenarios and in real-world flight experiments. © 2016 IEEE.

Title: Joint Impact of Missing Samples and Finite ADC Resolution on Parameter Estimation from Sensor Signals
Affiliations: Missouri University of Science, Technology, Department of Electrical, Computer Engineering, Rolla, 65409, MO, United States
Authors with affiliations: Omanda Bouraima M., Missouri University of Science, Technology, Department of Electrical, Computer Engineering, Rolla, 65409, MO, United States; Zawodniok M., Missouri University of Science, Technology, Department of Electrical, Computer Engineering, Rolla, 65409, MO, United States
Abstract: Reliable sensor data are critical for digital-twin accuracy, but practical measurements often suffer from missing samples and finite analog-to-digital converter (ADC) resolution. This letter investigates their combined impact on joint phase (φ) and damped-frequency (ωd) estimation in damped oscillatory signals. We derive closed-form Cramér-Rao lower bounds (CRLB) using an additive uniform-noise approximation for finite-bit ADC quantization and a missing completely at random missing-data model, incorporating imputation uncertainty. Monte Carlo simulations and real beam-vibration experiments consistently highlight the tradeoff between ADC resolution and data availability, while multiple recovery methods are compared against the CRLB benchmarks. The analysis provides practical guidance for selecting sensor resolution and maintaining sufficient data quality for reliable parameter estimation.  © 2017 IEEE.

Title: Artificial Intelligence for Lithium-Ion Batteries: Closed-Loop Discovery, State Prediction, and Trustworthy Management

Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming lithium-ion battery (LIB) research by linking heterogeneous data, predictive modeling, mechanistic interpretation, and experimental validation within a closed-loop paradigm. AI does not uniquely enable nonlinear representation; rather, it complements electrochemical, statistical, and control models by learning high-dimensional relationships among composition, structure, processing, interfacial chemistry, operating history, and performance. This review critically examines three connected domains: AI-assisted materials discovery, battery state prediction, and trustworthy intelligent management. To distinguish this contribution from recent topic-specific surveys, we organize methods along four complementary axes—model architecture, learning strategy, physics integration, and deployment strategy—and compare landmark studies using quantitative evidence such as independent cell count, validation design, reported error, experimental budget, and closed-loop acceleration. Materials applications include cathodes, anodes, liquid and solid electrolytes, and electrode-electrolyte interphases; operational applications include state of charge, state of health, remaining useful life, degradation diagnosis, safety warning, and digital twin-enabled management. The critical synthesis identifies data leakage, inconsistent metadata, domain shift, uncalibrated uncertainty, black-box reasoning, computational constraints, and limited external validation as recurring barriers. Future progress will depend less on model complexity alone than on FAIR data, cell-independent evaluation, physics-informed learning, uncertainty-aware decisions, autonomous experimentation, human oversight, and deployment-aware design. These elements define an evidence chain for moving LIB AI from proof-of-concept prediction toward reproducible, closed-loop, and trustworthy battery innovation. © 2026 by the authors.

Authors: Li Y.; Chen Y.
Title: From track to stability: A review of vibration behavior, structural reliability, and dynamic performance in railway vehicles
Affiliations: Zhan Tianyou College, Dalian Jiaotong University, Dalian, 116028, China
Authors with affiliations: Li Y., Zhan Tianyou College, Dalian Jiaotong University, Dalian, 116028, China; Chen Y., Zhan Tianyou College, Dalian Jiaotong University, Dalian, 116028, China
Abstract: Railway vehicles operate under continuously changing wheel-rail contact, track geometry, loading, speed, and environmental conditions, making vibration behavior a direct driver of ride comfort, running safety, structural fatigue, and maintenance demand. Existing studies often examine vehicle vibration, structural reliability, and dynamic performance separately, which can obscure the causal path from track excitation to vehicle response, fatigue damage, performance degradation, and maintenance action. This review synthesizes these topics within an integrated life-cycle framework. It first examines major vibration excitation mechanisms, including track irregularities, wheel and rail defects, turnouts, transition zones, traction and braking forces, and aerodynamic disturbances. It then reviews modeling and analysis methods, including multibody dynamics, finite element analysis, vehicle–track coupled models, co-simulation, monitoring-based validation, and uncertainty analysis, with emphasis on their ability to connect dynamic loads with stress histories and fatigue reliability. Structural reliability is discussed as the mechanism by which vibration-induced loads become service risk, while dynamic performance is evaluated through ride comfort, running safety, hunting stability, vibration control, and multi-objective optimization. Furthermore, key limitations such as simplified contact assumptions, insufficient full-scale validation, weak coupling between monitoring data and fatigue models, limited interpretability of AI diagnosis and immature digital-twin implementation are identified in this review. Finally, future directions are proposed toward physics-informed modeling, uncertainty-aware reliability assessment, intelligent monitoring, adaptive vibration control and reliability-centered maintenance for safer, more durable, and sustainable railway vehicles.
