Abstract: The integration of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) with Digital Twin (DT) frameworks offers a transformative pathway for modern bridge management, enabling satellite-data selection of structures to engage decision-making across the asset life cycle. This approach supports proactive Structural Health Monitoring (SHM), prioritization of predictive maintenance (PM) over repair and rehabilitation interventions, and enhanced informed planning. Therefore, promising case studies demonstrating the practicability of fusing satellite-derived displacement data with Building Information Modelling (BIM), based digital representations, taking into consideration several barriers, such as semantic interoperability, uncertainty quantification, real-time data assimilation, and institutional integration into Bridge Management Systems (BMS). This work outlines a systematic framework for implementing InSAR-enhanced digital twins according to a literature review, emphasizing their role in integration with BIM, lifecycle administration, and predictive assurance. By synthesizing recent advances and identifying key research gaps, this contribution aligns with ongoing international efforts to standardize and operationalize digital twin adoption for sustainable, resilient, and optimized bridge infrastructure management. © 2026 The Author(s)

Authors: Balijepalli P.R.B.; Soykan B.; Hasti V.R.
Title: Traffic and weather driven hybrid digital twin for bridge monitoring
Source title: Moving Toward Smart, Resilient and Sustainable Bridges
Affiliations: University of Central Florida, Orlando, FL, United States
Authors with affiliations: Balijepalli P.R.B., University of Central Florida, Orlando, FL, United States; Soykan B., University of Central Florida, Orlando, FL, United States; Hasti V.R., University of Central Florida, Orlando, FL, United States
Abstract: A hybrid digital twin framework is presented for bridge condition monitoring using existing traffic cameras and weather APIs, reducing reliance on dedicated sensor installations. The approach is demonstrated on the Peace Bridge (99 years in service) under high traffic demand and harsh winter exposure. The framework fuses three near-real-time streams: YOLOv8 computer vision from a bridge-deck camera estimates vehicle counts, traffic density, and load proxies; a Lighthill–Whitham–Richards (LWR) model propagates density ρ (x,t) and detects deceleration-driven shockwaves linked to repetitive loading and fatigue accumulation; and weather APIs provide deterioration drivers including temperature cycling, freeze-thaw activity, precipitation-related corrosion potential, and wind effects. Monte Carlo simulation quantifies uncertainty across traffic-environment scenarios, while Random Forest models map fused features to fatigue indicators and maintenance classification. The framework demonstrates utilizing existing infrastructure for cost-effective predictive maintenance of aging, high-traffic bridges in harsh climates. © 2026 The Author(s)

Title: Orthopedic Mechanophenotype: A Structured Narrative Review of Multiscale Biomechanics, Mechanotransduction, and Clinical Decision-Making
Affiliations: The First School of Clinical Medicine, Yunnan University of Chinese Medicine, Kunming, China; The First People's Hospital of Yunnan Province, Kunming, China
Authors with affiliations: Lan Z., The First School of Clinical Medicine, Yunnan University of Chinese Medicine, Kunming, China; Mu Z., The First School of Clinical Medicine, Yunnan University of Chinese Medicine, Kunming, China; Li H., The First School of Clinical Medicine, Yunnan University of Chinese Medicine, Kunming, China, The First People's Hospital of Yunnan Province, Kunming, China
Abstract: Orthopedic disorders are still classified mainly by anatomy or end-stage morphology, yet osteoporosis, osteoarthritis, fracture nonunion, spinal degeneration, and bone-implant interface failure share a common mechanobiological logic: external load is filtered by hierarchical tissue architecture, converted into cell-scale signals, and integrated with inflammation, metabolism, and repair capacity to determine whether adaptation or failure occurs. This structured narrative review synthesizes recent evidence on multiscale biomechanics, finite element analysis (FEA), mechanotransduction biology, tissue engineering, and emerging digital-twin approaches. Rather than introducing a separate disease entity, we define the orthopedic mechanophenotype as a clinically oriented integrative framework that describes the disease-relevant state generated by three interacting axes: load exposure, tissue susceptibility, and biological adaptability. We summarize how this three-axis state differs across bone, articular cartilage and the osteochondral unit, the intervertebral disc, fracture repair, and bone-implant interfaces. Particular emphasis is placed on evidence hierarchy, model assumptions, and persistent uncertainties, including timescale mismatch, idealized boundary conditions, incomplete cross-scale validation, and overinterpretation of cell-level causality from organ-level surrogates. We further illustrate how mechanophenotyping can be integrated with existing clinical pathways for osteoarthritis load redistribution, fracture fixation and rehabilitation, and spinal or implant-related planning. The central argument is that future progress will depend less on accumulating isolated mechanical variables and more on validated cross-scale markers that connect real-world loading, patient-specific structure, and stage-dependent biology to actionable orthopedic decisions. © 2026 The Author(s). Abstract: This work develops an active learning framework to intelligently enrich data-driven reduced-order models (ROMs) of parametric dynamical systems, which can serve as the foundation of virtual assets in a digital twin. Data-driven ROMs are explainable, computationally efficient scientific machine learning models that aim to preserve the underlying physics of complex dynamical simulations. Since the quality of data-driven ROMs is sensitive to the quality of the limited training data, we seek to identify training parameters for which using the associated training data results in the best possible parametric ROM. Our approach uses the operator inference methodology, a regression-based strategy which can be tailored to particular parametric structure for a large class of problems. We establish a probabilistic version of parametric operator inference, casting the learning problem as a Bayesian linear regression. Prediction uncertainties stemming from the resulting probabilistic ROM solutions are used to design a sequential adaptive sampling scheme to select new training parameter vectors that promote ROM stability and accuracy globally in the parameter domain. We conduct numerical experiments for several nonlinear parametric systems of partial differential equations and compare the results to ROMs trained on random parameter samples. The results demonstrate that the proposed adaptive sampling strategy consistently yields more stable and accurate ROMs than random sampling does under the same computational budget. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Science+Business Media, LLC, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Abstract: Rapid advances in nanomaterials, wearable biosensors, multimodal acquisition, and artificial intelligence have enabled increasingly integrated health-monitoring systems, yet their progression toward health digital twins remains unclear. We conducted a protocol-driven scoping review of original studies combining nano-enabled multianalyte or multimodal sensing, AI-supported analysis, and health applications. PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and IEEE Xplore were searched using a publication cutoff of 10 July 2026; platform execution was completed on 13 July 2026. Two reviewers independently screened 528 unique records and assessed 20 full-text reports. A 79-item charting form was jointly verified for 12 included studies. Nine studies reported reference-method or matrix-relevant analytical validation, nine included human-sample or on-body evidence, and six acquired longitudinal or continuous data. Under the author-proposed, corpus-specific functional classification, six systems were L0, five L1, and one L2; none of the 12 met the L3 or L4 functional criteria. No included study combined dynamic individual-state assimilation with prospective prediction or simulation, and none reported external-site validation or formal predictive uncertainty quantification. Because eligibility required nano-enablement, multiple analytes or channels, AI integration, and selected clinical domains, these findings do not estimate the prevalence or maturity of health digital twins in the wider literature. Progress requires longitudinal multimodal data, validated state updating, external generalization, confidence-aware AI, and prospective evaluation of governed feedback. © 2026 by the authors.

Abstract: Advances in computing and machine learning (ML) methods have led to a rapid rise in artificial intelligence (AI) research and applications in many fields. AI research benefitted from advances in computation hardware, collection and distribution of large data sets, and proliferation of software techniques. AI techniques include ML for provable results, deep learning for data exploration, reinforcement learning for control, and active learning for adaptive systems. Likewise, AI algorithms can handle large amounts of data, construct unknown representations, and provide a direct link between data and classification for decision making. These unmatched capabilities have been seen as a path to solving hard engineering problems, including that of structural health monitoring (SHM). SHM consists of automating the condition assessment task of civil, health, mechanical, and aerospace systems using measurements obtained from temporary or permanently installed sensors. Often, the systems of interest are geometrically large and/or technically complex, which complicates the development and application of physics-based methods. It follows that AI is seen as a key potential contributor enabling SHM in field applications for data-driven analysis. As with many research endeavors, many concepts using AI for SHM have been explored in the literature. Nevertheless, very few AI methods have been deployed in the context of SHM, which may be due to the lack of available data supporting their capabilities, limited integrated AI-SHM systems capable of providing results to users and operators with decision-making capabilities, or certification of AI methods for safety-critical applications. The objective of this Roadmap publication is to discuss the integration of AI at the system level enabling SHM, including associated challenges and opportunities such as those found in common metrics of concern (e.g. transparency, interpretability, explainability, security, certifiability, etc), with a particular focus on providing a path to research and development efforts that could yield impactful field applications. The overview of available methods and directions will provide the readers with applicability of AI for certain SHM designs (software), availability of common data sets for further AI comparisons (data), and lessons learned in implementation (hardware). © 2026 The Author(s). Title: Digital twins and physics-informed machine learning for safe agro-industrial waste valorization: Bioactive recovery, food-grade standardization, and regulatory readiness
Source title: Trends in Food Science and Technology
Affiliations: Bioprocessing Laboratory, Centre for Technology Alternatives for Rural Areas, Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Powai, Mumbai, 400076, India
Authors with affiliations: Sahu C.K., Bioprocessing Laboratory, Centre for Technology Alternatives for Rural Areas, Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Powai, Mumbai, 400076, India; Arora A., Bioprocessing Laboratory, Centre for Technology Alternatives for Rural Areas, Indian Institute of Technology Bombay, Powai, Mumbai, 400076, India
Abstract: Background: Agro-industrial residues are promising sources of phenolics, pigments, polysaccharides, proteins, and other functional ingredients, but food-grade valorization remains constrained by feedstock heterogeneity, sensor uncertainty, empirical scale-up, solvent and energy burdens, and contaminant co-extraction. Scope and approach: This review critically evaluates digital twins and physics-informed machine learning (PIML) as a safety-bounded framework for residue valorization. It examines process analytical technology, laboratory assays, soft sensors, unit-operation models, model predictive control, techno-economic assessment, life-cycle assessment, and regulatory audit trails. Particular emphasis is placed on coupling target-bioactive recovery with the transport and concentration of pesticides, mycotoxins, metals, residual solvents, and process impurities. Key findings and conclusions: PIML can embed transport, reaction, rheological, and degradation constraints into learning architectures, thereby improving extrapolation from sparse and drifting food-process datasets. Digital twins can extend these models into synchronized cyber-physical systems that optimize recovery while enforcing calibrated uncertainty, contaminant boundaries, explainability, traceability, and dossier-ready comparability for EFSA Novel Food, FDA GRAS, Codex, and related pathways. Persistent barriers include sensor fouling, calibration drift, missing benchmark datasets, computational latency, interoperability gaps, and limited toxicological validation. A staged maturity roadmap is proposed, from data shadows to qualified autonomous twins. An updated search through 6 June 2026 identified adjacent reviews, but no publicly indexed source jointly formalized PIML-constrained unit-operation twins, coupled bioactive-hazard states, uncertainty-bounded release invariants, and regulatory comparability. However, DT/PIML should be implemented as staged, risk-based decision-support systems, not universal replacements for conventional optimization, because scale-transfer uncertainty, rare-event coverage, and computational burden determine whether industrial use is justified. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Assessment of Readiness of Urban Logistics Operators for Digital Twin Technologies

Authors with affiliations: Sakhbieva A.I., Kazan (Volga) Federal University, Kazan, Russian Federation; Bulatova E.I., Kazan (Volga) Federal University, Kazan, Russian Federation; Nikonova T.V., Kazan (Volga) Federal University, Kazan, Russian Federation; Syurkova S.M., Kazan National Research Technical University Named After A.N. Tupolev-KAI, Kazan, Russian Federation
Abstract: In the conditions of increasing complexity and uncertainty in urban logistics, digital twin technologies are considered a promising tool for improving the efficiency of transport and logistics systems. Despite the active development of digital twins in scientific research and engineering practice, empirical evidence on the readiness of urban logistics operators to adopt these technologies remains limited. The aim of this study is to assess the readiness of urban logistics operators to implement digital twin technologies based on a survey of managerial staff from logistics and courier companies. The empirical basis of the study is formed from a survey of 64 middle- and senior-level managers operating in seven major Russian cities. The study investigates the level of awareness of digital twin technologies, the digital and organizational readiness of companies, the expected operational and economic effects, as well as the main barriers to implementation. The results show that, despite a moderate level of managerial awareness, the expected benefits of digital twin adoption are assessed significantly higher than the current level of readiness and availability of internal competencies. Comparative and regression analyses confirm that the intention to launch pilot digital twin projects is primarily driven by the expected benefits, the level of awareness, and data readiness. The practical significance of the study lies in the potential use of the results for self-assessment of the digital maturity of logistics companies and for substantiating a phased approach to the implementation of digital twin technologies in urban logistics. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Title: Beyond the Ranking Paradox: A Context-Weighted Liveability Index for Assessing Mediterranean Smart Cities—A Proof-of-Concept GIS-Based Comparison of Bologna and Athens
Affiliations: Department of Civil, Architectural and Environmental Engineering (DICEA), University of Padua, Padova, 35131, Italy
Authors with affiliations: Bove A., Department of Civil, Architectural and Environmental Engineering (DICEA), University of Padua, Padova, 35131, Italy; Ghiraldelli M., Department of Civil, Architectural and Environmental Engineering (DICEA), University of Padua, Padova, 35131, Italy
Abstract: Conventional international rankings assess urban efficiency via context-blind metrics, a design that the literature suggests may structurally disadvantage Mediterranean centres and obscure the sustainable policy pathways mandated by the Sustainable Development Goals, most notably the governance of urban transitions under SDG 11. This paper proposes the Context-Weighted Liveability Index (CWLI), which introduces context-sensitive weights into the aggregation of standard smart city KPIs, bridging the global comparability of IMD-style indices with the Mediterranean-specific assessment logic of the ASCIMER framework. Weights derive from five geographic coefficients—climate, culture, economy, historical density, and demography—through a transparent weighted additive formulation with an explicit sensitivity matrix, whose robustness is verified through Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis over 5000 perturbed configurations spanning parameters, coefficients, measurements and benchmarks. Coefficients and KPIs are computed from open spatial data through a replicable GIS protocol (QGIS; OpenStreetMap, Copernicus land cover and land surface temperature, and ISTAT/ELSTAT census data at sub-municipal scale). Applied comparatively to Bologna and Athens, the framework shows that contextual weighting concentrates over 60% of the total weight on climate-sensitive indicators and yields, through the decomposition of contributions, a policy diagnosis that differs from the one suggested by reading an overall smart city rank in isolation: Athens’ largest contribution is digital and its liveability deficit territorial—a profile with direct consequences for sustainable urban transition and talent attraction. Implications for SDG 11 monitoring, equitable access to urban green space, and digital twin integration are discussed. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Strategic Management of Airport Readiness for Digital-Twin-Enabled Smart-Energy Systems: A Reliability-Aware Bayesian Decision Framework
Affiliations: Atlas University, Department of Management Information Systems, Istanbul, 34403, Turkey; Department of Property Protection and Security, Istanbul Bilgi University, Istanbul, 34060, Turkey
Authors with affiliations: Mizrak F., Atlas University, Department of Management Information Systems, Istanbul, 34403, Turkey; Elbir U., Department of Property Protection and Security, Istanbul Bilgi University, Istanbul, 34060, Turkey
Abstract: Airports face growing pressure to decarbonize energy-intensive infrastructure while integrating digital twins, artificial intelligence, real-time monitoring, electrification, renewable-energy systems, and resilient operational controls. This study develops a reliability-aware Bayesian framework for assessing readiness for digital-twin-enabled smart-energy systems across 20 major international airports. The preferred latent model uses 15 airport-level capability indicators organized into four theory-defined domains: smart-energy infrastructure, digital twins and intelligent systems, managerial and organizational readiness, and governance and resilience. A sixteenth indicator, evidence transparency, is retained separately as an auxiliary reporting-quality measure. Eight additional variables describe the airport scale and country- or economy-level enabling environment. Evidence was compiled from official airport reports, sustainability disclosures, regulatory records, project documents, and international datasets, with explicit distinctions between operational systems, pilots, planned investments, and group-level claims. Observation-level reliability incorporates source quality, verification, temporal relevance, consistency, and completeness, while missing observations contribute no direct likelihood to the Bayesian measurement model. The preferred PyMC/NUTS specification produced stable posterior estimates with no divergent transitions, a maximum overall readiness R-hat of 1.003, and acceptable posterior predictive performance (RMSE = 0.094; MAE = 0.057). Singapore Changi, Hong Kong, Amsterdam Schiphol, and Copenhagen formed the highest-readiness group. Sensitivity analyses showed that the broad ordering was robust to alternative reliability assumptions, variance-floor choices, prior specifications, and high-information restrictions, although stronger informative-missingness assumptions affected several evidence-sparse airports. A complementary rule-based threshold screen identified capability shortfalls and evidence gaps without interpreting them as causal necessary conditions. The framework provides an uncertainty-aware basis for benchmarking, investment sequencing, procurement, and integrated digital and energy transition planning. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Research Gaps in AI-Supported Disassembly Sequence Planning in Remanufacturing

Abstract: Artificial intelligence has become increasingly important in research on Disassembly Sequence Planning (DSP). AI-based methods can now solve more complex problems and consider several economic, environmental and operational objectives. However, most studies still focus on optimizing the disassembly process after the recovery strategy and target components have already been selected. This study reviews AI-supported disassembly planning in remanufacturing and identifies the main research gaps and future research directions. The review combines bibliometric mapping of 241 publications with a qualitative analysis of 35 selected studies. Of these studies, 23 directly address DSP, seven concern related disassembly problems, and five focus on remanufacturing planning or scheduling outside DSP. The results show progress in metaheuristic optimization, reinforcement learning, digital twins, knowledge graphs, computer vision, large language models and robotic planning. At the same time, the analysis identified several recurring limitations that can be grouped into three broader dimensions: product-state knowledge and adaptability, validation and transferability, and decision scope and strategic-operational integration. The reviewed studies show that uncertainty, adaptive planning, digital twins and multi-objective optimization have already received considerable attention, but their application remains limited by predefined product representations, case-specific validation and weak integration between product-level recovery assessment and operational disassembly planning. The findings suggest that future research should complement further algorithmic development with more integrated, adaptive and knowledge-supported decision-support approaches that connect recovery assessment with the planning of the required disassembly process. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Counterfactual Deadline-Aware Edge Scheduling for Rehabilitation-Critical Motion Streams in Autonomous Orthopedic IoT Networks

Abstract: Autonomous orthopedic Internet-of-Things (IoT) systems require resource control mechanisms that can preserve time-critical rehabilitation monitoring despite simultaneous changes in motion intensity, wireless quality, queue occupancy, edge load, and energy availability. Conventional heuristic, machine learning, and deep reinforcement learning schedulers adapt to observed correlations but do not explicitly identify the mechanisms causing quality of service (QoS) degradation or estimate the effects of alternative interventions in the current operating state. This study proposes Counterfactual Deadline-Aware Edge Scheduling (CDAES), an uncertainty-aware causal resource control framework for rehabilitation-critical motion streams. CDAES constructs a dynamic structural causal model of motion, traffic, wireless, resource, energy, and QoS variables; detects impending service violations; evaluates individual and joint interventions through abduction-action-prediction; rejects uncertain or infeasible actions; and selects a Pareto-feasible policy under class-specific deadline, reliability, energy, and continuity constraints. The framework was implemented on a hardware-in-the-loop orthopedic edge-IoT platform with wearable inertial sensors, a body-area gateway, edge intelligence, controlled network and resource disturbances, and asynchronous digital twin support. Under high-load dynamic wireless conditions, CDAES achieved median, p95, and p99 latencies of 22, 58, and 95 ms, respectively, with 96.1% deadline satisfaction, 97.8% monitoring continuity, and 3.21 kB communication costs per valid event. Across 720 executed interventions, counterfactual predictions achieved R2 = 0.83, while uncertainty correlated with observed prediction error at p = 0.78. These results demonstrate that causal, counterfactual, and uncertainty-aware edge control can improve the QoS, resilience, and resource efficiency of autonomous rehabilitation IoT systems. © 2014 IEEE.

Title: Immersive Systems for Archaeological Parks and Urban-Scale Heritage: A Systematic Review of Augmented and Virtual Reality Across Ancient Cities, Historic Districts, and Participatory Urban Planning

Abstract: Immersive technologies support heritage interpretation and management, yet research remains divided between cultural and archaeological heritage and urban planning. This systematic review, reported according to PRISMA 2020, aimed to examine the design, application, and evaluation of augmented, virtual, and mixed reality systems in archaeological parks, historic districts, and urban-planning contexts. Peer-reviewed English-language journal articles and full conference papers published from 2010 to 15 July 2026 were eligible; museum-only, artifact-only, non-immersive, and methodologically insufficient reports were excluded. Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and SpringerLink were searched through 15 July 2026. A five-domain, study-type-adapted rubric was used for critical appraisal, and findings were synthesized narratively by spatial scale, delivery mode, technology pipeline, and evaluation. Of 10,790 records, 21 studies were included: 17 direct applications, three enabling methods, and one foundational survey. Twelve reported user or stakeholder evaluations, but only ten reported numerical sample sizes, precluding calculation of a pooled participant total. Evidence was heterogeneous, predominantly descriptive, and rarely longitudinal. The original screening, data extraction, and critical appraisal were performed by a single reviewer. Following peer review, all 21 included reports and the key coding and appraisal variables underwent retrospective independent verification and reconciliation. No supplementary hand-searching or citation searching was conducted. The urban dimension of ancient cities remains underexplored, while communication of uncertainty in city-scale reconstructions remains unresolved. The review proposes a cross-domain taxonomy, core evaluation outcomes, and an integrated research agenda. No external funding was received. The review was not registered, and no formal protocol was prepared. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Multi-Level Multi-Sensor Data Fusion in Bathymetric Modeling: A Systematic Review
Affiliations: Department of Imagery Intelligence, Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geodesy, Military University of Technology, Warsaw, 00-908, Poland
Authors with affiliations: Sybilski H., Department of Imagery Intelligence, Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geodesy, Military University of Technology, Warsaw, 00-908, Poland; Fryśkowska-Skibniewska A., Department of Imagery Intelligence, Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geodesy, Military University of Technology, Warsaw, 00-908, Poland; Jaczewska P., Department of Imagery Intelligence, Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geodesy, Military University of Technology, Warsaw, 00-908, Poland
Abstract: Accurate subaqueous morphological modelling is crucial for sustainable aquatic ecosystem management, yet single-sensor hydrographic surveys remain constrained by environmental limitations. Through a systematic review, this study aims to evaluate the efficacy of multi-level, multi-sensor data fusion approaches (acoustic, optical, LiDAR, and satellite) in bathymetric modelling. A search of five electronic databases (Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink) up to 14 August 2026 was conducted to identify relevant peer-reviewed studies. From 685 initial records, 62 studies were included for systematic synthesis. The eligible studies’ methodological quality was assessed via a customized six-domain risk-of-bias framework. The results indicated significant improvements in spatial coverage and accuracy at complex land–water transition zones compared to single-source baselines, reducing depth retrieval errors by 18% to over 50% and achieving sub-decimeter accuracies (RMSE < 0.10 m). Feature-level Geospatial Artificial Intelligence (GeoAI) further enhanced nonlinear environmental modelling and benthic habitat classification (accuracies > 98%). This review identified that multisensor fusion effectively enhances bathymetric accuracy, providing a critical foundation for sustainable water-resource management. While standardized uncertainty quantification remains an operational bottleneck, future interventions integrating predictive 4D Digital Twins show immense promise for long-term ecological monitoring, flood-risk mitigation, and climate-resilient infrastructure planning. © 2026 by the authors.

Title: Uncertainty-aware maintenance scheduling in water distribution networks via ensemble neural forecasting and explainable confidence indexing

Abstract: Maintenance scheduling in water distribution networks (WDNs) needs accurate demand forecasts. However, climate variability makes point predictions insufficient. Existing Digital Twin (DT) frameworks use deterministic forecasts, leading to over-scheduling and Service Level Agreement (SLA) violations during volatile weather. Bayesian uncertainty methods are rigorous but require 340 ms per inference, making them too slow for real-time scheduling on standard utility hardware. We propose CAUCCES, coupling an adaptive ensemble (LSTM, Prophet, LightGBM, XGBoost) with a novel Explainable Confidence Index (ECI). ECI is a closed-form uncertainty measure based on ensemble entropy and variance. It directly connects the forecasting module to a constraint-based scheduler. When confidence drops, non-critical tasks are deferred, turning forecast uncertainty into actionable decisions. Validated across 12 Spanish municipalities over 18 months, ECI-driven scheduling reduces SLA violations from 9.3% to 1.5% with only 3.1% extra operational cost. The ensemble achieves 14.12% MAPE, outperforming DeepAR (16.50%) and Temporal Fusion Transformer (16.92%) Furthermore, it achieves a 28 speedup (12 ms vs. 340 ms) compared to a Bayesian LSTM baseline. Finally, multi-regional testing shows 12–26% performance degradation across different climatic zones, showing that local recalibration is necessary. These results suggest that entropy-based uncertainty quantification can serve as a practical bridge between forecasting and scheduling for resource-constrained utilities, although broader validation across climates and operating conditions is still needed. © The Author(s) 2026.

Title: A novel Approach to Risk Management for University Research Projects

Abstract: Large-scale infrastructure projects are often characterized by a high degree of innovation but are also accompanied by uncertainties and risks. In university research projects, the complexity is even higher because, in addition to unknown factors, like unclear paths forward, they come with adaptive targets. These lead to higher uncertainties, and it is crucial to adhere to the magic triangle of project management to continuously monitor and ensure the achievement of the project goals. Additionally, in research, a dead-end does not inevitably lead to the failure of the project, but mostly it leads to new opportunities. This paper explores the relationship between project goals and risk management of university projects to create a tailored project plan. First, the challenges and needs were mapped out through a survey of ten project leaders at our university. This survey helped us understand the problems and led to a new approach for university projects. Second, the new approach including adjusted risk management and methodology is developed. Third, the results were combined with a project plan using a probabilistic methodology to modify the approach through predictive evaluations. This includes integrated cost, time, and risk analysis. The probabilistic results are based on a Monte Carlo simulation. In the paper differences and similarities between the management of large-scale infrastructure projects and research projects are highlighted. Therefore, a process for creating an exemplary, holistic project plan using a digital twin, which helps to optimize the management strategy for research is presented. Furthermore, the project plan is tailored to the needs of applied research, so that the results of the research can be useful for the industry. © 2024, Korea Institute of Construction Engineering and Management. Abstract: This work presents a data-driven framework for reconstructing thermochemical states in MILD combustion by coupling Sparse Sensing (SpS) with a Flamelet-Generated Manifold (FGM) formulation to reconstruct species fields from a limited number of temperature measurements. A non-adiabatic FGM database is first generated from counterflow flamelets and used to describe the thermochemical state through a reduced set of control variables. These variables are then reconstructed by a SpS model based on Proper Orthogonal Decomposition and Bayesian inference, using a predetermined sensor layout consistent with the reference experimental burner. The coupled framework is assessed on a lab-scale cyclonic MILD combustor. Results show accurate reconstruction of the main control variables and good prediction of major species, with R2 values above 0.94 for CH4, CO2, H2O, and O2, while intermediate and minor species exhibit larger deviations but remain correctly captured in terms of spatial trends and order of magnitude. Finally, the analysis of uncertainty propagation shows that species uncertainty is mainly governed by mixture fraction, while the contribution of the variance of the progress variable is negligible. Novelty and significance statement: Reduced-order models (ROMs) for turbulent combustion describe complex reactive flows by exploiting latent structure (Parente and Sutherland, 2013). Previous work (Procacci et al., 2023; Rosati et al., 2026) reduces the state by selecting key species to recover information for analysis, but the choice of target variables and the size of the state can degrade reconstruction accuracy and runtime. This work introduces, to the authors’ knowledge, the first application in a MILD cyclonic burner of an integrated framework coupling Sparse Sensing (Manohar et al., 2018) with Flamelet Generated Manifolds (FGM) (Van Oijen and De Goey, 2000) to reconstruct thermochemical states from a limited set of control variables. By combining physics-based tabulated chemistry with data-driven sparse reconstruction, the proposed SpS-FGM approach reduces sensing demand and decouples reconstruction performance from full-state dimensionality. The framework is compatible with established diagnostic workflows and can be extended to other reduction or data assimilation strategies, supporting the development of reliable, low-cost digital twins or soft-sensing tools for applications focused on low-emission combustion systems. © 2026 The Authors.

Title: Hybrid Intelligence for Fouling Prediction and Adaptive Clean-in-Place Optimization in Food Processing Heat Exchangers: A Systematic Review

Abstract: Fouling remains one of the principal challenges limiting the thermal efficiency, hygienic performance, and sustainability of food processing heat exchangers. The accumulation of protein, mineral, biofilm, and particulate deposits increases thermal resistance, energy consumption, production losses, and the frequency of cleaning-in-place (CIP) operations, thereby affecting process economics and food safety. This systematic review critically evaluates advances in hybrid intelligence for fouling prediction and adaptive CIP optimization in plate and tubular heat exchangers used in dairy, beverage, and liquid food processing. A structured literature review of publications from 2000 to 2026 was conducted using Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar. Unlike previous reviews that address these topics separately, this review integrates fouling mechanisms, predictive modeling, intelligent sensing, explainable artificial intelligence (AI), adaptive CIP, and digital twins within a unified engineering framework for food processing. The evidence indicates that hybrid intelligence approaches outperform purely mechanistic or data-driven models by improving predictive accuracy, robustness under variable operating conditions, physical consistency, and model interpretability. AI-enabled condition-based CIP strategies also demonstrate considerable potential to reduce water, chemical, and energy consumption while minimizing production downtime without compromising hygienic performance. However, industrial implementation remains constrained by limited food-specific datasets, insufficient large-scale validation, uncertainty quantification, model explainability, and integration with hazard analysis and critical control point–based food safety systems. Future research should prioritize physics-informed, food-specific hybrid intelligence frameworks integrating real-time sensing, digital twins, adaptive CIP control, and explainable decision support to enable sustainable, resilient, and intelligent food manufacturing systems. © 2026 Institute of Food Technologists.

Title: Fuel surrogate temperature prediction for microreactor using heat pipe under transient conditions
Affiliations: Department of Nuclear Engineering, Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology (UNIST), 50 UNIST-gil, Ulju-gun, Ulsan, 44919, South Korea
Authors with affiliations: Jin I.J., Department of Nuclear Engineering, Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology (UNIST), 50 UNIST-gil, Ulju-gun, Ulsan, 44919, South Korea; Bang I.C., Department of Nuclear Engineering, Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology (UNIST), 50 UNIST-gil, Ulju-gun, Ulsan, 44919, South Korea
Abstract: Remote operation and digital twin implementation for heat pipe cooled reactor systems require simplified and reliable thermal state estimation methods. In applications, fuel temperature should be inferred using a limited set of accessible measurements, while maintaining sufficient performance under transient operating conditions. In this study, a fuel surrogate temperature prediction method was developed using temperature measurements obtained from the adiabatic and condenser sections of a heat pipe with heat exchanger temperature. Deep learning architectures were applied to represent transient thermal behavior. An integrated LSTM–Transformer architecture was adopted to reflect short term temporal continuity and long term temporal dependency in the measured temperature signals. Model performance was evaluated using both separate and sequential transient datasets. The integrated LSTM–Transformer model achieved a mean absolute error of 1.68 K and a mean absolute percentage error of 0.19% for separate transient conditions. For sequential transient conditions, which included compounded and previously unseen transients, the mean absolute error and mean absolute percentage error increased to 4.74 K and 0.55%, respectively, while maintaining a coefficient of determination above 0.99. Model behavior was examined using attention weight analysis and SHAP-based feature attribution, confirming that interpretable temperature contributions were captured. Prediction uncertainty was quantified using Monte Carlo Dropout, with 95% confidence intervals remaining within 5–7 K for most operating conditions. The proposed approach provides a basis for fuel surrogate temperature monitoring and thermal assessment in heat pipe cooled microreactor systems, particularly for remote operation and digital twin applications where model complexity and instrumentation availability are constrained. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Digital Twin for Context Awareness, Security, and Resilience in Vehicular Networks for 5G and Beyond: A Comprehensive Survey
Source title: IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society
Affiliations: Université Laval, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Québec City, G1V 0A6, QC, Canada; University of Wolverhampton, School of Mathematics and Computer Science, Wolverhampton, WV1 1LY, United Kingdom
Authors with affiliations: Karim M., Université Laval, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Québec City, G1V 0A6, QC, Canada; Hassan M.Z., Université Laval, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Québec City, G1V 0A6, QC, Canada; Rahman M.A., University of Wolverhampton, School of Mathematics and Computer Science, Wolverhampton, WV1 1LY, United Kingdom
Abstract: Effective vehicular network management is essential for enabling reliable communications between vehicles and infrastructure in dynamic environments. The integration of terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks (NTNs), together with the growing adoption of the Internet of Things (IoT) and diverse vehicular applications, introduces multifaceted challenges in context awareness, security, spectral resource management, and network resilience. Digital twin (DT) technology offers a promising paradigm for addressing these challenges by providing high-fidelity virtual representations of physical network entities that enable predictive simulation, what-if analysis, and proactive closed-loop control. This paper presents a comprehensive survey of DT-enabled vehicular network management. First, the bidirectional relationship between artificial intelligence (AI) and DT is explored, in which AI serves as a key enabler of DT-assisted operations by supporting intelligent sensing, state prediction, anomaly detection, and adaptive decision-making, while DT environments facilitate safe and efficient AI training and validation. Subsequently, a novel DT-driven functional taxonomy is proposed, organizing the literature by DT functionality layers (sensing, prediction, control, feedback, resilience and security), with NTNs and terrestrial networks serving as cross-layer enablers. Based on the identified research gaps, an NTN-integrated, context-aware, and multi-function DT framework is presented to support proactive, resilient, and intelligent vehicular network management for 6G and beyond. The framework addresses critical operational requirements, including DT state modeling and prediction, DT synchronization in dynamic environments, and integrated multilevel data management and computing. Two illustrative case studies are discussed, focusing on DT-assisted radio resource management under channel-modeling uncertainty and DT synchronization under constrained communication resources. Finally, open research challenges and future directions are outlined toward scalable, interoperable, and trustworthy DTs for vehicular networks. © 2020 IEEE.

Abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled digital twins are increasingly used to improve monitoring, prediction, control, and sustainability assessment in circular biorefineries. However, the literature remains fragmented, with many studies focusing on isolated prediction tasks rather than validated, decision-oriented digital-twin systems. This review critically examines AI-enabled digital twins for circular biorefineries that convert heterogeneous bioresources into biogas, hydrogen, volatile fatty acids (VFAs), microbial products, algal products, bio-oil, syngas, and biochar. The review differs from earlier studies by linking digital-twin architecture with soft sensing, hybrid modeling, constrained control, embedded techno-economic analysis (TEA), life-cycle assessment (LCA), and deployment-readiness requirements. Particular attention is given to VFA-platform biorefineries, where product speciation, pH control, separation energy, product routing, and uncertainty strongly influence process value. Across the reviewed literature, the most useful digital-twin functions are early detection of instability, estimation of hard-to-measure variables, feedstock-adaptive optimization, energy-intensity reduction, and transparent cost-emission trade-off analysis. The main barriers are limited online observability, weak external validation, poor transferability across sites, incomplete reporting of uncertainty, and insufficient integration between AI models and TEA-LCA decision layers. Future work should move from stand-alone predictive models toward validated hybrid twins with transfer learning, auditable data pipelines, constrained model predictive control (MPC), and carefully governed large-language-model interfaces to support operators and interpret scenarios. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Authors: Scholes M.S.
Author full names: Scholes, Myron S. (24548407600)
Title: Artificial intelligence and uncertainty
Affiliations: Stanford University, United States
Authors with affiliations: Scholes M.S., Stanford University, United States
Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has both capabilities and limitations in managing uncertainty, particularly in handling average cases versus extreme outliers. AI excels at analyzing large datasets and predicting typical outcomes, but struggles with rare, critical scenarios that require flexibility beyond its data-driven approach. Integrating human expertise with AI, especially in managing anomalies, enhances AI's potential to address complex situations. The discussion also highlights the tension between rapid innovation and rigid governance, emphasizing the importance of trust and adaptable frameworks for progress in technology and finance. Governance must evolve to allow faster, individualized solutions while maintaining oversight to prevent risks. The concept of "digital twins" improves adaptability and cost efficiency by modeling and simulating physical entities. Transitioning from hardware- to software-driven solutions underscores the need for production agility, enabling industries to adapt without major structural changes. The analysis addresses AI's role in large-scale societal issues like decarbonization, stressing the importance of managing not just mean outcomes but also catastrophic tail risks. AI must identify gaps in its understanding, enhancing efficiency through collaborative training. Technological advancements, including sensors and digital twins, enhance AI's real-time analysis capabilities, expanding applications in robotics, precision agriculture, and decentralized healthcare. The interplay between AI, governance, and innovation shows potential for solving major challenges in finance, healthcare, and sustainability, contingent on integrating adaptive human-AI collaboration. Title: Uncertainty-aware digital twins for safe operation and active fault-tolerance in degrading heterogeneous pumping systems
Affiliations: Hefei Institutes of Physical Science, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Hefei, 230031, China; University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, 230026, China; High Magnetic Field Laboratory of Anhui Province, Hefei, 230031, China

Abstract: Conventional deterministic controls often fail in fluid systems under mechanical degradation due to epistemic uncertainties, leading to constraint violations. While passive fault diagnosis has advanced, autonomous risk-averse decision-making post-degradation remains lacking. To bridge this gap, this study proposes an Adaptive Probabilistic Digital Twin (APDT) framework. Utilizing Uncertainty Quantification (UQ), the APDT establishes mathematical guardrails based on the Probability of Feasibility, actively preventing physical boundary violations under deep uncertainties. Furthermore, the framework dynamically reconstructs system mappings online to adapt to non-stationary asymmetrical degradation, overcoming the limitations of static models. An embedded Trust-Region mechanism ensures smooth state transitions by preventing actuator fatigue. Crucially, trajectory analysis reveals an emergent “strategic offloading” behavior: the APDT autonomously shifts operational loads from degraded to healthy units. This acts as an active fault-tolerant mechanism, mitigating stress on deteriorating components to prevent sudden failures while maintaining robust output. Ultimately, the APDT offers a reliable, physics-compliant paradigm for the active safety management and life-extension of cyber-physical systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Abstract: Disassembly is key to circular production, enabling end-of-life products to be recovered through reuse, remanufacturing, or recycling. However, disassembly is characterized by high uncertainty about product condition and process feasibility, which requires dynamic, product-specific planning. While predictive disassembly planning anticipates uncertainties, disassembly systems must additionally be able to adapt their plans in real time when deviations occur. This is addressed by Reactive Disassembly Planning (RDP), which enables the dynamic adaptation of disassembly processes and schedules during disassembly. However, unlocking RDP's full potential requires complex decision-making based on comprehensive real-time data. To support such data-driven RDP, a modular Digital Twin architecture is presented that integrates all decision-making steps into an automated, real-time planning pipeline. The architecture is instantiated and deployed as a Digital Twin in a learning-factory disassembly system to demonstrate the feasibility and end-to-end operation of the proposed modules and connectors. Its potential is illustrated in a representative scenario, in which the instantiated Digital Twin achieves a 78% reduction in lead time and a 2% increase in profit compared to operating without RDP, and a 529% profit increase compared to a rule-based process-termination strategy. These results serve as illustrative proof of applicability, indicating that data-driven RDP via Digital Twins can support efficient, resilient disassembly operations and thereby strengthen the business case for circular factories and the transition to more sustainable production. © 2026 The Authors

Abstract: The real-time supervisory control of advanced reactors requires accurate forecasting of plant-wide thermal-hydraulic states, including locations where physical sensors are unavailable. This need calls for surrogate models that combine predictive fidelity, millisecond-scale inference, and robustness to partial observability. We present a physics-guided message-passing graph neural network coupled with a neural ordinary differential equation (GNN-ODE) that addresses all three requirements. The system is represented as a directed sensor graph whose edges encode hydraulic connectivity through flow- and heat-transfer-aware message passing, and the latent dynamics are advanced in continuous time by a controlled neural ODE. A topology-guided initializer reconstructs uninstrumented states at rollout start. Prediction then proceeds fully autoregressively. On held-out simulation transients, the surrogate achieves an average MAE of 0.92 K at 60 s and 1.97 K at 300 s for uninstrumented nodes. Inference runs at approximately 105 times faster than simulated time on a single GPU, which makes 64-member ensemble rollouts practical for uncertainty quantification. To assess sim-to-real transfer, we adapt the pretrained surrogate to measurements collected on the physical thermal-fluid testbed using layerwise discriminative fine-tuning with 30 training sequences. The learned flow-dependent heat-transfer scaling recovers a Reynolds-number exponent consistent with established correlations, indicating constitutive learning beyond trajectory fitting. The model tracks a steep power-change transient at instrumented locations and produces physically plausible trajectories at uninstrumented ones. © 1963-2012 IEEE.

Authors: Alp S.
Title: Digital Transformation of the Energy Ecosystem: Opportunities, Challenges, and Pathways to Sustainability
Affiliations: Istanbul Okan University, Istanbul, Turkey
Authors with affiliations: Alp S., Istanbul Okan University, Istanbul, Turkey
Abstract: This chapter examines how the energy sector is progressing through digitalization, highlighting its opportunities, challenges, and impact on sustainability. Technologies like AI, big data, blockchain, smart grids, and digital twins are changing the way energy is produced, distributed, and consumed. They provide real-time data and tools that enable more innovative resource management, enhance operational efficiency, increase prosumer participation, and support low-carbon transitions. However, digitalization also introduces challenges, such as cybersecurity threats, regulatory uncertainties, infrastructure problems, and environmental issues related to data centers and blockchain systems. It emphasizes the importance of fair and equal digital access, digital literacy, and governance to ensure a just energy transition. The chapter advocates for digital policies aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and strategies at various levels that address ethical, environmental, and socio-economic concerns. While digitalization offers many benefits, it also presents risks that can be mitigated through more thoughtful and inclusive policies. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

Title: Toward autonomous infrastructure management: Agentic AI for structural health monitoring, robotics, and digital twins
Affiliations: Department of Civil Engineering, University of Texas at Arlington, Arlington, 76010, TX, United States
Authors with affiliations: Khan M.A., Department of Civil Engineering, University of Texas at Arlington, Arlington, 76010, TX, United States; Hong P., Department of Civil Engineering, University of Texas at Arlington, Arlington, 76010, TX, United States; Lin Z., Department of Civil Engineering, University of Texas at Arlington, Arlington, 76010, TX, United States
Abstract: Modern sensing, robotics, artificial intelligence (AI), and digital twins (DTs) are reshaping the design, construction, operation, and maintenance of civil infrastructure. This review examines the evolution of structural health monitoring (SHM) from predictive models toward agentic AI for autonomous infrastructure management. Current research has achieved substantial progress in vibration-based monitoring, vision-based inspection, robotic sensing, and transformer-enabled analytics; however, most workflows remain diagnostic and lack autonomous reasoning and decision-making capabilities. This review defines the emerging concept of Agentic SHM, synthesizes recent advances in reinforcement learning, large language models, robotics, and DTs, and proposes layered architecture integrating perception, reasoning, planning, execution, and governance. Key challenges, including trustworthy autonomy, uncertainty-aware decision-making, reproducibility, standards compliance, and multi-agent coordination, are identified. The review concludes that progressively validated, human-supervised agentic AI provides a practical pathway toward safer, more resilient, and lifecycle-oriented infrastructure automation, while providing a roadmap for future research and practical implementation across infrastructure. © 2026 Elsevier B.V. Title: AgriTwin-SA: A Multimodal, Physics-Informed GeoAI Architecture Toward an Agricultural Digital Twin for Southern Africa
Affiliations: South African National Space Agency (SANSA), Earth Observation Research, Applications and Development (EO-RAD), Pretoria, South Africa
Authors with affiliations: Masemola C., South African National Space Agency (SANSA), Earth Observation Research, Applications and Development (EO-RAD), Pretoria, South Africa; Ngcoliso N., South African National Space Agency (SANSA), Earth Observation Research, Applications and Development (EO-RAD), Pretoria, South Africa
Abstract: Southern African agriculture is dominated by rain-fed maize and is acutely exposed to recurrent drought, flooding, and heat extremes, yet no operational multi-country system couples continuous Earth observation (EO) with predictive simulation at district scale. We propose AgriTwin-SA, an agricultural digital-twin architecture that fuses Sentinel-1 synthetic aperture radar (SAR), harmonized optical reflectance, satellite rainfall, climate reanalysis, terrain, soil, and open cropland reference products into a continuously updated virtual representation of the regional cropping system. The architecture couples a two-branch temporal encoder (a temporal convolutional network and a Transformer self-attention encoder) with a physics-informed latent crop-state layer, a spatial graph-neural-network module, and a weekly data-assimilation loop, exposing three coupled outputs: in-season crop-stress monitoring, pre-harvest district yield forecasting with calibrated uncertainty, and a counterfactual scenario-simulation engine. In a simulation-based proof-of-concept calibrated to regional agronomic statistics, AgriTwin-SA attains the highest monitoring accuracy and the lowest yield error among compared baselines while producing better-calibrated probabilities; ablation attributes forecast lead-time skill to the climate branch, cloud-window robustness to SAR, and probability reliability to the calibration layer. We outline operational pathways, limitations, and data-sovereignty considerations, and identify multi-season operational validation as the essential next step. This paper presents the methodological framework and a simulation-based proof-of-concept; the full multi-season, multi-country empirical validation is reported in a forthcoming full paper. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Critical aspects of hybrid microgrids: Architectures, energy management, optimization techniques, and future research directions-A review

Abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy resources has accelerated the development of hybrid microgrids as a key solution for enhancing the sustainability, reliability, and operational flexibility of modern power systems. However, the intermittent nature of renewable generation, the growing integration of distributed energy resources (DERs), and the increasing complexity of energy management require advanced control, optimization, and storage technologies. This paper presents a comprehensive critical review of hybrid microgrids, covering their architectural configurations, hierarchical control strategies, energy management systems (EMSs), optimization techniques, and hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs). A systematic methodology supported by PRISMA-based literature screening, bibliometric analysis, and a taxonomy framework is employed to ensure a transparent and structured evaluation of the literature. Comparative analyses are conducted to assess conventional and artificial intelligence (AI)-based control strategies, mathematical and metaheuristic optimization methods, and emerging HESS configurations in terms of efficiency, scalability, computational complexity, and practical implementation challenges. Furthermore, critical issues including communication latency, interoperability, cybersecurity, battery degradation, explainable AI, and uncertainty-aware energy management are comprehensively discussed. Based on the identified research gaps, future directions are proposed, emphasizing digital twins, federated learning, distributed intelligence, resilient cyber-physical architectures, and next-generation AI-driven energy management. This paper provides a comprehensive reference study for researchers and practitioners involved in the design, control, optimization, and deployment of intelligent hybrid microgrid systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Authors: Chen Z.; Lei L.; Wang Y.
Title: Digital Twin-driven Visual Analytics and Spatio-Temporal Collaborative Intelligent Monitoring for Guangxi Karst Terrain
Source title: Proceedings of the 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Interaction Design, AIVRID 2026
Affiliations: Xiangsi Lake College, Guangxi University for Nationalities, Guangxi, Nanning, China
Authors with affiliations: Chen Z., Xiangsi Lake College, Guangxi University for Nationalities, Guangxi, Nanning, China; Lei L., Xiangsi Lake College, Guangxi University for Nationalities, Guangxi, Nanning, China; Wang Y., Xiangsi Lake College, Guangxi University for Nationalities, Guangxi, Nanning, China
Abstract: Karst landforms are widely distributed in Guangxi. Their unique geological structures, characterized by developed karst caves, interlaced underground rivers, and thin overburden layers, lead to frequent geological disasters such as landslides and karst collapses, posing a severe threat to the safety of people's lives and property. Traditional monitoring methods primarily rely on single-sensor data or manual inspections, which struggle to meet the requirements for real-time, accurate, and reliable disaster warning in complex terrains. This paper proposes a Static Perception-Dynamic Inspection Spatio-Temporal Collaborative Intelligent Monitoring System (KSTFN) tailored for the karst terrain in Guangxi. The system achieves early identification and precise warning of geological disasters by deeply integrating static geological models (InSAR, LiDAR) with dynamic inspection data (UAV multi-sensors). The core innovations include: (1) The Karst Spatio-Temporal Fusion Network (K-STFN), which utilizes a multi-scale dilated attention mechanism to capture multi-scale geological features ranging from micron-level fractures to hundred-meter-level karst caves. (2) A static-dynamic collaborative reasoning framework that achieves deep coupling of static knowledge and dynamic observations through geological prior-guided feature extraction and a bidirectional cross-modal attention mechanism. (3) An edge-cloud collaborative architecture, where a lightweight edge model supports real-time processing on UAVs (25 FPS), while a cloud-based deep model performs complex analysis and long-term trend forecasting. Experimental results demonstrate that the KSTFN system achieved a Mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 0.75 in landslide detection within typical karst areas of Guangxi, which is 19.5% higher than the current state-of-the-art method (FTransUNet). Additionally, disaster warning accuracy increased by 22.3%, and emergency response time was shortened by 35.6%. This study not only provides technical support for geological disaster monitoring in Guangxi's karst regions but also offers a scalable solution for disaster prevention and control in similar complex terrains. © 2026 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

Title: Predict First, Sync When Needed: A Risk-Aware Approach to Adaptive Digital Twin Synchronization Under Bandwidth Constraints
Source title: Proceedings of IEEE/IFIP Network Operations and Management Symposium, NOMS 2026
Affiliations: University Of Helsinki, Department Of Computer Science, Finland; Eurecom, Department Of Communication Systems, France
Authors with affiliations: Wanigarathna Y.R., University Of Helsinki, Department Of Computer Science, Finland; Tarkoma S., University Of Helsinki, Department Of Computer Science, Finland; Morabito R., University Of Helsinki, Department Of Computer Science, Finland, Eurecom, Department Of Communication Systems, France
Abstract: Maintaining real-time synchronization between physical assets and their Digital Twins over bandwidth-limited wireless links is a complex challenge. Existing approaches either transmit all sensed data, resulting in unnecessary network overhead, or rely solely on forecasting, which cannot guarantee fidelity when operating conditions change. In response, we present a risk-aware, event-driven synchronization framework that leverages predictive modeling to minimize network traffic while maintaining the fidelity of digital twins. Our approach utilizes a Gated Recurrent Unit-based quantile forecaster to predict key states with calibrated uncertainty. Additionally, it employs online quantile coverage and Kullback-Leibler divergence tests to monitor reliability and detect changes in distribution. The system operates in a predictive mode, fetching only selected states, and shifts to full synchronization and model retraining when deviations are detected. We conducted experiments using public LTE and 5G datasets, achieving R2>0.80 in most cases, with a peak of 0.99. Real-world evaluations using a commercial smartphone showed network-traffic reductions of 5. 4-7. 0 % versus continuous synchronization, along with mean absolute error (MAE) reductions of about 64% on average relative to simpler predictive methods. These findings demonstrate that predictive synchronization, coupled with awareness of drift, enables highfidelity digital twinning even under strict bandwidth constraints. © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Latency-robust corridor supervisory control for hybrid nuclear–HVDC–renewable power systems under communication-constrained low-inertia operation
Affiliations: Electrical, Instrumentation and Automation Department, Doris Engineering UK Co. (ODE), London, United Kingdom; AAU Energy, Aalborg University, Esbjerg, Denmark
Authors with affiliations: Astan S., Electrical, Instrumentation and Automation Department, Doris Engineering UK Co. (ODE), London, United Kingdom; Hajizadeh A., AAU Energy, Aalborg University, Esbjerg, Denmark
Abstract: Hybrid nuclear–HVDC–renewable transmission corridors introduce new supervisory coordination challenges due to reduced inertia, heterogeneous asset dynamics, and non-negligible bounded communication delay. Conventional coordination approaches typically assume ideal communication or treat latency as a secondary implementation issue, limiting robustness under wide-area supervisory operation. This paper proposes Latency-Robust Corridor Supervisory Control (LR-CSC), a reproducible engineering framework for delay-robust supervisory coordination under bounded communication delay. The methodology integrates a compact corridor-level state-space representation, a delay-embedded min–max supervisory formulation, and a digital-twin-based feasibility screening engine. Rather than relying on continuous online optimisation or centralised control authority, LR-CSC evaluates candidate supervisory actions over an admissible state envelope and enforces constraint satisfaction for all delays within a specified design bound. Validation is conducted using a fully specified synthetic nuclear–HVDC–renewable corridor benchmark under disturbance variation, stochastic bounded communication delay, and inertia degradation. Results demonstrate three principal outcomes. First, embedding bounded communication delay directly within supervisory feasibility expands the stable inertia–delay operating region relative to delay-blind coordination strategies. Second, delay-embedded feasibility screening suppresses oscillatory interaction between fast converter dynamics and slower synchronous response, yielding improved frequency nadir, reduced peak RoCoF, and faster settling behaviour. Third, robustness improvements persist across Monte-Carlo disturbance and communication uncertainty scenarios, indicating that performance gains arise from structural delay-embedded supervisory coordination rather than scenario-specific tuning. The proposed framework is intentionally positioned as a supervisory feasibility layer for low-inertia corridor coordination and provides a transparent balance between bounded computation, reproducibility, and practical implementability under communication-constrained operation. © 2026 Elsevier B.V.

Author full names: Moradi Sarkhanlou, Milad (59183487700); Toufigh, Vahab (55233818000); Ghaemian, Mohsen (8209299400)
Title: Integrated monitoring models for dam health and safety: A review of methods and considerations
Affiliations: Department of Civil Engineering, Sharif University of Technology, Tehran, Iran
Authors with affiliations: Moradi Sarkhanlou M., Department of Civil Engineering, Sharif University of Technology, Tehran, Iran; Toufigh V., Department of Civil Engineering, Sharif University of Technology, Tehran, Iran; Ghaemian M., Department of Civil Engineering, Sharif University of Technology, Tehran, Iran
Abstract: Dam safety and health monitoring are critical to ensuring the long-term reliability of water infrastructure, given the complex behavior of dams and the potentially severe consequences of failure. To evaluate current monitoring approaches, this study employs a structured literature review methodology that includes systematic database searching, screening, and qualitative synthesis of 215 relevant publications. The reviewed studies were organized into four major categories comprising artificial intelligence (AI)-based models, numerical models, hybrid models, and modern monitoring technologies. The review critically assesses the strengths, limitations, and application domains of these approaches, highlighting the increasing integration of AI techniques with numerical simulations to improve predictive accuracy while maintaining physical interpretability. Particular attention is given to methodological factors influencing model performance, including input variable selection, data quality, model validation strategies, and uncertainty management. The study also examines the role of explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) in improving transparency, interpretability, and engineering trust in safety-critical decision-making processes. Furthermore, emerging technologies such as digital twins, remote sensing systems, and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-assisted inspections are evaluated as key enablers of real-time monitoring and early warning systems. The review identifies major research challenges, including data scarcity, model generalization, computational demands, and interoperability across monitoring platforms. Future research directions are discussed, emphasizing the potential of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), foundation models, federated learning, and cyber-secure monitoring frameworks to support the next generation of intelligent dam monitoring systems. The findings provide practical insights for researchers and practitioners and help guide the development of more reliable and resilient dam monitoring frameworks. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.

Title: Hybrid grey-box digital twin and the Bees Algorithm optimization for batch chocolate conching: industrial-scale calibration and validation under hold-window robustness

Abstract: This paper develops a digital-twin workflow for batch chocolate conching by integrating a hybrid grey-box dynamic model with the Bees Algorithm (BA) to synthesize constraint-satisfying operating policies and additive schedules. The modelling contribution is a compact, equation-driven representation that couples (i) event-driven phase progression (dry–plastic–liquid), (ii) temperature–mixing–aeration accelerated moisture and volatile stripping, and (iii) structure-governed Herschel–Bulkley rheology via an interpretable closure linking a latent coating/dispersion index to yield stress and consistency evolution. The optimization contribution is a band-constrained formulation that enforces industrial rheology bands together with strict limits on residual moisture/volatiles and caps on maximum temperature and specific energy, while enabling early-stop termination once feasibility is sustained over a discharge-relevant hold window. Industrial-scale experiments were conducted on an instrumented 2.5-t conche at MEMAK using three batches, with two batches used for parameter calibration and one batch retained for independent cross-validation. Measured temperature and power/energy trajectories, together with discrete rheology, moisture, and volatile-marker measurements, were used to estimate uncertain model parameters and to provide a preliminary assessment of predictive performance under the investigated formulation and operating conditions. Simulation–experiment agreement was quantified using trajectory-level error metrics and discharge-relevant hold-window comparisons. The optimized policy achieved ηref = 3.229 Pa·s within the prescribed 3–5 Pa·s range and τy = 7.165 Pa within the 7–9 Pa range, while satisfying moisture, volatile, temperature, and specific-energy constraints and enabling early termination at 451.7 min. Given the limited three-batch dataset, these results should be interpreted as preliminary industrial-scale calibration and cross-validation rather than definitive evidence of plant-wide robustness. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer-Verlag GmbH Germany, part of Springer Nature 2026.

Abstract: This paper recasts the grid metaverse as an operating protocol, not as a collection of visualization technologies. The proposed protocol begins with an event claim, binds the claim to asset-level evidence, selects a task model, exposes uncertainty to the operator, and records the approved response together with post-action verification. A compact state package is used to join electrical measurements, spatial relations, weather exposure, inspection evidence, maintenance status, and data confidence. Four task modules - inspection triage, renewable ramp assessment, hazard localization, and carbon-record checking - share the same execution logic but use different evidence gates and performance measures. Rather than repeating a broad technology survey, the paper contrasts database-indexed research streams by the operational link each stream leaves unresolved. The resulting framework is evaluated as a protocol through baseline comparison, event replay, and staged field testing. Its principal value is a testable separation between evidence, inference, human authority, and physical feedback.  © 2026 IEEE.

Title: Physics-driven and data-driven hybrid digital twin framework for methanol fuel supply system based on dynamic Bayesian network

Abstract: Methanol has attracted increasing attention as a potential low-carbon marine fuel. However, the safe operation of methanol fuel supply systems is challenged by coupled hydraulic, thermal, and control dynamics, together with time-varying degradation and operational uncertainty. To address these challenges, this study proposes a physics-driven and data-driven hybrid digital twin framework based on a dynamic Bayesian network (PDH-DBN) for methanol fuel supply systems. The framework combines a conservation law-based physics-driven model, a temporal convolutional network (TCN)-based data-driven model, online Bayesian updating through particle filter, and adaptive model fusion. The physics-driven branch updates pump-related parameters online, while the data-driven branch updates correction parameters for the TCN outputs. The two branches are then fused adaptively using their current posterior residuals. The updated parameters are further used to construct pump health indices. The proposed approach was validated on a laboratory test bench under varying flow conditions and a preset pump fault. Under normal operation, the fused framework achieved RMSEs of 0.104–0.110 Hz for pump frequency, 0.022–0.031 bar for pressure, and 0.015–0.017 °C for temperature. Under the preset pump fault scenario, PDH-DBN effectively isolated primary-pump degradation. These results indicate that PDH-DBN can support accurate state estimation, adaptive fusion, uncertainty-aware health assessment, and pump-level fault isolation for methanol fuel supply systems. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd

Title: Development and performance analysis of a supercritical carbon dioxide power cycle for scramjet cooling and power generation considering digital twin of heater
Affiliations: Science and Technology on Reactor System Design Technology Laboratory, Nuclear Power Institute of China, Chengdu, 610213, China; College of Mechanical and Vehicle Engineering, Hunan University, Changsha, 410082, China
Authors with affiliations: Cao L., Science and Technology on Reactor System Design Technology Laboratory, Nuclear Power Institute of China, Chengdu, 610213, China; Zhou J., College of Mechanical and Vehicle Engineering, Hunan University, Changsha, 410082, China; Zhang F., College of Mechanical and Vehicle Engineering, Hunan University, Changsha, 410082, China; Liao G., College of Mechanical and Vehicle Engineering, Hunan University, Changsha, 410082, China
Abstract: Thermodynamic analyses of supercritical carbon dioxide (sCO2) power cycles commonly rely on zero-dimensional (0D) or quasi-one-dimensional models that cannot resolve the three-dimensional thermohydraulic behaviour of scramjet cooling channels, whereas full computational fluid dynamics (CFD) is too expensive for iterative cycle analysis. Here, we develop a CFD-based digital-twin reduced-order model (ROM) of the heater and integrate it into a two-way coupled 0D-3D model of a recuperated onboard sCO2 cycle for scramjet cooling and power generation. CFD predictions agreed with two published experimental datasets within the reported uncertainty bands. The ROM was trained using 24 operating conditions generated by Latin hypercube sampling and tested against nine independent CFD cases. Maximum errors were 0.095%, 0.059%, 0.059%, 0.004%, and 1.157% for average outlet temperature, maximum inner- and outer-wall temperatures, average inlet pressure, and pressure drop, respectively. At identical mass flow rates, the conventional and coupled models predicted similar overall cycle performance, but the conventional model overestimated heater cooling and underestimated maximum wall temperature. The coupled model predicted that the inner- and outer-wall temperatures exceeded 1100 K at sCO2 mass flow rates below 1.75 and 1.80 kg s−1, respectively. Under the same wall-temperature constraint, the conventional model overestimated turbine and net power, thermal efficiency, recuperator mass, and total heat-exchanger mass, while underestimating compressor power, cooling-fuel consumption, cooler mass, and required sCO2 mass flow. The coupled model therefore provides a more reliable basis for performance and thermal-safety assessment. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd.
